title: Registration of Establishment
detail: An employer seeking registration for an establishment shall apply electronically in FORM-I containing the particulars of the establishment, accompanied by documents relating to registration, proof of identity and address on the Shram Suvidha Portal. Certificate of registration in FORM-III issued within 7 days; auto-generated if delayed. Certificate is non-transferable and shall be displayed at conspicuous places (Rule 3(4)). Registration number shall be quoted on all documents and correspondence (Rule 3(7)).
frequency: Before commencement; within 30 days of any change in particulars (Rule 3(8))
monitoringAuthority: Registering Officer via Shram Suvidha Portal
remarks: Late fee applicable after 60 days of notification. Existing establishments to update within 6 months of rules coming into force (Rule 3(6)).

title: Application for Cancellation of Registration Certificate
detail: The employer shall within thirty days of the closing of the establishment intimate to the Registering Officer and also to Inspector-cum-Facilitator having jurisdiction, intimating the actual date of closing in FORM-II along with certificate of payment of all dues and statutory returns to workers. Information auto-shared to EPFO and ESIC. Cancellation certificate in FORM-IV issued within 60 days; auto-generated if delayed (Rule 3(11)).
frequency: Within 30 days of closing of establishment
remarks: Show cause opportunity of 30 days before cancellation.

title: Notice of Commencement / Reopening / Cessation / Discontinuance / Abandonment of Mine Operations
detail:
OSH: The employer of every mine shall give not less than thirty days prior notice of the commencement, reopening, cessation, discontinuation or abandonment of operations or closing of mines in FORM-VII.

CMR Reg 3(1): The notice shall be accompanied by (a) a plan showing boundaries of the mine, shafts or openings, tri-junction or revenue pillars and other prominent surface features; (b) a copy of the surface plan under Reg 65(1)(a); and (c) a copy of Safety Management Plan under Reg 104. Surface plan within 60 days, SMP within 1 year of CMR coming into force for existing mines.

CMR Reg 5(1): When intended to abandon or close or discontinue >60 days — state reasons and number of persons likely to be affected.

CMR Reg 6(1): When intended to reopen after abandonment/closure/discontinuance >60 days — ≥30 days prior notice.
formNo: FORM VII (OSH); Form as specified by CI (CMR)
frequency: Not less than 30 days prior notice; forthwith if unforeseen (CMR Reg 5(1) proviso)
monitoringAuthority: Registering Officer + ICF (OSH); CI + RI + DM (CMR)
remarks: Greenfield blocks must file commencement notice before opening. CMR Reg 3(1) proviso: on change of boundary under Reg 121/122, plan showing new boundary within 7 days.

title: Communication of actual date of opening / reopening
detail: When a mine has been opened, the owner, agent or manager shall forthwith communicate the actual date of opening to the Chief Inspector, the Regional Inspector and to the District Magistrate. Same requirement on reopening under Reg 6(2).

title: Notice after actual abandonment / closure / discontinuance exceeding 60 days
detail: When a mine or seam has been abandoned, closed or the workings thereof has been discontinued over a period exceeding sixty days, the owner, agent or manager shall, within seven days of the abandonment, closure or expiry of the said period of discontinuance, give notice in the Form and method as may be specified by the Chief Inspector.
frequency: Within 7 days of abandonment/closure or expiry of 60-day discontinuance

title: Notice of change in name / ownership / address of owner
detail: When a change occurs in the name or ownership of a mine or in the address of the owner, the owner, agent or manager shall, within seven days from the date of the change, give notice. Proviso: where the owner is a firm or association — change of any partner, member, director (public co.) or shareholder (private co.) shall also be intimated within 7 days.

title: Intimation of transfer of ownership — plans and records handed over
detail: When the ownership of a mine is transferred, the previous owner or his agent shall make over to the new owner or his agent, within a period of seven days of the transfer of ownership, all plans, sections, reports, registers and other records maintained in pursuance of the Act and of the regulations, and all correspondence relating to the working of the mine; and when the requirements have been duly complied with, both the previous and the new owners or their respective agents shall forthwith inform the CI and RI in writing.
frequency: Within 7 days of transfer; forthwith after compliance

title: Notice of appointment / termination of Agent, Manager, Engineer, Surveyor, VO, SO, Asst Manager o...
detail: When any appointment is made of an agent, manager, engineer, surveyor, ventilation officer, safety officer, or assistant manager or when the employment of any such person is terminated or any such person leaves the said employment, or when any change occurs in the address of any agent or manager, notice shall be given within seven days.
frequency: Within 7 days of appointment / termination / change

title: Statement of persons authorised to act on behalf of owner + changes
detail:
Reg 7(4): The owner shall submit in writing a statement showing the name and designation of every person authorised to act on behalf of the owner in respect of management, control, supervision or direction of the mine.
Reg 7(5): The statement shall state the responsibilities of every such person and the matters in respect of which he is authorised.
Reg 7(6): Every such person shall be an agent for the mine or group of mines.
Reg 7(7): Any change, addition or alteration shall be reported in writing within 7 days.
frequency: On appointment; within 7 days of any change / addition / alteration

title: Notice of accident (loss of life / serious bodily injury) or dangerous occurrence
detail:
OSH Rule 7(1): Where an accident occurs resulting in death — inform ICF forthwith in FORM-XI and inform electronically and by telephone to CICF, ICF, DM/SDO and the police station and family members or kin of the victim.
OSH Rule 7(2): Where accident results in bodily injury preventing work ≥48 hours — inform in FORM-XI within 12 hours after completion of 48 hours.
OSH Rule 7(3): Dangerous occurrence whether causing injury or not — within 12 hours send intimation to ICF and DM/SDO.
Proviso: if death occurs after notice already sent — forthwith send further notice by telephone and electronically, confirmed in writing within 12 hours.

CMR Reg 8(1): Forthwith inform RI by telephone/fax/email/special messenger; within 24 hours give formal notice to DM, CI, RI and Competent Authority for compensation. List of dangerous occurrences in Reg 8(1)(b)(i)-(xix) includes: explosion, spontaneous heating, fire, fall of HEMM from height, bursting of pressurised equipment, influx of gases, irruption of water, premature collapse, accident due to explosives, breakage of rope/chain/headgear, failure of dump or side in OC working, failure of structure/installation, electrical flash-over causing burn.

CMR Reg 8(2): Exhibit copy on special notice board at mine office ≥14 days.
formNo: FORM XI (OSH); Form as specified by CI (CMR)
frequency: Forthwith (death — OSH/CMR); within 12 hrs (injury >48hr / DO — OSH); within 24 hrs (CMR formal)
monitoringAuthority: ICF + DM/SDO + Police + Family (OSH); DM + CI + RI + Comp Authority (CMR)
remarks: CMR Reg 8(1)(b)(xvii): failure of dump or side in OC working is a dangerous occurrence — critical for OC mines.

title: Notice of electrical accident
detail: When an accident causing loss of life, serious bodily injury or burn injury occurs in or about a mine in connection with the generation, storage, transformation, transmission, supply or use of electrical energy, the owner, agent or manager shall also forthwith inform the Inspector of Mines (Electrical) by telephone, fax, e-mail or by special messenger. Proviso: if sent by email, shall be immediately followed by fax or letter.
remarks: Additional to S.No. 10 — applies when accident is connected with electrical energy.

title: Notice if death results from reported injury or injury becomes serious
detail: If death results from any injury already reported as serious under Reg 8(1) or if an injury other than the serious injury becomes serious, the owner, agent or manager shall within twenty-four hours of his being informed of the same, give notice to DM, CI, RI and Competent Authority; and if such death or injury is connected with electrical energy, also to the IM(E).
monitoringAuthority: DM + CI + RI + Comp Authority; IM(E) if electrical

title: Particulars of persons killed or injured
detail: In respect of every person killed or injured, the owner, agent or manager shall send particulars in the Form and method as may be specified by the Chief Inspector, within seven days of the occurrence, and also within fifteen days of the injured person returning to duty.
frequency: Within 7 days of occurrence; within 15 days of injured person returning to duty
remarks: Event-driven submission, not periodic.

title: Notice of notifiable disease
detail:
OSH Rule 8(1): Where in any establishment, a worker contracts any disease specified in the Third Schedule of the Code, the employer shall send a notice in FORM-XI to the ICF within such time as applicable.

CMR Reg 9: Where any person employed in a mine contracts any disease notified by the Central Government under section 25 of the Act, notice shall be given within three days of being informed, to the CI, RI, Inspector of Mines (Medical), DM, and Competent Authority for compensation.
formNo: FORM XI (OSH); Form as specified by CI (CMR)
monitoringAuthority: ICF (OSH); CI + RI + IM(Medical) + DM + Comp Authority (CMR)

title: Notice of temporary authorisation of person to act as Manager
detail: If for any unavoidable reason the manager is unable to carry out his duties, and has authorised a qualified person to act in his place, the owner, agent or manager shall forthwith inform the Regional Inspector by registered post or speed post or fax, stating the reason, qualifications, experience and period of authorisation.
remarks: Maximum 30 days without CI consent in writing. CI may extend subject to conditions.

title: Notice of temporary authorisation of person to act as Engineer
detail: When the engineer is unable to carry out duties by reason of temporary absence, illness or other cause, the manager shall forthwith authorise in writing another person with similar qualifications to act in his place and inform the Regional Inspector.
remarks: Maximum 30 days without RI consent in writing.

title: Notice of appointment / termination of Training Officer
detail: Every appointment, discharge, dismissal, resignation or termination of service of a Training Officer and of the date thereof shall be sent by the owner or agent to the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator and the Inspector-cum-Facilitator within seven days from the date of such appointment, authorisation, discharge, dismissal, resignation or termination of service.
remarks: OSH-independent; not in CMR.

title: Training module for new technology / equipment — submit before introduction
detail: In case new technology, equipment and system of work is introduced in the mine, the employer shall prepare and submit the training module, at least sixty days before such introduction, to the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator, who may at any time, by an order in writing, require such modification in the training module as may be specified therein.
remarks: CICF may require modifications.

title: Training Scheme — submit to CICF
detail: The employer of every mine shall ensure that a training scheme, based on the guidelines on the scheme of training, wherever no authority, specified by the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator for persons employed or to be employed in the mine. The CICF or ICF may by an order in writing, require such modification in the training scheme as may be specified therein.
frequency: Before employment of persons; revised as needed
remarks: Scheme shall include: initial training, refresher training, new technology training, competency assessment, training records auditing.

title: Notice of closure / discontinuance of vocational training centre (>60 days)
detail: When it is intended to close a training centre or to discontinue the working thereof for a period exceeding sixty days, the employer or owner of common VTC shall give notice in the manner and form as may be specified by the CICF stating the reasons, not less than thirty days prior to such closure or discontinuance. Proviso: forthwith when on account of unforeseen circumstances.

title: Notice of medical examination — initial and periodical
detail:
Rule 111(1): For initial medical examination, employer shall give at least seven days prior notice in writing to the person to be examined, in Form to be specified by the CICF; copy sent to examining authority.
Rule 111(2): For periodical medical examination, the manager shall give at least twenty days prior notice in writing; copy sent to examining authority along with previous medical certificates.
Rule 111(4): If person fails to appear, a second notice of minimum ten days shall be given.
frequency: 7 days prior (initial); 20 days prior (periodical); 10 days (second notice)
monitoringAuthority: Person to be examined + Examining Authority (copy)
remarks: Examining authority to inform manager within 1 week if person appeared or not (Rule 111(5)).

title: Safety Management Plan — submit copy
detail: A copy of the Safety Management Plan shall be submitted to the Regional Inspector. The RI may at any time, by an order in writing, require such modification in the Safety Management Plan as may be specified therein.
remarks: SMP shall cover: hazard identification, risk assessment, safe operating procedures, emergency response.

title: Transport Rules — submit copy
detail: The manager shall frame transport rules regulating the running and use of any transport machinery in the mine and shall submit a copy to the Regional Inspector. The RI may, by an order in writing, require such modification as may be specified. In mines already in operation, submit within 90 days of CMR coming into force.
frequency: Before use of transport machinery; within 90 days of CMR for existing mines
remarks: Copies placed at conspicuous places + with operators/drivers/officials.

title: Code of Practice for each machinery / operation — submit copy
detail: The manager shall frame a code of practice for each machinery used or operation performed in the mine and submit a copy to the Regional Inspector. The RI may require modification. For existing mines, within 90 days of CMR.
frequency: Before introducing machinery/operation; within 90 days of CMR for existing
remarks: Shall be in English and local language with illustrative sketches.

title: Permission for change of mine boundary in opencast mine
detail: No boundary of an opencast mine shall be changed without the prior permission in writing of the Chief Inspector.
remarks: Plan showing new boundary to be submitted within 7 days (Reg 3(1) proviso).

title: Standing orders for use of two types of explosives in same OC shot-hole
detail: Where two types of explosives are used in the same shot hole in opencast working, standing orders framed by the manager shall be submitted to the Regional Inspector before such use.
remarks: OC-specific provision.

title: Blasting permission near permanent buildings
detail: Permission for blasting within the danger zone (up to 500m) of permanent buildings or structures — the aggregate maximum charge shall be based on scientific study and permission granted by the Chief Inspector.
frequency: Before blasting within 500m of permanent building/structure
remarks: Scientific study required to determine safe charge.

title: Emergency Response and Evacuation Plan — submit
detail: The owner, agent or manager shall prepare and submit an Emergency Response and Evacuation Plan to the Regional Inspector before commencement of operations. The plan shall be reviewed periodically and mock drills conducted.

title: Intimation to adjacent mine — workings within 60m of boundary
detail: As soon as the workings of a mine are extended within sixty meters of the boundary, the owner, agent or manager of the mine shall intimate the owner, agent or manager of the adjacent mine and shall give facilities for survey to the surveyor of the adjacent mine.
frequency: As soon as workings extend within 60m of boundary
monitoringAuthority: Owner / Agent / Manager of adjacent mine

title: Scientific study report for mechanised OC mine — submit and keep at office
detail: Before starting a mechanised opencast mine, a scientific study shall be carried out by the owner or agent regarding design of the mine, ultimate pit slope, dump slope, slope stability and slope monitoring. The study report shall be kept at the mine office and produced to the RI on demand. For existing mines, within 1 year of CMR coming into force. Reg 106(3): Recommendations of the study shall be complied with.
frequency: Before starting; within 1 year of CMR for existing
remarks: Non-compliance of recommendations = contravention.

title: IMMEDIATE REPORT of accident, fire, explosion, loss, shortage or theft of explosives
detail: Report by phone/email/fax within 24 hrs, written report follows, to Chief Controller, Controller, DM & nearest police. Shortage/theft also reportable; wreckage untouched pending Chief Controller's visit.
regulationRef: Rule 131(1)-(2); SET-VII Cond. 11 & 38; SET-V Cond. 19; SET-VIII conditions
frequency: WITHIN 24 HOURS by fastest means + written report; licence conditions require IMMEDIATE reporting of loss/shortage/theft
monitoringAuthority: Chief Controller + Controller + District Magistrate + Officer-in-charge nearest Police Station + Licensing Authority
mode: Telephone / Fax / E-mail / Electronic / Special Messenger, followed by written report
remarks: CRITICAL. Note SHORTAGE OF STOCK is reportable, not just theft — a stock reconciliation discrepancy triggers this obligation. Rule 131(2) SCENE PRESERVATION is absolute: wreckage and debris must not be disturbed pending the Chief Controller visit, except for rescue and body recovery. This runs parallel to (not instead of) the CMR Reg 8 and OSH Rule 7 accident notices to DGMS.

title: Notice of accident, breakdown, fire or explosion involving the ROAD VAN
detail: Any accident, fire or explosion involving road van: (a) comply with road accident law; (b) inform nearest police station; (c) licensee informs Chief Controller AND Controller in jurisdiction of accident with full details; arrange safe custody of explosives. Breakdown (no accident): inform licensee who informs Chief Controller and Controller. LE-7 Cond. 11 also requires immediate report to licensing authority; if loss of life/serious injury — also nearest police station.
monitoringAuthority: Chief Controller of Explosives + Controller (in whose jurisdiction accident/breakdown occurred) + Licensing Authority + nearest Police Station (if loss of life/serious injury)
remarks: NOTE: A mere BREAKDOWN with no fire or explosion is itself reportable. Rule 69 requires Chief Controller + Controller notification — this is broader than LE-7 Cond. 11 alone. Both apply. After breakdown, major repairs may not be commenced until explosives are removed and the van is moved at least 300 m from inhabited premises.

title: Statutory notice of accident / dangerous occurrence where employer reporting is required
detail: Statutory notice of accident / dangerous occurrence where employer reporting is required
remarks: Coordinate with Safety

title: Notice relating to mine employee medical examination
detail: Notice relating to mine employee medical examination
remarks: Medical process

title: Accident/dangerous occurrence statutory notice where employer-side reporting is applicable
detail: Accident/dangerous occurrence statutory notice where employer-side reporting is applicable
remarks: Safety should own technical investigation

title: Medical examination notice/scheduling for mine employees
detail: Medical examination notice/scheduling for mine employees

title: Annual Return — category of employees, health & welfare
detail:
OSH Rule 74: Every employer of an establishment shall send an annual return in FORM-XVII (Part II) relating to category of employees, health and welfare facilities, retrenchment or layoffs, bonus, maternity benefits etc. to the ICF having jurisdiction so as to reach on or before the last day of February following the end of each Calendar year electronically.
Rule 72(5): Upload return in FORM-XVII and XVIII on the designated portal on or before 28th/29th February.

CMR Reg 4(1): On or before 1st day of February in every year, the owner, agent or manager shall submit to the CI, RI and DM annual returns in respect of the preceding year.
formNo: FORM XVII Part II (OSH); Form as specified by CI (CMR)
frequency: On or before last day of February (OSH) / 1st February (CMR) every year
remarks: Unified return covering all establishments under OSH Code including mines. Both OSH and CMR returns to be filed.

title: Annual Self-Declaration — EPF / ESIC Compliance
detail: Every establishment to which Chapter III (EPF) and Chapter IV (ESIC) of the Code on Social Security 2020 applies shall submit a self-declaration in PART-IV of FORM-XVII electronically.
remarks: Uploaded together with the annual return filing.

title: Annual Return — Principal Employer (Contract Labour)
detail: Every principal employer of an establishment shall submit annual return in FORM-XVII (Part-III) electronically to the authority and concerned Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) so as to reach on or before last day of February following the end of each Calendar year, except in cases of contract which undertakes to produce given result.
frequency: On or before last day of February
remarks: Relevant as principal employer for contractor-deployed manpower in mines and SME plant.

title: Half-Yearly Return — Contractor
detail: Every contractor shall send half-yearly return in FORM-XVIII electronically to the Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) concerned not later than thirty days from the close of the half year, that is to say January to June, July to December.
remarks: Filed by contractor; principal employer should obtain proof of filing.

title: Certificate of Registration displayed at conspicuous places
detail: The certificate of registration shall be non-transferable and shall be displayed at conspicuous places within the premises of the establishment.

title: Display on notice board — establishment details, hours, wages, accident data, ICF details
detail:
OSH Rule 73: Every employer shall display at conspicuous places: name and address of establishment, hours of work, wage period, date of payment, details of accident and dangerous occurrence for the last five years, name and address of ICF having jurisdiction, date of payment of unpaid wages — in English or Hindi and local language.

CMR Reg 238: Notices displayed prohibiting smoking, unauthorised entry at prescribed places.
mode: Physical (posted in English + Hindi + local language)
remarks: OSH broader than CMR Reg 238; includes accident history display.

title: Notice of periods of work displayed + copy to ICF
detail: The notice referred to in sub-section (2) of section 31 of the Code shall be displayed at conspicuous places on a notice board or electronic board of the establishment and maintained in FORM-XII and a copy of such notice shall be sent to Inspector-cum-Facilitator electronically or by speed post.

title: Letter of Appointment to every employee
detail: No employee shall be employed in any establishment unless an appointment letter has been issued in the prescribed format containing: name, DOB, father/mother name, Aadhaar (with consent), LIN, UAN/Insurance No., designation, type of employment (Regular/Fixed-term/Contractual), category of skill, date of joining, wages/basic/DA, other allowances, social security applicability, nature of duties, maternity benefit (for women).
remarks: OSH-independent; mandatory for all employees including contract.

title: Employee Register
detail: Every employer shall maintain employee register in FORM XIII. Entries in English or Hindi and local language. Preserved 5 years from last entry. Produced on demand before ICF.

title: Attendance Register-cum-Muster Roll
detail:
OSH Rule 72(1)(ii): Attendance register-cum-muster roll in FORM XIV maintained electronically or otherwise.

CMR Reg 40(3): Names of all persons employed in the mine shall be recorded in a register maintained at the mine before and after each shift. Hard copy to be kept forthwith. CI may approve electronic system.

CMR Reg 61(5): The attendance clerk shall remain on duty throughout the working hours and shall report to the manager or assistant manager within two hours of commencement of shift about any official absent from duty.
remarks: Attendance clerk reporting absent official within 2 hrs is critical for statutory compliance.

title: Register of Wages, Overtime and Deductions
detail: Register for wages, overtime and deductions in FORM XV. Entries in English or Hindi and local language. Preserved 5 years from date of last entry.

title: Wage Slips issued to employees
detail: Every employer shall issue wage slips electronically to the employees in FORM XVI on or before the day of payment of wages to the employee.

title: Register of Leave with Wages
detail: The employer of every establishment shall maintain in respect of every employee a record of leave with wages electronically or otherwise in FORM-XX and shall share the leave records of the respective employee, once in a Calendar year, on demand. The register shall be preserved for a period of five years after the last entry and shall not be destroyed even after the expiry of that period unless it has been properly transferred to the new register.
frequency: Continuous; preserved 5 years (not destroyed even after unless transferred)

title: Register of Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences
detail:
OSH Rule 75: Registers of accident and dangerous occurrences shall be maintained in FORM-XIX. Preserved 5 years.

CMR Reg 8(2): Copy of accident/dangerous occurrence notice exhibited on special notice board at mine office for ≥14 days from date of exhibition.
frequency: Continuous; preserved 5 years; notice displayed ≥14 days (CMR)

title: Preservation of all registers and records — 5 years
detail:
Rule 72(4): All registers and records shall be maintained complete and up-to-date and unless otherwise provided for, shall be kept at an office or the nearest convenient building within the precincts of the workplace or at a place within a radius of three kilometres.
Rule 72(7)(ii): Preserved in original for a period of five years after the date of the last report or entry. If original lost or destroyed, true copies preserved for the specified period.
Rule 72(7)(iii): Produced electronically or by speed post, on demand before CICF or ICF.

title: Written authorisation for person to act as Manager during absence
detail: If the manager is unable to carry out his duties for any unavoidable reason, the owner, agent or manager may authorise in writing any person holding the requisite qualifications to act as manager. No such authorisation shall have effect for a period exceeding thirty days except with previous consent in writing of the Chief Inspector and subject to conditions.
frequency: On every occasion of manager absence

title: Written appointments — Safety Officer, Asst Manager, Engineer, Overman, Surveyor (with qualificat...
detail: Each appointment of Safety Officer (Reg 29), Assistant Manager (Reg 30), Ventilation Officer (Reg 31 — UG only), Engineer (Reg 32), Surveyor (Reg 33), Overman (Reg 34) shall be made in writing by the owner, agent or manager with qualifications as specified in respective regulations.

title: Bound paged book — list of all competent persons appointed
detail: The manager shall maintain in a bound paged book, a list of all competent persons appointed, showing their names, designations and the duties assigned to them.

title: Manager's verification of competence on taking charge
detail: On taking charge of a mine, the manager shall satisfy himself as to the competency of all persons who have been appointed as competent persons and shall either countersign their appointments or issue fresh appointments.

title: Charge Report on change of manager
detail: When a change of manager takes place, the outgoing and incoming managers shall jointly prepare and sign a charge report covering the state of the mine, plans, registers, records and any pending matters. A copy shall be sent to the Regional Inspector.

title: Medical fitness certificate for officials >60 years
detail: No person who has attained the age of sixty years shall act as a manager, engineer, ventilation officer, safety officer, assistant manager, overman, sirdar, or in any other official capacity unless he has been certified as fit by a qualified medical practitioner within the preceding one year. No person >70 years shall act as manager or in any official capacity.
frequency: Within preceding 1 year for >60 yrs; no person >70 yrs

title: Manager's Diary
detail: The manager shall maintain a diary in a bound paged book showing the results of his daily inspections and the action taken thereon.
remarks: Core statutory record. Manager must inspect mine once in 24 hours when work is in progress.

title: Manager's written report on materials/appliances needed for safety
detail: Reg 43(4): If the manager considers it necessary that any material or appliance should be provided for the safety of persons employed, or that any measures should be taken for that purpose, he shall make a written report to the owner or agent in a bound paged book. Reg 43(5): The owner or agent shall respond within three days of receipt of such report.
monitoringAuthority: Owner / Agent + bound book copy at mine
remarks: Owner/Agent must respond within 3 days.

title: Manager's countersigning of all reports, registers and records
detail: The manager shall countersign with date all reports, registers and other records required under these regulations. He may delegate this duty to an assistant manager except in cases where countersigning by the manager is specifically required.

title: Manager's enquiry into accident / dangerous occurrence
detail: The manager or assistant manager authorised by him shall enquire into every accident or dangerous occurrence and shall record the result of such enquiry together with a plan, sections and photographs in a bound paged book. A copy of the enquiry report shall be sent to the CI and RI within fifteen days of the occurrence.
frequency: On every accident / dangerous occurrence; copy to CI+RI within 15 days

title: Safety Officer's daily record of work
detail: The safety officer shall maintain a daily record of his work in a bound paged book or in retrievable and non-editable electronic form.
remarks: OC safety officer holds First Class Manager Certificate (Coal) or restricted certificate.

title: Assistant Manager's inspection record
detail: The assistant manager shall maintain a record of his inspections in a bound paged book.

title: Overman's OC duties record + shift report
detail:
Reg 47(6): In case of opencast workings, the overman shall ensure: (a) bench dressing and bench stability; (b) haul road maintenance; (c) dump stability; (d) no overcrowding of persons or machinery; (e) adequate lighting; (f) blasting precautions; (g) safe operation of machinery; (h) compliance with transport rules.
Reg 47(7)(d): At the end of every shift, the overman shall make a general report in a bound paged book on the performance of his duties, safety and discipline.
remarks: OC-specific duties under Reg 47(6)(a)-(h).

title: Sirdar's OC inspection report
detail:
Reg 129(7): In OC workings, the sirdar or competent person shall inspect at least once during each shift for: overhangs, undercuts, loose material or trees within 3m of edge of excavation, fencing, PPE, dump condition.
Reg 129(8): At the end of each shift, the sirdar shall record the results of inspection in a bound paged book.
remarks: Must include details per Reg 129(8)(a)-(d).

title: Surveyor's record book
detail: The surveyor shall maintain in a bound paged book a record of facts relating to boundary approach, plan accuracy concerns and other survey matters. Entries shall be signed by the surveyor and countersigned by the manager.

title: Danger withdrawal record + re-admission examination
detail: When any place in the mine is found to be dangerous, the competent person shall withdraw all persons and record the withdrawal. Re-admission shall be after examination and report.

title: HEMM operator (shovel/excavator/dragline) shift inspection record
detail: The operator of every HEMM (shovel, excavator, dragline) shall inspect the machine at the beginning and end of every shift and record the results in a bound paged book.

title: Truck/Tipper/Dumper operator shift inspection record
detail: The operator of every truck, tipper or dumper shall inspect the vehicle at the beginning and end of every shift and record the results in a bound paged book.

title: Mine Plans and Sections — maintained up-to-date
detail:
Reg 65(1): The following plans and sections shall be maintained: (a) Surface plan; (c) Vertical mine sections — proviso for OC: vertical projections at intervals not exceeding 100m both longitudinal and transverse, irrespective of inclination of coal seam; (e) Joint survey plan (where workings within 60m of boundary); (f) Geological plan; (g) Water-danger plan.
All plans inked on durable paper/tracing cloth/polyester film. Not to be removed from mine without RI approval. Corrected up-to-date — not older than 3 months.
frequency: Maintained corrected up-to-date (not older than 3 months)
remarks: OC proviso in Reg 65(1)(c) requires vertical sections at ≤100m intervals.

title: Field books, notes + list of all plans/sections/instruments
detail: The surveyor shall maintain field books, notes and a list of all plans, sections and instruments in a bound paged book. Entries signed by surveyor and countersigned by manager.

title: Surveyor's certificate of correctness on every plan/section
detail: Every plan and section shall bear a certificate of correctness signed by the surveyor and countersigned by the manager with date.

title: Safety Management Plan document
detail: The Safety Management Plan shall be maintained as an auditable document at the mine.

title: Transport Rules — copies maintained and displayed
detail: Copies of transport rules shall be kept at conspicuous places and with every operator, driver and official.

title: Codes of Practice for each machinery/operation — maintained and displayed
detail: Copies of the code of practice shall be kept at the mine office and at the location of the machinery. Shall be in English and local language with illustrative sketches.

title: Register of Contraventions
detail:
Reg 117(1): There shall be kept at the mine an interleaved, paged and bound register of contraventions.
Reg 117(2): An Inspector shall enter contravention noticed and initial and date the entry.
Reg 117(3)(a): The owner/agent/manager shall, within 15 days, return to the Inspector one copy with action taken.
Reg 117(3)(b): Copy displayed on notice board within 1 day for not less than 15 days.
Reg 117(5): Register kept for not less than 3 years after last entry.
frequency: On each inspection; copy returned within 15 days; displayed ≥15 days
monitoringAuthority: Mine Office (kept ≥3 years after last entry)

title: Manpower distribution plan — monthly survey
detail: During the first week of every month, a survey shall be taken of the number of persons present in each section and shift.

title: Explosives licence copy at mine office
detail: A copy of the licence for possession, use, sale, transport or manufacture of explosives shall be kept at the mine office.

title: Magazine register — explosives issued to each competent person + returned
detail:
Reg 185(3): No explosive shall be issued from the magazine or explosive store except on written requisition signed by the shot-firer. The written requisition shall be preserved.
Reg 185(4): A register in a bound paged book shall be maintained showing the quantity of explosives issued to each competent person and the quantity returned.
remarks: Written requisition signed by shot-firer to be preserved.

title: Shot-firing apparatus test record
detail: Every shot-firing apparatus shall be tested at intervals not exceeding three months and after every failure, and the results recorded in a bound paged book.

title: Inspection record after shot-firing
detail: After every shot-firing, the shot-firer shall inspect the place and shall not declare it safe until satisfied that no danger exists. The inspection shall be recorded in a bound paged book.

title: Misfire report register
detail:
Reg 204(10)(b): Every misfire, whether suspected or confirmed, shall be reported by the shot-firer to the competent person and the overman.
Reg 204(10)(c): The shot-firer shall record every misfire and the action taken in a bound paged book.

title: Shot-firer's end-of-shift record
detail: At the end of every shift, every shot-firer shall record in a bound paged book: the quantity of explosive taken from the magazine, the quantity used, the quantity returned to the magazine, the places where shots were fired, the number of shots fired and any misfires.

title: Weekly Thorough Inspection of All Machinery and Plant (incl. HEMM)
detail:
Reg 213(3): Every person in-charge of any machinery, apparatus or appliance shall, before commencing work, see that it is in proper working order and if he observes any defect therein, he shall immediately report the fact to the manager, engineer or other competent person.
Reg 213(5): A competent person or persons appointed for the purpose shall, once at least in every seven days, make a thorough inspection of all machinery and plant in use, and shall record the result thereof in a bound paged book kept for the purpose.
Reg 213(6): In respect of electrical machinery and plant, the competent person shall be an engineer or electrician holding qualifications as specified in CEA Regulations 2010.
frequency: Once at least in every 7 days (weekly thorough inspection); defect reporting is continuous/before commencing work
remarks: CORRECTED: This is a single weekly thorough inspection requirement for ALL machinery, distinct from the operator's own daily shift inspection under Reg 62(c)/63(c) (S.No. 28-29). Reg 213 does NOT prescribe separate daily/monthly/annual tiers — that was an earlier drafting error, now fixed. This weekly inspection is over and above the operator's daily pre-shift check.

title: Cranes / lifting gear — test certificates, SWL markings, examination records
detail: No crane or lifting gear shall be used unless it has been tested and certified before first use and periodically thereafter. Safe Working Load (SWL) shall be clearly marked. Examination records maintained in bound paged book.
frequency: Before first use; periodically as prescribed

title: HEMM design, operation and maintenance records per Code of Practice
detail: HEMM shall be designed, operated and maintained in accordance with the code of practice framed under Reg 110. Records of maintenance and operation shall be maintained.

title: Initial + Periodical medical examination of every mine employee
detail:
Rule 109(1)(i): Initial medical examination of every person seeking employment in a mine.
Rule 109(1)(ii): Periodical medical examination of person employed in a mine annually.
Rule 109(1)(iii): Medical examination conducted as per FORM-IX.
Rule 109(2): Periodical or X-ray examination at frequent intervals if examining authority deems necessary for suspected dust-related disease.
remarks: Examining authority: qualified medical practitioner in employer service or assigned by employer or Govt Medical Officer (Rule 110).

title: Medical examination records — retention and transfer
detail:
Rule 113(2): Copy of medical certificate in FORM-IX issued to person concerned and employer.
Rule 114(1): All medical examination records with medical history and job details to depict the occupational dust exposure profile shall be retained in the possession of the manager so long as the person is employed and for five years thereafter. Proviso: manager shall send all certificates to manager of any other mine where person is to be employed, if requested.
Rule 114(2): If examining authority is relieved, shall transfer all records to the manager.
frequency: Continuous; retained ≥5 years after employment ends

title: Training Scheme document
detail:
Rule 157(1): Employer of every mine shall ensure a training scheme based on CICF guidelines. Scheme shall include: (i) initial training; (ii) refresher training; (iii) new technology training; (iv) competency assessment; (v) training needs assessment; (vi) appointing competent trainers; (vii) keeping and auditing training records; (viii) relevant standards/modules; (ix) course material for different categories.
Rule 158: Every person to be employed shall be imparted training before employment.
Rule 159: Refresher training at least once in four years.
Rule 162: Training after long absence (>1 year), after serious accident, or change of job.
frequency: Before employment of persons; revised as needed

title: Training Officer records — training given + monthly reports + annual summary
detail:
Rule 166(iv): Maintain records of training given to every person and furnish monthly reports to the mine manager on progress of persons undergoing training.
Rule 166(v): Maintain records of supervision of practical training on actual operations.
Rule 166(2): At end of every year, forward to CICF/ICF having jurisdiction, through the employer, a summary of the report of work during the year.
frequency: Monthly reports; continuous records; annual summary to CICF/ICF

title: Certificate of training — issued on completion
detail:
Rule 173(1): Every person who completes training shall, on acceptable performance, be granted a certificate signed by the Training Officer.
Rule 173(3): Manager shall countersign with date after being satisfied of successful completion.
Rule 174(1): Person shall deliver certificate to manager who shall keep in safe custody and issue receipt.
Rule 174(3): On termination of employment, certificates returned to employee.

title: Safety Committee — constitution, composition, minutes
detail:
Rule 14(1): Every establishment with ≥500 workers shall constitute a Safety Committee.
Rule 15(5): Minutes of meetings recorded and maintained.
Rule 16: For mines — equal representation of management and workers. Management side: manager (chairman), safety officer (secretary), asst manager, engineer, medical officer, training officer. Workers side: elected representatives including sirdar, HEMM operator, shot-firer.
Rule 17: Functions include: discuss remedial measures, review accident/DO reports, study safety statistics, make recommendations, assist in safety campaigns, review SMP.

title: First Aid — equipment register, boxes, ambulance room
detail: First aid boxes at the rate of one for every 50 workers or part thereof. In OC mines, ambulance room where ≥150 workers. First aid equipment register maintained.

title: Mock Drills — conducted and records maintained
detail:
OSH Rule 59: Mock drills conducted as prescribed.
CMR Reg 252: Emergency Response and Evacuation Plan reviewed periodically and mock drills conducted. Records maintained.

title: Accident site preservation — plan and photographs prepared
detail:
Reg 251(1): Where an accident occurs causing death or serious bodily injury, the place of accident shall not be disturbed or altered until an Inspector has inspected or given permission.
Reg 251(2): Wait up to 3 days for Inspector; CI may extend.
Reg 251(3): Manager shall prepare a plan and take photographs of the accident site.

title: Fencing of top of opencast working
detail: The top of every opencast working shall be securely fenced to prevent persons from inadvertently going over the edge.

title: Emergency Response & Evacuation Plan document
detail: The Emergency Response and Evacuation Plan shall be maintained as a document, reviewed periodically, displayed, and mock drills conducted.

title: Fire Detection and Suppression System on HEMM (Opencast) + Monthly Fire Equipment Examination
detail:
Reg 139(1)(d): Every heavy earth moving machinery used in opencast workings shall be provided with automatically operated fire detection and suppression device or system. Proviso: for trucks and dumpers of less than 35 tonne capacity used in OC mines, a semi-automatic type fire suppression system may suffice.
Reg 139(6): A competent person shall, once at least in every month, examine all the equipment, material and arrangements provided for fire-fighting and shall discharge and re-fill fire-extinguishers as necessary; any deficiency found shall be immediately remedied.
Reg 139(7): A report of every such examination shall be made in a bound paged book, duly signed and dated by the person making the examination.
frequency: Fire suppression system: fitted before HEMM deployment; Examination: once at least every month
remarks: Direct HEMM-specific fire safety requirement — every OC HEMM unit must carry auto fire detection/suppression; smaller trucks/dumpers (<35T) may use semi-automatic type.

title: Precaution Against Dust — Sampling of Airborne Respirable Dust (Surface & Belowground)
detail:
Reg 143(1): The owner, agent or manager of every mine shall take steps necessary for minimising emission of dust and for suppression of dust entering the air at any workplace belowground OR ON SURFACE, ensuring worker exposure to respirable dust is limited to permissible levels.
Reg 143(3): Within 3 months of CMR coming into force and once at least in every month thereafter (or whenever RI requires), air at every workplace where airborne dust is generated shall be sampled and concentration of respirable dust determined.
Reg 143(8): All results of measurement of airborne respirable dust shall be systematically recorded within 14 days of sample collection, in a bound paged book, and every entry countersigned and dated by the manager within 24 hours.
frequency: Monthly sampling; results recorded within 14 days; manager countersign within 24 hours
remarks: Applies to OC surface operations directly — not UG-only as commonly assumed.

title: Dust Suppression Device — Weekly Inspection + Monthly Test
detail: Every device used for the prevention and suppression of dust produced by any machinery, equipment or process, as also for the filtering of exhausted air and every dust respirator, shall be inspected once at least in every seven days and shall be thoroughly examined and tested at least once in every month, and the results of every such inspection, examination and test shall be recorded in the register maintained under Reg 143(8).
mode: Physical (bound paged book — same register as Reg 143(8))
remarks: Directly relevant to OC: water spray systems on drills, crushers, haul roads.

title: Weekly Examination of Surface Fences
detail: Every fence erected on the surface shall, once at least in every seven days, be examined by a competent person and a report of every such inspection shall be recorded in a bound paged book kept for the purpose, duly signed and dated by the person who made the examination.
remarks: Distinct record from Reg 128(1) fencing requirement — this is the periodic examination/record obligation for that fencing, including the OC top-edge fence.

title: Plans and Sections Submitted After Abandonment, Closure or Discontinuance
detail:
Reg 66(1): Where any mine or seam or section thereof is abandoned, closed or the working thereof has been discontinued over a period exceeding sixty days, the person who was the owner of the mine at the time of abandonment, closure or discontinuance shall, within thirty days after the abandonment or closure, or within ninety days after the discontinuance of the workings, submit to the Chief Inspector two true copies of the up-to-date plan and section of the workings of the mine or seam or section maintained under clauses (a), (b), (c), (e) and (g) of sub-regulation (1) of regulation 65, showing the bearing and distance of at least one of the shafts or openings of the mine from a tri-junction or revenue pillar or other prominent permanent surface feature, the position of all water-dams built belowground (with dimensions and construction particulars), and the spot levels at the ends of the workings. Proviso: if change of ownership occurs after abandonment/closure and before expiry of the 30/90 day period, plans and sections shall be submitted forthwith.
Reg 66(2): The original or a certified true copy of the plan and section submitted shall be kept in the office at the mine.
Reg 66(3): The Chief Inspector may, on conditions and on payment of cost, supply copies of the plan/section to any person having bonafide interest in the mine, or to the owner/agent/manager of an adjacent mine.
frequency: Within 30 days of abandonment/closure; within 90 days of discontinuance; forthwith if ownership changes during that period
mode: Physical (2 true copies of plan + section)
remarks: GAP IDENTIFIED from original register cross-check (Sep 2026). Applies to all mines, not UG-only — was mistakenly dropped when UG-specific items were removed. Distinct from the Reg 5 notice (intention to abandon) — this is the actual plan submission after the fact.

title: Plans, Sections and Records — Electronic Form (Special Permission)
detail: Where special conditions exist, the Chief Inspector may permit preparation and maintenance of plans, sections and records required to be maintained under the provisions of these regulations, subject to such conditions as he may specify, in electronic form within the limits of error of survey and plotting as specified under sub-regulation (3) of regulation 64.
frequency: As permitted by CI, on application by owner/agent/manager
remarks: GAP IDENTIFIED from original register cross-check (Sep 2026). Minor — this is an enabling provision allowing electronic maintenance of statutory plans/records rather than a standalone active compliance obligation; relevant only if the mine seeks CI permission to digitize plans/records.

title: Vibration Report — ground vibration record for each blast
detail: Daily ground vibration record (seismograph) for every blast, per condition of the site-specific DGMS blasting permission.
signerRole: Blasting Officer / Shot-firer; countersigned by Manager
remarks: Not a CMR requirement — CMR is silent on vibration. This is a condition of your specific DGMS blasting permission, so track it exactly as that permission requires and re-verify if the permission is renewed or revised.

title: TRAINING OF PERSONNEL at licensed factory — records of training maintained
detail: Every person engaged in the manufacturing factory must be imparted PERIODIC SAFETY TRAINING by a competent person covering manufacture, handling, transportation and storage of explosives. Records of all such training must be maintained. SME supervisor must be appointed in WRITING by the licensee (SET-V Cond. 6) and be conversant with emergency procedures.
formNo: Training records (no prescribed form); SME supervisor written appointment letter
frequency: PERIODIC (frequency to be defined in SMP); records retained continuously
mode: Physical training records + written supervisor appointment
remarks: NEW. Two sub-obligations: (1) periodic safety training for ALL factory personnel — records maintained; (2) SME supervisor must be APPOINTED IN WRITING by the licensee (SET-V Cond. 6). Define and document the training frequency in your SMP (Rule 26(3)(t): 'competence of personnel for tasks' is a mandatory SMP element).

title: SAFETY MANAGEMENT PLAN (SMP) — maintain, implement and annually test emergency plan
detail: The SMP submitted with the project report (Rule 26(2)(g)) must be actively maintained and implemented. Rule 26(3)(e): SMP must include emergency response planning with TESTING OF THE EMERGENCY PLAN ONCE IN A YEAR. SMP must cover 21 mandatory elements including hazard identification, accident reporting, escape routes, fire fighting, material handling, self-auditing and external safety auditing.
formNo: SMP document (per Rule 26(3)); emergency plan test records
frequency: Annual emergency plan test (Rule 26(3)(e)); SMP maintained continuously; self-audit and external safety audit periodically
monitoringAuthority: Controller of Explosives (on inspection); Chief Controller (process approval per Rule 26(4))
mode: Written SMP document + annual emergency plan test record
remarks: NEW. The SMP is NOT just a licence application document — it is a LIVE OPERATIONAL DOCUMENT that must be maintained and implemented. Annual testing of the emergency plan (Rule 26(3)(e)) is a time-bound compliance event. Rule 26(3)(u): safety meetings, self-auditing AND external safety auditing are mandatory SMP elements.

title: RECORDS OF ALL ACCIDENTS within licensed premises
detail: Records of all accidents occurring within the licensed premises must be maintained and made available to the inspecting authority.
frequency: Continuous — on every accident within licensed premises
remarks: Covers ALL accidents — not only those reportable under Rule 131. Maintain this register separately from the DGMS accident register under OSH FORM XIX. Every accident, not just serious ones.

title: FIRE EXTINGUISHERS — provision, location, examination and recharging
detail: Road van: 2 fire extinguishers minimum 2 kg each (one for electrical fires, one for petroleum/other fires). BMD vehicles: at least 2 fire extinguishers of suitable size capable of fighting BOTH ELECTRICAL AND PETROLEUM fires, in easily accessible positions, kept ready during manufacture. All extinguishers examined and recharged per manufacturer's recommendations.
frequency: Examined and recharged AS PER MANUFACTURER'S RECOMMENDATIONS; kept ready during SME manufacture
remarks: EACH BMD VEHICLE must carry at least two extinguishers — per-vehicle, not a pooled arrangement at the plant. Verify at each vehicle inspection. Read with CMR Reg 139(6) monthly fire equipment examination.

title: BMD VEHICLE — operation, driver competence, banksman and movement controls
detail: No mixing during transit or while vehicle is in motion. A SECOND PERSON (banksman) must guide the driver whenever the BMD vehicle moves in the charging area. No smoking, matches or flame-producing device in or about bulk vehicle during mixing/loading operations. BMD vehicle driven only by capable, competent driver trained in operation, mixing/conveying equipment, and emergency procedures.
regulationRef: Schedule VI Part 2, items 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13; SET-V Cond. 6
frequency: Continuous during every SME loading operation
remarks: BANKSMAN IS MANDATORY (item 12): a second person must guide the driver's movements in the charging area. This has direct manpower implications for every BMD loading shift.

title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURE — personnel to be conversant; written procedure maintained
detail: Licensee and employees must be conversant with emergency procedures specific to each licensed premises (magazine, SME plant, road van). Written emergency procedure maintained with dated training/briefing records for all employees.
regulationRef: SET-VII Cond. 35; SET-V Cond. 16; LE-7 Cond. 14
frequency: Continuous — training and awareness maintained; annual emergency plan test (see Records S.No. 7 — SMP)
remarks: Maintain a documented emergency procedure specific to explosives premises — separate from the general mine ERP under CMR Reg 252.

title: RESPONSIBILITY OF PERSON IN CHARGE of blasting operations — dual statutory liability
detail: Licensee/shot-firer personally responsible for all precautions against fire, accident, loss and pilferage of explosives at the blasting site. Blasting in mines governed by Mines Act 1952 and CMR 2017 — but shot-firer remains PERSONALLY LIABLE under the Explosives Act 1884 and ER 2008 simultaneously.
signerRole: Licensee + Shot-firer (personally liable under both statutes)
remarks: DUAL STATUTORY LIABILITY: Rule 97 confirms mine blasting is governed by CMR, BUT the shot-firer remains liable under Explosives Act as well. Rule 98 (shot-firer's certificate from Controller) applies to areas OTHER THAN mines — the CMR-appointed shot-firer applies in the mine.

title: Explosive Loading Sheet — quantity charged per hole with hole depth
detail: Quantity of explosive charged and hole depth logged per hole, per blast, by shot-firer.
remarks: Cross-statutory record — CMR obligation that reconciles with ER 2008 magazine RE-5 issue records.

title: RECORD OF POST-SHOT-FIRING INSPECTION in bound paged book (CMR Reg 203)
detail: After each shot-firing, the shot-firer must examine the area for safety before allowing re-entry; examination particulars recorded in a bound paged book, signed and dated.
monitoringAuthority: Maintained at mine; produced to DGMS Inspector / Controller on demand
remarks: Distinct from the Explosive Loading Sheet (quantity/hole-depth) — this is the POST-blast safety inspection record. Cross-statutory obligation under CMR.

title: TRAINING of personnel for operation and maintenance of electrical installations + REFRESHER TRAIN...
detail:
Reg 118(1): The persons engaged for OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF ELECTRICAL INSTALLATIONS IN MINES are required to UNDERGO THE TYPE OF TRAINING MEANT FOR THE PARTICULAR MINING INSTALLATION OF COAL or Oil or Metal, training syllabus AS ISSUED BY DGMS from time to time under intimation in writing to the Authority.
Reg 118(2): The owner or manager or agent of the mine SHALL ARRANGE FOR TRAINING of their personnel in his OWN INSTITUTE or any other institute RECOGNISED BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT OR STATE GOVERNMENT.
Reg 118(3): THE REFRESHER TRAINING SHALL BE IMPARTED AT A PERIODICITY OF INTERVALS NOT MORE THAN TWO YEARS. A REGISTER or in electronic form shall be MAINTAINED wherein the NAMES OF THE PERSONS TRAINED, DUE DATE OF REFRESHER TRAINING AND THE LIKE shall be entered, and THE REGISTER MAINTAINED SHALL BE PRODUCED BEFORE THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES WHENEVER REQUIRED BY HIM.
frequency: REFRESHER TRAINING AT INTERVALS NOT MORE THAN 2 YEARS; register maintained continuously
remarks: NOTE THE DIFFERENT INTERVAL: electrical refresher training is every 2 YEARS under CER, whereas general mine refresher training under OSH Rule 159 is every 4 YEARS. Track them separately. The register must record the DUE DATE of the next refresher, not merely the date trained.

title: Display of INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESUSCITATION of persons suffering from electric shock
detail:
Reg 30(1): INSTRUCTIONS, in ENGLISH OR HINDI AND THE LOCAL LANGUAGE OF THE DISTRICT (and where Hindi is the local language, in English and Hindi), FOR THE RESUSCITATION OF PERSONS SUFFERING FROM ELECTRIC SHOCK, SHALL BE AFFIXED BY THE OWNER IN A CONSPICUOUS PLACE in every generating station, enclosed substation, enclosed switching station, MINES and in every factory in which electricity is used.
Reg 30(2): The owner shall ENSURE THAT ALL DESIGNATED PERSONS or persons engaged or appointed to operate and maintain electrical plants ARE ACQUAINTED WITH AND ARE COMPETENT TO APPLY THE INSTRUCTIONS referred to in sub-regulation (1).
frequency: Continuous display; competence of designated persons ensured on an ongoing basis
remarks: Not merely a display obligation — Reg 30(2) requires the owner to ENSURE COMPETENCE of every designated person to actually APPLY the resuscitation instructions. Keep a training/briefing record demonstrating this.

title: PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT — fire buckets, fire extinguishers (tested), first-aid boxes, gas masks, art...
detail:
Reg 29(1): FIRE BUCKETS FILLED WITH CLEAN DRY SAND and ready for immediate use, IN ADDITION TO FIRE EXTINGUISHERS suitable for dealing with fires, shall be CONSPICUOUSLY MARKED AND KEPT in all generating stations, enclosed substations and enclosed switching-stations in convenient location.
Reg 29(2): Appropriate type of fire extinguisher conforming to relevant standards shall be INSTALLED, MAINTAINED, PERIODICALLY INSPECTED AND TESTED as per the relevant standards, and RECORD OF SUCH TESTS SHALL BE MAINTAINED.
Reg 29(3): SUFFICIENT NUMBER OF FIRST-AID BOXES OR CUPBOARDS conspicuously marked and equipped shall be provided and maintained at appropriate locations in every generating station, enclosed substation, enclosed switching station AND IN VEHICLES USED FOR MAINTENANCE OF LINES, readily available and accessible at all times; and except in unattended substations, kept UNDER THE CHARGE OF RESPONSIBLE PERSONS TRAINED IN FIRST-AID, one of whom shall be AVAILABLE DURING WORKING HOURS.
Reg 29(4): TWO OR MORE GAS MASKS shall be provided and maintained at accessible places in every generating station of 5 MW and above and ENCLOSED SUBSTATION WITH TRANSFORMATION CAPACITY OF 5 MVA AND ABOVE.
Reg 29(5): In every generating station, substation or switching station, an ARTIFICIAL RESPIRATOR, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, FIRST-AID BOXES AND GAS MASKS shall be provided and KEPT IN GOOD WORKING CONDITION, and LOCATIONS OF THE SAME SHALL BE DISPLAYED IN THE CONTROL ROOM AND OPERATOR CABIN.
frequency: Continuous provision; fire extinguishers periodically inspected and TESTED with RECORD MAINTAINED
remarks: Note the 5 MVA threshold triggers the GAS MASK requirement for enclosed substations — commonly overlooked in OC mine substations. First-aid boxes are also required IN LINE MAINTENANCE VEHICLES, not just at fixed installations.

title: FLEXIBLE CABLE examination by designated operator + length limits for OC HEMM
detail:
Reg 109(5): EVERY FLEXIBLE CABLE ATTACHED TO A PORTABLE OR TRANSPORTABLE MACHINE SHALL BE EXAMINED PERIODICALLY BY THE PERSON DESIGNATED TO OPERATE THE MACHINE, and if such cable is used underground it shall be examined AT LEAST ONCE IN EACH SHIFT by such person; and IF SUCH CABLE IS FOUND TO BE DAMAGED OR DEFECTIVE, IT SHALL FORTHWITH BE REPLACED BY A CABLE IN GOOD CONDITION.
Reg 109(8): FLEXIBLE CABLE EXCEEDING ONE HUNDRED METRE IN LENGTH SHALL NOT BE USED with any portable or transportable apparatus.
SECOND PROVISO: The aforesaid cable IN CASE OF AN OPEN CAST MINE WHEN USED WITH ELECTRICALLY OPERATED HEAVY EARTH MOVING MACHINERY SHALL NOT EXCEED SIX HUNDRED METRE IN LENGTH, and FOR BUCKET WHEEL EXCAVATOR AT 11 kV SHALL NOT EXCEED ONE THOUSAND METRE IN LENGTH.
THIRD PROVISO: In case of DRAGLINE OR 42 CUBIC METRE CAPACITY SHOVEL, flexible cable length may be raised UP TO 600 METRE.
Reg 109(11): Where flexible cables are used they shall be DETACHED OR OTHERWISE ISOLATED FROM THE SOURCE OF SUPPLY WHEN NOT IN USE, and ARRANGEMENTS SHALL BE MADE TO PREVENT THE ENERGISING OF SUCH CABLES BY UNDESIGNATED PERSONS.
frequency: Examined PERIODICALLY by the designated operator (at least once per shift if used underground); replaced forthwith if damaged
remarks: DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO OC HEMM. Trailing cable length limits: 600 m for electrically operated HEMM including draglines and 42 cu.m shovels; 1000 m for bucket wheel excavator at 11 kV. Exceeding these is a contravention. Note also Reg 109(6) proviso exempts reeling/unreeling OC equipment from the flexible metallic screening requirement.

title: FIRE EXTINGUISHING APPLIANCES in every place in a mine containing apparatus
detail: Reg 100(3): FIRE EXTINGUISHING APPLIANCES OF ADEQUATE CAPACITY AND OF AN APPROVED TYPE as per relevant standards as amended from time to time SHALL BE INSTALLED AND PROPERLY MAINTAINED IN EVERY PLACE IN A MINE CONTAINING APPARATUS, other than cables, telecommunication and signalling apparatus.
remarks: Applies to EVERY PLACE containing apparatus, not just substations. Read together with CMR Reg 139(6) which requires monthly examination of all fire-fighting equipment, and Reg 29(2) of CER which requires periodic testing with records.

title: HANDLING OF ELECTRIC SUPPLY LINES AND APPARATUS — PPE, permit-to-work and Schedule I precautions
detail:
Reg 21(1): BEFORE ANY CONDUCTOR OR APPARATUS IS HANDLED, ADEQUATE PRECAUTIONS SHALL BE TAKEN, BY EARTHING OR OTHER SUITABLE MEANS, TO DISCHARGE ELECTRICALLY SUCH CONDUCTOR OR APPARATUS,
Reg 21(2): EVERY PERSON WORKING ON AN ELECTRIC SUPPLY LINE OR APPARATUS SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH — (a) PPE, TOOLS AND DEVICES such as RUBBER GLOVES AND SAFETY FOOTWEAR SUITABLE FOR WORKING VOLTAGE, SAFETY BELTS FOR WORKING AT HEIGHT, NONCONDUCTIVE LADDER, EARTHING DEVICES OF APPROPRIATE CLASS, HELMET, LINE TESTER, HAND LINES, VOLTAGE DETECTOR AND HAND TOOLS; and (b) ANY OTHER DEVICE FOR PROTECTING HIM FROM MECHANICAL AND ELECTRICAL INJURY DUE TO ARC FLASH; and such PPE SHALL ALWAYS BE MAINTAINED IN SOUND WORKING CONDITION.
Reg 21(3): NO PERSON SHALL OPERATE AND UNDERTAKE MAINTENANCE WORK on any part of an electrical plant or supply line, AND NO PERSON SHALL ASSIST SUCH PERSON, UNLESS HE IS DESIGNATED IN THAT BEHALF AND OBSERVES THE SAFETY PRECAUTIONS GIVEN IN PART-I, PART-II, PART-III AND PART-IV OF SCHEDULE I.
Reg 21(5): ALL NON-CURRENT CARRYING METAL PARTS OF SWITCHGEAR AND CONTROL PANELS SHALL BE PROPERLY EARTHED AND INSULATING FLOORS OR MATS conforming to relevant standards, OF APPROPRIATE VOLTAGE LEVEL, SHALL BE PROVIDED IN FRONT AND REAR OF THE PANELS.
Schedule I Part-II requires the Engineer or Supervisor in-charge to IDENTIFY HAZARDS, BRIEF THE WORKING GROUP, and OBTAIN PROPER PERMIT-TO-WORK from the Operation In-charge, ensuring the section is ISOLATED FROM ALL SOURCES OF ENERGY, DE-ENERGISED AND EARTHED.
frequency: Before and during every job on electrical lines/apparatus; PPE maintained continuously
remarks: PERMIT-TO-WORK SYSTEM IS MANDATORY via Schedule I Part-II. Insulating mats are required in FRONT AND REAR of panels, not just in front. Maintain permit-to-work records as evidence of compliance.

title: Register of accidents and dangerous occurrences
detail: Register of accidents and dangerous occurrences
remarks: Coordinate with Safety

title: Medical examination record for mine employees
detail: Medical examination record for mine employees
remarks: Mine-specific form

title: Display statutory workplace particulars and labour notices
detail: Display statutory workplace particulars and labour notices
remarks: Includes establishment details, hours, wage period/payment date, accident/dangerous occurrence information etc.

title: Safety Committee worker representation and functioning
detail: Safety Committee worker representation and functioning
remarks: Safety owns technical safety; HR owns worker-representation/admin side

title: Mine employee medical examination records
detail: Mine employee medical examination records

title: IMMEDIATE REPORT of accident, fire, explosion, loss, shortage or theft of explosives
detail: Report by phone/email/fax within 24 hrs, written report follows, to Chief Controller, Controller, DM & nearest police. Shortage/theft also reportable; wreckage untouched pending Chief Controller's visit.
regulationRef: Rule 131(1)-(2); SET-VII Cond. 11 & 38; SET-V Cond. 19; SET-VIII conditions
frequency: WITHIN 24 HOURS by fastest means + written report; licence conditions require IMMEDIATE reporting of loss/shortage/theft
monitoringAuthority: Chief Controller + Controller + District Magistrate + Officer-in-charge nearest Police Station + Licensing Authority
mode: Telephone / Fax / E-mail / Electronic / Special Messenger, followed by written report
remarks: CRITICAL. Note SHORTAGE OF STOCK is reportable, not just theft — a stock reconciliation discrepancy triggers this obligation. Rule 131(2) SCENE PRESERVATION is absolute: wreckage and debris must not be disturbed pending the Chief Controller visit, except for rescue and body recovery. This runs parallel to (not instead of) the CMR Reg 8 and OSH Rule 7 accident notices to DGMS.

title: PRIOR APPROVAL of site and construction before establishing licensed premises
detail: Prior approval of site, plans & specification from licensing authority (Chief Controller/Controller) needed before any construction of factory/magazine. Separate sequence: (i) prior approval → (ii) NOC → (iii) licence application on completion — three distinct steps, not one.
formNo: AE-1 / AE-3 / AE-7 (application forms); scrutiny fee as per Schedule IV
remarks: Applies whenever a new magazine or SME/ANFO facility is planned or an existing one is materially expanded. NOTE: Rule 101(4) — prior approval NOT necessary for: manufacture of ANFO in tractor compressor, tractor compressor licence, shop possession, import/export.

title: NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE (NOC) from DGMS / District Magistrate before construction
detail: After prior approval under Rule 101, and before commencing construction of licensed premises, an NOC must be obtained. For ANFO/SME/LOX sites coming under Mines Act 1952, the DGMS is the NOC authority — NOT the District Magistrate. For other sites, DM is the authority. NOC must be obtained within 6 months of application, in the format prescribed in Part 2, Schedule V.
formNo: FORM AE-12 (application for NOC); NOC in format prescribed in Part 2, Schedule V
frequency: After prior approval, before construction begins; authority to complete within 6 months of application
monitoringAuthority: Director General of Mines Safety [DGMS] (for ANFO/SME/LOX under Mines Act) OR District Magistrate (other sites)
remarks: DISTINCT STEP between site approval (Rule 101) and the licence application (Rule 105). CRITICAL: For OC coal mine ANFO/SME plant under Mines Act, DGMS is the NOC authority per Rule 103(2). Do not approach DM for this NOC.

title: APPLICATION for grant of licence after completion of construction
detail: On completion of construction per approved plans, application for grant of licence made in the appropriate form with all documents per Rule 113. Licensing authority conducts inspection, endorses the licence — licence comes into force only from date of endorsement. Provisional permission may be issued pending endorsement.
formNo: AE-1 (manufacture), AE-3 (possession/use), AE-7 (road van); licence forms LE-1, LE-3, LE-7
frequency: After completion of construction; licence endorsed only after inspection by licensing authority
monitoringAuthority: Licensing authority per Schedule IV Part 1 (Chief Controller/Controller for LE-1 SME/ANFO, LE-3 use; Controller for LE-7)
remarks: THIRD STEP of the three-step sequence. Note Rule 107(3): licence endorsed (and comes into force) only after inspection by licensing authority — operating before endorsement is a contravention. Provisional permission may be issued pending endorsement.

title: PRIOR APPROVAL for MANUFACTURING PROCESS from licensing authority
detail: Before manufacturing any authorised explosive, the process of manufacture must be approved by the licensing authority and written permission obtained — separate from the licence itself. A project report (containing 9 specified particulars including detailed process, raw material specs, SMP, MSDS and prescribed scrutiny fee) must be submitted to the Chief Controller separately for each explosive. Rule 26(5): No change in process, composition, specification or limiting % of raw materials without prior written approval of licensing authority. Rule 27: A copy of the Safety Management Plan must be submitted to the District Magistrate.
formNo: Project report per Rule 26(2); scrutiny fee per Schedule IV (Rs. 1,000 for scrutiny of manufacturing process change; Rs. 2,000 for new explosive approval)
frequency: Before commencing manufacture of each explosive; before any process change; one-time per explosive formulation + event-triggered on any change
monitoringAuthority: Chief Controller of Explosives (project report + process approval); District Magistrate (SMP copy per Rule 27)
remarks: CRITICAL. TWO SEPARATE SUBMISSIONS: (1) Project report + SMP to Chief Controller for process approval per Rule 26(2); (2) Copy of SMP to District Magistrate per Rule 27. Rule 26(5) imposes a change-control obligation — any change in formulation, process, raw material spec or limiting % requires prior written approval from the licensing authority BEFORE the change is made. Rule 26(6): Chief Controller may order tests on raw materials/ingredients at any time.

title: PRIOR APPROVAL for any change or alteration to licensed premises
detail: No changes/alterations to licensed premises without prior written approval of licensing authority. If authority directs repairs/changes, licensee must execute and report compliance within specified period. Rule 109: licence amendment required when physical alteration changes the premises from what the licence drawings show.
regulationRef: SET-VII Cond. 13; SET-VIII Cond. 12; SET-V Cond. 18; Rule 109
frequency: Before any change/alteration; compliance report within period specified by authority
remarks: TWO-WAY OBLIGATION: prior approval before the licensee makes changes, AND mandatory execution + compliance reporting when the authority directs changes. Track any written direction from the Controller with its deadline. Read with Rule 37(4): after MAJOR REPAIRS to a building or machinery, the building must not be taken back into use without permission of the licensing authority — a separate re-commissioning approval.

title: IMMEDIATE communication of any ENCROACHMENT OF SAFETY DISTANCE
detail: Any encroachment of safety distance (incl. HT lines, highways, railways, dwelling houses) to be immediately communicated to licensing authority for advice and action.
regulationRef: SET-VII Cond. 17; SET-VIII Cond. 15; Rule 86; Schedule VIII
remarks: CRITICAL FOR AN ACTIVE OC MINE. Protected works expressly include OVERHEAD HIGH TENSION POWER LINES, PUBLIC HIGHWAYS and RAILWAY LINES. As the mine develops — new haul roads, new HT lines, new workshops, contractor colonies — an encroachment can arise on the protected-works side without anything changing at the magazine. Re-verify safety distances per Schedule VIII Tables 1/2 whenever the site layout changes.

title: FORTHWITH report if magazine becomes UNFIT for storage
detail: Magazine kept in good repair at all times; licensee to report forthwith if it becomes unfit for storage for any reason whatsoever.
frequency: FORTHWITH on the magazine becoming unfit
remarks: Triggered by structural damage, roof leakage, lightning conductor failure, flooding — 'for any reason whatsoever' is deliberately broad. Do not wait to assess — report first, then arrange inspection.

title: IMMEDIATE intimation if any explosive found DETERIORATED or UNSERVICEABLE
detail: Any explosive showing signs of deterioration must be immediately reported to licensing authority and physically SET ASIDE for examination. Disposal only per the authority's written directions, at the licensee's expense — not at the mine's own initiative.
frequency: IMMEDIATELY on detection; explosive set aside pending authority's examination
remarks: TWO DISTINCT ACTIONS: (1) REPORT immediately; (2) PHYSICALLY SET ASIDE the deteriorated explosive — do not use, do not destroy, do not return to storage pending the authority's written direction. Frozen NG explosives: thawed only under supervision of experienced persons (Rule 91(4)).

title: PRIOR INTIMATION before REPACKING explosives from damaged outer packages
detail: Explosives from damaged outer packages may be repacked only after giving prior intimation WELL IN ADVANCE to the Controller having jurisdiction, with all necessary details. Repacking must be done in an APPROVED OPEN-SIDED SHED, never inside the magazine or storehouse.
frequency: PRIOR INTIMATION WELL IN ADVANCE of repacking
remarks: TWO ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS: repacking must NEVER be done inside the magazine or storehouse; it must be done in an APPROVED open-sided shed at an approved distance. Confirm an approved repacking shed exists and is shown in the approved drawings before the need arises.

title: PERMIT for storage of explosives IN EXCESS of licensed quantity
detail: Excess storage permit valid maximum 15 days, capped at 1/3 of licensed quantity, on payment of prescribed fees. Repeated requests may be refused.
formNo: Written application; fee per Part 2 Schedule IV (Rs. 500 for first 15 days + Rs. 200 per additional day)
frequency: Before exceeding licensed quantity; permit valid MAXIMUM 15 DAYS; excess capped at 1/3 of licensed quantity
remarks: HARD LIMITS: 15 days maximum, one-third of licensed quantity maximum, and REPEATED applications themselves become a ground for refusal. Plan indent scheduling so excess-storage permits are not routinely needed.

title: RENEWAL of licence before expiry
detail: Renewal application (Form RE-1 + original licence + fee) must REACH licensing authority on or before expiry date. Maximum 3 months' grace after expiry — after which treated as a fresh licence application. AMENDED: Explosives (Amendment) Rules, 2025 (notified 1 May 2025) amended Rule 112(1) and 112(8) — renewal period is now up to TEN financial years (was five), subject to no contravention history.
formNo: FORM RE-1 (+ original licence + renewal fee per Schedule IV)
frequency: ON OR BEFORE DATE OF EXPIRY; absolute cut-off 3 MONTHS after expiry (after which fresh licence required)
monitoringAuthority: Licensing Authority (Chief Controller / Controller / District Magistrate)
remarks: CRITICAL DEADLINE — UPDATED FOR 2025 AMENDMENT. Licence period now up to 10 financial years (was 5) per amended Rule 112(1) and 112(8). Late fee (equal to one year's licence fee) if renewal application reaches after expiry but within 3 months and delay is beyond licensee's control. Miss 3 months: the licence is gone and a fresh application is required. CONFIRMED: current LE-3 valid till 31.03.2030.

title: Application for AMENDMENT of licence — alteration, change of name, change of partners/directors
detail: Any alteration to premises (requiring amended drawings), name change of licensee entity, or change in partners/directors requires licence amendment. Application with prescribed scrutiny fee and amendment fee.
formNo: Application form as per licence type; scrutiny fee + amendment fee per Part 2, Schedule IV
frequency: On any alteration, change of name, change of partners/directors, or transfer
remarks: Company restructuring, board changes or change in registered name — commonly overlooked when corporate changes happen at head office. Rule 111: NEW directors/partners inducted (even without name change) must be separately intimated to licensing authority with antecedent verification, scrutiny fee and new occupier photographs.

title: INDENT for purchase of explosives
detail: Indent (Form RE-11) signed by licensee or authorised representative; photograph and specimen signature of licensee AND authorised representative must be on file with the supplier before delivery. Supplier must verify photo and signature before effecting delivery. Authorised representative may represent ONE licensee only. A copy of RE-11 must be carried in the vehicle during transport.
frequency: Per purchase; raised monthly at this mine per site practice
monitoringAuthority: Supplier (against licence); records produced to Controller on demand
