remarks: Three authentication requirements: (1) RE-11 signed; (2) licensee's photo + signature filed with supplier; (3) authorised rep's photo, attested specimen signature and address filed with supplier — refresh whenever personnel change. RE-11 copy must be in the vehicle during every consignment (Rule 50(1)(a)). Rule 77(2)(e): one authorised representative per licensee only.

title: TRANSPORT PASS for each consignment of explosives + copy despatch to five authorities
detail: Transport pass (Form RE-12) issued by consignor per consignment; attached to way-bill/invoice. A COPY must be sent FORTHWITH by the consignor to: (a) licensing authority of the consignor; (b) Controller AND District SP in whose jurisdiction the consignor is located; (c) Controller AND District SP in whose jurisdiction the consignee is located — FIVE SEPARATE AUTHORITY DESPATCHES per consignment. Original copy of RE-12 must be carried in the vehicle during transport.
frequency: Per consignment; COPY SENT FORTHWITH (immediately on issue) to five authorities; filed monthly at this mine per site practice
monitoringAuthority: Controller of Explosives (origin + destination) + District Superintendent of Police (origin + destination) + Licensing Authority of consignor — FIVE AUTHORITIES
remarks: CORRECTION: The original register listed only 'Controller + District SP (origin and destination)' — the licensing authority of the consignor (Rule 47(3)(a)) is a fifth mandatory copy recipient. THREE DOCUMENTS must be carried in the vehicle: authenticated transport licence copy, indent RE-11 copy, and transport pass RE-12. Verify all three on every inbound consignment before accepting delivery.

title: Notice of accident, breakdown, fire or explosion involving the ROAD VAN
detail: Any accident, fire or explosion involving road van: (a) comply with road accident law; (b) inform nearest police station; (c) licensee informs Chief Controller AND Controller in jurisdiction of accident with full details; arrange safe custody of explosives. Breakdown (no accident): inform licensee who informs Chief Controller and Controller. LE-7 Cond. 11 also requires immediate report to licensing authority; if loss of life/serious injury — also nearest police station.
monitoringAuthority: Chief Controller of Explosives + Controller (in whose jurisdiction accident/breakdown occurred) + Licensing Authority + nearest Police Station (if loss of life/serious injury)
remarks: NOTE: A mere BREAKDOWN with no fire or explosion is itself reportable. Rule 69 requires Chief Controller + Controller notification — this is broader than LE-7 Cond. 11 alone. Both apply. After breakdown, major repairs may not be commenced until explosives are removed and the van is moved at least 300 m from inhabited premises.

title: CUSTODY OF MAGAZINE KEYS + intimation of key-holder details with photograph
detail: Magazine keys kept only with licensee or authorised agent; key-holder's name, address and passport-size photograph must be furnished to BOTH the licensing authority AND the Controller having jurisdiction. Updated whenever the key custodian changes.
frequency: Continuous; INTIMATION on appointment and on every change of key custodian
remarks: EASILY MISSED: both the licensing authority AND the Controller must receive the key-holder details with photograph — not just one of them. Update whenever the magazine in-charge changes.

title: RESTRICTION ON NIGHT LOADING of explosives within a licensed factory
detail: Loading of explosives after sunset within a licensed factory may be carried out only up to 22:00 hours, and only at a place that is well-illuminated and specifically APPROVED BY THE CHIEF CONTROLLER.
frequency: Applicable whenever loading takes place after sunset within a licensed factory
monitoringAuthority: Chief Controller of Explosives (written approval of loading place required)
mode: Written approval of loading place; compliance at site
remarks: NEW. If BMD/road van loading at the support plant ever runs into evening hours, confirm the Chief Controller has specifically approved that loading place for after-dark use — or restrict loading to daylight hours.

title: CE-1 TEST CERTIFICATE for transport of Class 3 (Nitro-compound) explosives
detail: Before transporting or tendering for transport any explosive of Class 3 (Nitro-compound — emulsion explosives, ANFO boosters, dynamite etc.), the consignor must attach a VALID Certificate in Form CE-1 granted by the testing officer. CE-1 is valid for 12 months from date of issue. The mine as consignee must verify CE-1 is attached before accepting delivery.
regulationRef: Rule 48(1)-(3); Form CE-1; Part 2A Schedule IV
formNo: FORM CE-1 (Test Certificate for Explosives); fee: Rs. 100 initial test; Rs. 50 renewal without fresh test; Rs. 500 renewal with fresh test
frequency: Per consignment of Class 3 explosives transported; CE-1 valid for 12 MONTHS from issue
monitoringAuthority: Testing Officer (issues certificate); Commissioner of Customs (for imports); mine verifies on receipt
remarks: CRITICAL NEW FINDING — ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM PREVIOUS REGISTER. Class 3 explosives (most common mine explosives) cannot be transported without a current CE-1. Mine must verify the CE-1 is attached, valid, and covers the specific batch and date of manufacture before accepting delivery. A consignment without a current CE-1 must not be accepted.

title: LICENCE for possession/conversion of Ammonium Nitrate (SME plant & AN storage)
detail: No person shall store or convert ammonium nitrate beyond prescribed limits except under a licence granted under the AN Rules 2012. Distinct from ER 2008 licences — a separate regulatory instrument.
formNo: P-forms as applicable under AN Rules 2012
remarks: NEW — distinct from the AN stock account (daily record). This is the underlying AN Rules 2012 LICENCE obligation. AN Rules 2012 text not verified against ER 2008 PDF (different Act) — confirm current P-form number and threshold quantities with PESO before relying.

title: SME MANUFACTURE — dual clearance from Chief Controller + DGMS before commencing BMD/SME operations
detail: Before SME can be manufactured in a BMD vehicle within the mining area: (1) Written permission of the specific SME formulation from the Chief Controller of Explosives (SET-V Cond. 1); (2) Clearance from the Director General of Mines Safety under Mines Act in force (SET-V Cond. 2). SME manufactured only in accordance with conditions imposed by DGMS. This is a one-time approval per site/formulation, not a recurring filing.
frequency: Before commencing SME/BMD manufacturing operations; on any change of site, vehicle or formulation
monitoringAuthority: Chief Controller of Explosives + Director General of Mines Safety (DGMS)
mode: Written permissions (to be retained on file)
remarks: DUAL-REGULATOR CLEARANCE — both must be obtained. Day-to-day operating restrictions (sunrise-to-sunset, end-of-day cleaning) are compliance conditions tracked separately in Records. Also: Rule 26(5) — any change in SME formulation/process requires prior written approval of licensing authority before the change is made.

title: SPECIAL SANCTION for Class 3 (nitro-compound) explosives retained BEYOND 1 year from manufacture
detail: Where Class 3 (nitro-compound) explosive is to be kept beyond one year from date of manufacture, special written sanction must be obtained from the Licensing Authority/Controller of Explosives. Written sanction certificate retained and produced on demand at each inspection. Triggered only if FIFO stock rotation fails to move stock within a year.
frequency: CONDITIONAL: only if/when stock is retained beyond 1 year from manufacture
mode: Written sanction certificate retained and produced on demand
remarks: CONDITIONAL OBLIGATION — arises only if FIFO rotation fails. Sanction certificate must be obtained from the Controller at each inspection and retained. Disposal of explosives no longer fit for storage is at the licensee's own expense, per directions of Chief Controller/Controller.

title: Notice of accident (loss of life / serious bodily injury) or dangerous occurrence
detail:
OSH Rule 7(1): Where an accident occurs resulting in death — inform ICF forthwith in FORM-XI and inform electronically and by telephone to CICF, ICF, DM/SDO and the police station and family members or kin of the victim.
OSH Rule 7(2): Where accident results in bodily injury preventing work ≥48 hours — inform in FORM-XI within 12 hours after completion of 48 hours.
OSH Rule 7(3): Dangerous occurrence whether causing injury or not — within 12 hours send intimation to ICF and DM/SDO.
Proviso: if death occurs after notice already sent — forthwith send further notice by telephone and electronically, confirmed in writing within 12 hours.

CMR Reg 8(1): Forthwith inform RI by telephone/fax/email/special messenger; within 24 hours give formal notice to DM, CI, RI and Competent Authority for compensation. List of dangerous occurrences in Reg 8(1)(b)(i)-(xix) includes: explosion, spontaneous heating, fire, fall of HEMM from height, bursting of pressurised equipment, influx of gases, irruption of water, premature collapse, accident due to explosives, breakage of rope/chain/headgear, failure of dump or side in OC working, failure of structure/installation, electrical flash-over causing burn.

CMR Reg 8(2): Exhibit copy on special notice board at mine office ≥14 days.
formNo: FORM XI (OSH); Form as specified by CI (CMR)
frequency: Forthwith (death — OSH/CMR); within 12 hrs (injury >48hr / DO — OSH); within 24 hrs (CMR formal)
monitoringAuthority: ICF + DM/SDO + Police + Family (OSH); DM + CI + RI + Comp Authority (CMR)
remarks: CMR Reg 8(1)(b)(xvii): failure of dump or side in OC working is a dangerous occurrence — critical for OC mines.

title: Standing orders for use of two types of explosives in same OC shot-hole
detail: Where two types of explosives are used in the same shot hole in opencast working, standing orders framed by the manager shall be submitted to the Regional Inspector before such use.
remarks: OC-specific provision.

title: Blasting permission near permanent buildings
detail: Permission for blasting within the danger zone (up to 500m) of permanent buildings or structures — the aggregate maximum charge shall be based on scientific study and permission granted by the Chief Inspector.
frequency: Before blasting within 500m of permanent building/structure
remarks: Scientific study required to determine safe charge.

title: Written permission before BLASTING within 300 m of substation or lines exceeding 650 V
detail: No blasting for any purpose shall be done within THREE HUNDRED METRE from the boundary of a substation or from the electric supply lines of voltage exceeding 650 V or tower structure thereof, without the WRITTEN PERMISSION of the owner of such substation or electric supply lines or tower structures; and IN CASE OF MINING LEASE HOLD AREA, WITHOUT THE WRITTEN PERMISSION OF THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES.
frequency: Before every blasting activity within 300 m
monitoringAuthority: Owner of substation/line/tower + ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES (mandatory for mining lease hold area)
remarks: CRITICAL for OC blasting operations. Note the dual permission requirement — owner of the asset AND Electrical Inspector of Mines, the latter being specific to mining lease hold areas.

title: QUARTERLY RETURN of explosives manufactured, received, sold, transferred, used, destroyed
detail: Quarterly return to Controller of Explosives + District Magistrate — covering all explosives manufactured, received, sold, transferred, used, destroyed, imported or exported. Return must REACH the authority within the 10th day of every succeeding quarter. Applies SEPARATELY to each licence held — magazine (LE-3) and SME/ANFO plant (LE-1) each generate their own return.
formNo: Form prescribed in Part 5 of Schedule V (RE-7 for magazine; RE-2 extract for SME plant)
frequency: QUARTERLY — return must REACH authority BY THE 10th DAY OF THE SUCCEEDING QUARTER
remarks: Deadline is for the return to REACH the authority by the 10th — not merely to be despatched. Apply separately for each licence. NOTE: This return goes to Controller + DM. The RE-7 return to DM + SP/CP is a SEPARATE return (see Returns S.No. 2 below) — do not treat one as a substitute for the other.

title: QUARTERLY RETURN (RE-7) by magazine licensee to District Magistrate and District SP/Commissioner ...
detail: Quarterly RE-7 return (covering explosives received, used, sold, destroyed, stolen in the quarter) to District Magistrate AND District Superintendent of Police / Commissioner of Police, due by 10th of succeeding quarter. Supporting schedules: RE-12 transport passes for the quarter and RE-2 SME/ANFO stock register extract. This is DISTINCT from the Rule 24(3) return to Controller + DM.
regulationRef: SET-VII Cond. 16; SET-VIII Cond. 14 r/w Rule 24(3)-(4)
formNo: FORM RE-7 (with RE-12 and RE-2 attached as supporting schedules, per site practice)
frequency: QUARTERLY — to reach BY THE 10th DAY OF THE SUCCEEDING QUARTER
monitoringAuthority: District Magistrate + District Superintendent of Police / Commissioner of Police
remarks: DISTINCT FROM Returns S.No. 1 — different recipients (DM + SP/CP, not Controller) and different form (RE-7). CONFIRMED WITH BLASTING OFFICER: RE-7 filed with RE-12 (blasting accessories transport passes) and RE-2 (SME/ANFO stock register extract) attached.

title: Monthly magazine inspection report to Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM)
detail: Monthly magazine inspection report submitted to SDM on company letterhead, per district administration directive. District-specific obligation layered on top of the Explosives Rules 2008 return requirements.
remarks: Reclassified from Records to Returns — periodic submission to an external authority. Verify continued applicability with the SDM office periodically as district directives may change.

title: MAINTENANCE OF RECORDS in prescribed forms — page numbering, officer certification, 3-year retention
detail: Every licensee must maintain records in the prescribed RE forms specified in Part 5, Schedule V. Stock books must be PAGE-NUMBERED and CERTIFIED BY AN OFFICER AUTHORISED UNDER THESE RULES. All records retained for 3 years, unless otherwise directed.
formNo: RE series forms (RE-2, RE-3, RE-4, RE-5, RE-6) as applicable per licence type
monitoringAuthority: Controller / authorities specified in Rule 128 (on demand)
remarks: TWO EASILY-MISSED FORMALITIES: stock books must be PAGE NUMBERED, and must be CERTIFIED BY AN AUTHORISED OFFICER. Retention is 3 years — shorter than the DGMS 5-year rule; do not conflate. Erasures or overwriting in a page-numbered RE stock book can constitute falsification under Rule 23 — use single-line strike-through with initials and date.

title: STOCK REGISTER OF EXPLOSIVES MANUFACTURED — SME / ANFO bulk plant (Form RE-2)
detail: Record of all SME/ANFO manufactured in FORM RE-2; page-numbered stock book produced to Controller on demand. Each BMD vehicle batch manufactured must be separately accounted for.
frequency: Continuous — record of every manufacturing operation; produced on demand
monitoringAuthority: Controller of Explosives / authorised officers (on demand)
remarks: RE-2 records explosives MANUFACTURED — distinct from the RE-3/RE-4 magazine stock records. Each BMD vehicle batch must be accounted for. This is also the source document for the RE-7 and Rule 24(3) quarterly returns.

title: STOCK REGISTER OF MAGAZINE — receipts, issues, balance (Forms RE-3, RE-4, RE-5)
detail: Magazine stock continuously updated in forms: RE-3 (daily stock/receipts), RE-4 (account of sales), RE-5 (issue/consumption by shot-firer). Which forms apply depends on which licence SET (VII or VIII) is annexed to the magazine licence. Entries made on every receipt and issue.
formNo: FORM RE-3 (daily stock/receipts); FORM RE-4 (sales); FORM RE-5 (issue/consumption) — per licence SET
frequency: Continuous — updated on EVERY receipt and issue; produced on demand
monitoringAuthority: Controller of Explosives / authorised officers (on demand)
remarks: LICENCE-SET SPECIFIC: SET-VII requires RE-2 and RE-4; SET-VIII requires RE-3 and RE-4 OR RE-5. Confirm which SET is annexed to YOUR magazine licence and maintain exactly those forms. RE-3 is the daily basis stock update entry.

title: RECORD OF EXPLOSIVES TRANSPORTED by road van (Form RE-6 per Rule 61(2))
detail: Licensee of road van must maintain records of ALL transactions in FORM RE-6 (Rule 61(2)). NOTE ON DISCREPANCY: LE-7 Condition 13 specifies FORM RE-5 (account of explosives used) rather than RE-6 — this appears to be a drafting error in the licence conditions. Rule 61(2) (the substantive rule prescribing RE-6, 'Records of explosives transported by road van') takes precedence. Verify current PESO interpretation before determining which form to maintain.
formNo: FORM RE-6 per Rule 61(2); FORM RE-5 cited in LE-7 Cond. 13 — maintain BOTH pending PESO clarification
frequency: Continuous — per consignment transported; produced on demand
remarks: DISCREPANCY FLAGGED: Rule 61(2) = Form RE-6; LE-7 Cond. 13 = Form RE-5. As a matter of abundant caution, maintain RE-6 per the substantive rule. A signed AUTHORISATION DOCUMENT naming persons permitted to drive and accompany the van must be carried in the vehicle whenever the licensee is not the driver.

title: RECORD OF SERVICING, MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS — plant and equipment at SME/ANFO plant
detail: Every building, plant and equipment in the licensed factory must be regularly serviced and maintained. Rule 37(3): If repairs require use of any SOURCE OF FIRE, a WRITTEN HOT-WORK PERMIT must be issued, copies preserved for 3 months and produced on demand to inspecting authority. Rule 37(5): Record of all servicing and maintenance maintained until next servicing; for major repairs/replacement, record preserved until replacement of that machinery/equipment.
formNo: Written hot-work permit (Rule 37(3)); maintenance log (Rule 37(5)); both produced on demand
frequency: Continuous; hot-work permit copies retained 3 MONTHS and produced on demand; maintenance log retained until replacement of equipment
mode: Physical records (hot-work permit log + maintenance register)
remarks: NEW. TWO DISTINCT DOCUMENTS: (1) WRITTEN HOT-WORK PERMIT before any fire source is used during repairs (copy preserved 3 months); (2) MAINTENANCE LOG per piece of equipment. Critical for BMD vehicles — ammonium nitrate residue in hollow shafts + welding = explosion risk. Hot-work permit is mandatory, not optional.

title: TRAINING OF PERSONNEL at licensed factory — records of training maintained
detail: Every person engaged in the manufacturing factory must be imparted PERIODIC SAFETY TRAINING by a competent person covering manufacture, handling, transportation and storage of explosives. Records of all such training must be maintained. SME supervisor must be appointed in WRITING by the licensee (SET-V Cond. 6) and be conversant with emergency procedures.
formNo: Training records (no prescribed form); SME supervisor written appointment letter
frequency: PERIODIC (frequency to be defined in SMP); records retained continuously
mode: Physical training records + written supervisor appointment
remarks: NEW. Two sub-obligations: (1) periodic safety training for ALL factory personnel — records maintained; (2) SME supervisor must be APPOINTED IN WRITING by the licensee (SET-V Cond. 6). Define and document the training frequency in your SMP (Rule 26(3)(t): 'competence of personnel for tasks' is a mandatory SMP element).

title: SAFETY MANAGEMENT PLAN (SMP) — maintain, implement and annually test emergency plan
detail: The SMP submitted with the project report (Rule 26(2)(g)) must be actively maintained and implemented. Rule 26(3)(e): SMP must include emergency response planning with TESTING OF THE EMERGENCY PLAN ONCE IN A YEAR. SMP must cover 21 mandatory elements including hazard identification, accident reporting, escape routes, fire fighting, material handling, self-auditing and external safety auditing.
formNo: SMP document (per Rule 26(3)); emergency plan test records
frequency: Annual emergency plan test (Rule 26(3)(e)); SMP maintained continuously; self-audit and external safety audit periodically
monitoringAuthority: Controller of Explosives (on inspection); Chief Controller (process approval per Rule 26(4))
mode: Written SMP document + annual emergency plan test record
remarks: NEW. The SMP is NOT just a licence application document — it is a LIVE OPERATIONAL DOCUMENT that must be maintained and implemented. Annual testing of the emergency plan (Rule 26(3)(e)) is a time-bound compliance event. Rule 26(3)(u): safety meetings, self-auditing AND external safety auditing are mandatory SMP elements.

title: ANNUAL TESTING of LIGHTNING CONDUCTOR + display of test certificate
detail: Every magazine and process building must have efficient lightning conductors per BIS specifications. Earth resistance tested at least ONCE EVERY YEAR by a qualified electrical engineer or State Govt-certified competent person. Resistance not more than 10 ohms. Test certificate showing results and date of last test CONSPICUOUSLY DISPLAYED at the premises.
formNo: Test certificate (no prescribed form) — prominently displayed; fee Rs. 500 if tested by Departmental officer
frequency: AT LEAST ONCE IN EVERY YEAR; certificate CONSPICUOUSLY DISPLAYED
monitoringAuthority: Displayed at premises; produced to Controller / testing officer on demand
signerRole: Qualified Electrical Engineer or State-Govt certified competent person; Licensee (display obligation)
remarks: THREE DISTINCT REQUIREMENTS: annual test by a QUALIFIED PERSON; resistance ≤10 OHMS; certificate CONSPICUOUSLY DISPLAYED with date of last test. A test done but not displayed is still a contravention. Note: LE-4 condition (tractor compressor) requires annual check of compressor fittings — safety valve, limiting pressure switch and pressure gauge — in addition to lightning conductor.

title: THUNDERSTORM PROCEDURE — withdrawal of persons, locking and sealing of magazine
detail: On any imminent thunderstorm, every person in or about the magazine, storehouse or process building must be WITHDRAWN to a safe distance. Magazine/storehouse must be CLOSED AND LOCKED until the threat has passed. This is an absolute obligation — it does not require the thunderstorm to actually occur, only appear imminent.
frequency: On every occasion a thunderstorm appears imminent
mode: Written standing procedure + record of occurrences
remarks: HIGHLY RELEVANT IN CHHATTISGARH during monsoon and pre-monsoon season. Should be a written standing order with a defined safe-distance assembly point, and occurrences logged. Links directly to SME condition that manufacture is only between sunrise and sunset.

title: 15 METRE CLEAR ZONE around magazine + maintenance of Schedule VIII safety distances
detail: 15 metre zone surrounding the magazine kept clear of dried grass, bush and flammable materials at all times. Licensed factory/magazine must maintain safety distances per Schedule VIII Tables (Table 1 for ZZ category explosives, Table 2 for Y category). Guard shelter must be not less than 30 metres from the magazine.
regulationRef: Rule 86(1); SET-VII Cond. 21; SET-VIII Cond. 19; Schedule VIII
frequency: Continuous — clear zone maintained at all times; safety distances maintained
remarks: ACTIVE VEGETATION MANAGEMENT required — dried grass and bush accumulate rapidly in the post-monsoon period. Note ANFO shed requires fencing at a distance of 15 m (SET-III Cond. 2) as an additional specific requirement. Re-verify all safety distances per Schedule VIII whenever the mine layout changes.

title: SECURITY GUARDS — provision, strength, shelter; perimeter fencing for factory; max 4 persons in m...
detail: Rule 21(1)-(2): Security guards provided at licensee's cost, strength determined by District Magistrate. Rule 21(3): Factory licensed for manufacture of explosives must be surrounded by wall or security fencing at LEAST 2 METRES HIGH — to prevent entry of unauthorised persons. Rule 21(4): Fenced area must cover the full safety zone around process buildings. Rule 21(5): Guard shelter minimum 30 metres from magazine. SET-VIII Cond. 23: Not more than 4 persons inside magazine at any one time.
frequency: Continuous; guard strength determined by DM order (to be obtained in writing)
monitoringAuthority: District Magistrate (determines guard strength); Controller on inspection
remarks: CORRECTION: Original register cited Rule 21(1)-(2) and (5) only — Rule 21(3) and 21(4) (perimeter fencing requirement for the manufacturing factory) were missing. Guard strength is determined by DM — obtain and retain that determination in writing. The 4-person limit inside the magazine must be posted and enforced. Perimeter wall/fencing ≥2 m high for the ANFO/SME support plant.

title: RECORDS OF ALL ACCIDENTS within licensed premises
detail: Records of all accidents occurring within the licensed premises must be maintained and made available to the inspecting authority.
frequency: Continuous — on every accident within licensed premises
remarks: Covers ALL accidents — not only those reportable under Rule 131. Maintain this register separately from the DGMS accident register under OSH FORM XIX. Every accident, not just serious ones.

title: FIRE EXTINGUISHERS — provision, location, examination and recharging
detail: Road van: 2 fire extinguishers minimum 2 kg each (one for electrical fires, one for petroleum/other fires). BMD vehicles: at least 2 fire extinguishers of suitable size capable of fighting BOTH ELECTRICAL AND PETROLEUM fires, in easily accessible positions, kept ready during manufacture. All extinguishers examined and recharged per manufacturer's recommendations.
frequency: Examined and recharged AS PER MANUFACTURER'S RECOMMENDATIONS; kept ready during SME manufacture
remarks: EACH BMD VEHICLE must carry at least two extinguishers — per-vehicle, not a pooled arrangement at the plant. Verify at each vehicle inspection. Read with CMR Reg 139(6) monthly fire equipment examination.

title: BMD VEHICLE — static electricity control, hose testing, electrical continuity and bonding
detail: Grounding device and semiconductive hose used during mixing/loading to prevent static electricity. Flexible hoses tested PERIODICALLY by water at prescribed pressure AND for electrical continuity. BMD vehicle body and equipment electrically continuous with chassis and bonded. Generator/battery cut-off switch accessible.
regulationRef: SET-V Cond. 7, 8; Schedule VI Part 2, items 14, 15, 17
frequency: PERIODIC hose tests — hydraulic pressure test AND electrical continuity test; static evaluation before each day's operations
mode: Physical + dated test records per hose per vehicle
remarks: TWO SEPARATE PERIODIC HOSE TESTS required: water pressure test AND electrical continuity test. Maintain dated test record per hose per vehicle. Periodicity not fixed by rule — define and justify in SOP (e.g. quarterly).

title: BMD VEHICLE — welding/cutting/hot-work prohibitions and mandatory wash-down
detail: No welding or cutting on BMD vehicle until vehicle is washed down and all explosive material, ingredients and oxidizer are removed. Hollow shafts must be cleaned inside and outside and vented before welding. No open flames around any part of mixing/delivery equipment unless completely washed down and oxidizer removed. HOT-WORK PERMIT mandatory per Rule 37(3).
formNo: Written hot-work permit (copy retained 3 months and produced on demand)
frequency: Before every welding, cutting or hot-work operation on a BMD vehicle; permit copy retained 3 months
remarks: CRITICAL WORKSHOP CONTROL. Ammonium nitrate residue in hollow shafts has caused fatal explosions during welding — documented case history. HOT-WORK PERMIT is mandatory, not discretionary. Wash-down and oxidizer removal must be documented before any hot work.

title: BMD VEHICLE — operation, driver competence, banksman and movement controls
detail: No mixing during transit or while vehicle is in motion. A SECOND PERSON (banksman) must guide the driver whenever the BMD vehicle moves in the charging area. No smoking, matches or flame-producing device in or about bulk vehicle during mixing/loading operations. BMD vehicle driven only by capable, competent driver trained in operation, mixing/conveying equipment, and emergency procedures.
regulationRef: Schedule VI Part 2, items 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13; SET-V Cond. 6
frequency: Continuous during every SME loading operation
remarks: BANKSMAN IS MANDATORY (item 12): a second person must guide the driver's movements in the charging area. This has direct manpower implications for every BMD loading shift.

title: CONVEYANCE OF EXPLOSIVES to blasting site and RETURN of unused explosives
detail: Explosives conveyed from licensed storage to site in original unopened packages or closed/locked containers. Not brought within 50 m of site until site is READY FOR CHARGING. No vehicle with other materials/tools except for blasting. Leftovers returned to magazine at end of every day's work. Detonators conveyed in separate non-metal/non-conductive containers, separately from other explosives and separately from batteries/electric energy sources. Loading for road transport only near or at a licensed magazine/premises.
frequency: Every conveyance to blasting site; return of leftover explosives AT END OF EVERY DAY'S WORK
monitoringAuthority: Controller (on inspection); reconciled in magazine records
mode: Compliance at site + magazine return records
remarks: THE 50-METRE RULE (Rule 90(2)) is frequently overlooked. Rule 90(4): leftover return — any unreturned balance is a reportable shortage. Rule 53(1): Loading/unloading must be at a safe distance from dwelling houses, factories, public buildings and flammable goods storage. Rule 53(2): Loading for road transport only near/at a licensed magazine.

title: PRECAUTIONS AT BLASTING SITE — power discontinuation, 15 m exclusion, charged holes unattended
detail: Electric power discontinued before charging. No work other than charging within 15 m of holes. Charged holes never left unattended until blasting is complete. Surplus explosives removed from vicinity of hole after charging. No damage to fuse/wires during stemming.
remarks: Rule 92(4): CHARGED HOLES MUST NEVER BE LEFT UNATTENDED — significant manpower implication for overnight or multi-shift charging. Read with CMR Reg 203/206.

title: WARNING PROCEDURE, signals and public warning before and after blasting
detail: Written warning procedure with warning signs and audible signals established and all persons in area made conversant with them. Red flags in danger zone; all persons sheltered before firing. No person allowed within 30 minutes of firing unless CERTAIN all shots have exploded. Public not to approach site within 1 hour after explosion (or 30 minutes for open quarry).
frequency: Every blasting operation; written warning procedure maintained continuously
remarks: SHOT COUNTING IS MANDATORY (Cond. 33) — the 30-minute re-entry wait applies unless it is CERTAIN all shots have exploded. Read with CMR Reg 203 (inspection after shot-firing) and Reg 204 (misfires).

title: MISFIRE HANDLING — relieving hole distance, prohibitions on re-boring and tampering
detail: No re-boring, no tampering, no attempt to withdraw a charge before or after misfire, no deepening of sockets. Relieving hole must be not less than 30 cm from and PARALLEL to the misfired hole.
monitoringAuthority: Controller (on inspection); misfire register maintained at mine
remarks: ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS. No exceptions. Read with CMR Reg 204(10) misfire register obligation.

title: CHARGING AND STEMMING — wooden tamping rod only; no iron/steel tools; no smoking near charges
detail: Wooden tamping rod only (no iron or steel tools, scrapers or tamping rods with any metal part). No smoking or naked flame allowed in or near place where explosive charges are being prepared or kept. Precautions to limit stone projection before every blast. Wire ends stripped 5 cm, cleaned bright 2.5 cm and twisted for positive metal contact.
remarks: TAMPING ROD MUST BE MADE ENTIRELY OF WOOD — a rod with a metal ferrule or tip does not comply. Verify tamping rods at the magazine issue point. Rule 94(4) specifies the precise wire-joining procedure for electric initiation.

title: PRECAUTIONS AGAINST STRAY CURRENTS and regular testing of exploders
detail: Tests made for stray currents wherever electrically operated equipment is used in conductive ground or continuous metal objects are present. Exploders regularly tested and maintained in fit condition; must not be used above rated capacity. Electric circuit tested for continuity before firing; all non-essential persons withdrawn before continuity testing.
frequency: Stray current tests per blasting round (where applicable); exploders REGULARLY TESTED; continuity tested BEFORE EVERY FIRING
remarks: DIRECTLY RELEVANT IN AN OC MINE with HT lines, trailing cables and conveyor structures — conductive ground and continuous metal objects are the norm. Read with CER Reg 113 and CMR Reg 195(5) quarterly exploder testing.

title: EXPLOSIVES EXAMINED BEFORE USE and on receipt into magazine
detail: TWO EXAMINATION POINTS: (1) On RECEIPT into the magazine — every package examined for sound condition (SET-VII Cond. 22). (2) Before USE — visually examined for visible defects; defective explosives not used. Caked gunpowder not used. Frozen NG explosives only thawed under supervision of experienced persons.
frequency: On receipt of every package into the magazine; before every use
remarks: Record both examination points — receipt examination and pre-use examination. Defects found during use that were missed on receipt are harder to attribute.

title: SEGREGATION OF INCOMPATIBLE EXPLOSIVES in storage — separate compartments
detail: Detonators (Class 6 Div 3) stored in separate rooms or compartments. Gunpowder (Class 1) stored separately. Class 2 and Class 3 explosives, safety fuse (Class 6 Div 1) and detonating fuse (Class 6 Div 2) may be kept together provided no exposed iron/steel. Per SET-V Cond. 13: boosters, detonators and detonating fuses for SME operations must be kept in the licensed MAGAZINE — not at the SME support plant.
remarks: DETONATORS MUST ALWAYS BE SEPARATE. Boosters/detonating fuses for SME must be in the licensed magazine (SET-V Cond. 13) — not stored at the support plant.

title: MAGAZINE INTERIOR — no exposed iron/steel, grit-free, water trough at each entrance, no oily rags
detail: Interior of magazine, benches, shelves and fittings so constructed/lined as to prevent exposure of iron/steel or detachment of grit. Cemented trough at least 15 cm deep near EACH entrance, kept filled with clean water — no person enters without dipping overshoes or feet. Oiled cotton, oiled rags, oiled waste or spontaneously-igniting articles not taken into magazine. Before any repairs: all explosives removed and thorough washing done.
frequency: Continuous; trough kept filled with clean water at all times
remarks: THE WATER TROUGH is a specifically and frequently deficient requirement at inspections — one trough per entrance, maintained filled and clean, and use enforced on every entry. Before ANY repair work, all explosives removed and magazine thoroughly washed.

title: STACKING OF PACKAGES to permit inspection and reading of manufacture particulars
detail: Packages stacked to allow at least one person to move between stacks and check condition of ALL packages and read the manufacture particulars of each package. Red stacking-height line at 2.5 m on interior walls. Magazine interior volume ≥0.4 cubic metre per 100 kg of explosives.
regulationRef: Rule 79; SET-VII Cond. 19; SET-VIII Cond. 17; Schedule VII Spec. 2
remarks: Stacking must physically permit a person to WALK BETWEEN stacks and READ THE MANUFACTURE DATE on each package — this links directly to the Class 3 one-year age limit (Records S.No. 29) and FIFO rotation. Do not stack against walls — perimeter gangway required.

title: REMOVAL AND DESTRUCTION OF EMPTY PACKAGES + disposal of waste and split explosives
detail: Empty packages removed at the earliest and destroyed. Spillages/split explosives immediately collected and destroyed at safe place. Rule 42(1): Process buildings and machineries swept and cleaned at end of each shift; waste explosives collected, stored safely and safely disposed. Rule 42(2): Adequate facilities for safe destruction at a LICENSING-AUTHORITY-APPROVED place must be provided. Effluents discharged after proper treatment.
regulationRef: Rule 17; Rule 42(1)-(2); SET-VII Cond. 24; SET-V Cond. 11
frequency: Empty packages removed AT THE EARLIEST and destroyed; spillages collected and destroyed IMMEDIATELY; process building cleaning at END OF EACH SHIFT
monitoringAuthority: Controller (on inspection); destruction accounted in RE returns
remarks: NEW: Rule 42(1) end-of-shift cleaning and Rule 42(2) approved destruction place were missing from previous register. The destruction-approved place must be separately approved by the licensing authority — confirm this is in place. Destruction of explosives must be accounted for in quarterly return (Rule 24(3) covers explosives DESTROYED).

title: PROHIBITION on toxic, corrosive or flammable substances in explosives premises
detail: No toxic, corrosive, flammable or spontaneously-igniting substances allowed in or near premises used for manufacture, storage, sale, handling of explosives. Oiled cotton, oiled rags, oiled waste and spontaneously-igniting articles not taken into any building where explosives are kept.
remarks: Common inspection finding — diesel cans, oily rags, paint, grease and cleaning solvents near magazine premises. Enforce and document an exclusion list at the magazine and support plant.

title: AGE LIMIT TRACKING on Class 3 (nitro-compound) explosives — FIFO stock rotation in magazine
detail: Class 3 (nitro-compound) explosives tracked by batch number and date of manufacture in the magazine stock register. FIFO rotation maintained so stock approaching the 1-year limit is identified and used first. If stock is retained beyond 1 year, the sanction request (Notices S.No. 22) must be triggered.
formNo: Batch number and manufacture date tracked in RE-3/RE-4 stock register
frequency: Continuous — FIFO rotation maintained; stock approaching 1-year limit flagged
monitoringAuthority: Tracked continuously in magazine records; Controller on inspection
remarks: FIFO discipline is the operational control that prevents the Class 3 one-year age limit from being breached. If the RE-3/RE-4 does not record batch numbers and manufacture dates, FIFO tracking is impossible.

title: USE OF ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT in explosives premises requires prior written CHIEF CONTROLLER PERMIS...
detail: No electrical equipment may be used in places where explosives are being manufactured, handled or stored without prior written permission of the Chief Controller. Equipment type must be acceptable to the Chief Controller.
frequency: Prior written permission before installing or using any electrical equipment
mode: Written permission (retained on file with licence)
remarks: CRITICAL AND OFTEN OVERLOOKED. Even lighting, fans, CCTV cameras or a mobile charging point inside or at a magazine requires PRIOR WRITTEN PERMISSION OF THE CHIEF CONTROLLER, and the equipment type itself must be acceptable to him. Retain that permission permanently with the licence file.

title: PROHIBITION on falsification of records and alteration of licence documents
detail: No false or misleading information in any application or statement. No falsification, erasure or fraudulent alteration of any log, document or record required under these rules. No change or alteration of any licence, permit or other document issued under these rules.
remarks: Directly relevant to stock book discipline — erasures or overwriting in a page-numbered RE stock book can be construed as falsification. Use single-line strike-through with initials and date for corrections.

title: FREE ACCESS to licensed premises for inspecting and sampling officers
detail: Free access and full facilities given to inspecting/sampling officers at all times. Inspection findings from Controller/DM must be tracked to closure. Rule 136: inspection report endorsed to licensing authority — can lead to suspension/revocation under Rule 118.
regulationRef: Rule 128; SET-VII Cond. 12, 36; SET-V Cond. 17; LE-7 Cond. 15
frequency: At all times / all reasonable times
monitoringAuthority: Inspecting or Sampling Officer / Controller / District Magistrate
remarks: Rule 128(4): Executive Magistrates/Police Officers must carry out inspections of magazines ONCE IN SIX MONTHS — cooperate fully and retain inspection reports. Rule 136: every inspection observation creates a compliance obligation — track to documented closure.

title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURE — personnel to be conversant; written procedure maintained
detail: Licensee and employees must be conversant with emergency procedures specific to each licensed premises (magazine, SME plant, road van). Written emergency procedure maintained with dated training/briefing records for all employees.
regulationRef: SET-VII Cond. 35; SET-V Cond. 16; LE-7 Cond. 14
frequency: Continuous — training and awareness maintained; annual emergency plan test (see Records S.No. 7 — SMP)
remarks: Maintain a documented emergency procedure specific to explosives premises — separate from the general mine ERP under CMR Reg 252.

title: RESPONSIBILITY OF PERSON IN CHARGE of blasting operations — dual statutory liability
detail: Licensee/shot-firer personally responsible for all precautions against fire, accident, loss and pilferage of explosives at the blasting site. Blasting in mines governed by Mines Act 1952 and CMR 2017 — but shot-firer remains PERSONALLY LIABLE under the Explosives Act 1884 and ER 2008 simultaneously.
signerRole: Licensee + Shot-firer (personally liable under both statutes)
remarks: DUAL STATUTORY LIABILITY: Rule 97 confirms mine blasting is governed by CMR, BUT the shot-firer remains liable under Explosives Act as well. Rule 98 (shot-firer's certificate from Controller) applies to areas OTHER THAN mines — the CMR-appointed shot-firer applies in the mine.

title: Explosive Loading Sheet — quantity charged per hole with hole depth
detail: Quantity of explosive charged and hole depth logged per hole, per blast, by shot-firer.
remarks: Cross-statutory record — CMR obligation that reconciles with ER 2008 magazine RE-5 issue records.

title: Daily consumption record of explosives in the mine (Form RE-5 / RE-13)
detail: Daily consumption of explosives at mine recorded in FORM RE-5 (account of explosives used by licensee — issued to/returned by shot-firer) and reconciled against magazine issue register. NOTE on RE-13: the original register cited FORM RE-13 — this form does not appear in the Explosives Rules 2008 Part 5 Schedule V as notified. Verify with PESO whether RE-13 has been prescribed by a subsequent notification or is a site-specific form.
formNo: FORM RE-5 (explosives used/returned); NOTE: FORM RE-13 not found in ER 2008 — verify with PESO
remarks: CORRECTION/VERIFICATION NEEDED: Original register cited FORM RE-13. RE-13 is not prescribed in ER 2008 Part 5 Schedule V as extracted from the gazette. This may be a site-specific internal form or a form prescribed under a subsequent PESO notification — verify and update citation.

title: Ammonium Nitrate stock account — receipt, conversion and consumption
detail: Daily AN receipt, conversion (to SME/ANFO) and consumption account kept at licensed premises; produced to licensing authority on demand.
remarks: AN Rules 2012 not uploaded — verify exact rule number and prescribed form before relying. Distinct from the ER 2008 RE-2 manufacturing record.

title: Daily magazine stock update — issues and returns (Form RE-3)
detail: Daily basis magazine stock update — explosives issued and returned recorded in FORM RE-3 (account of receipt of explosives).
remarks: Distinct daily entry alongside the RE-4 balance register. RE-3 captures receipts; RE-5 captures issue/consumption by shot-firer.

title: Daily issue, consumption and return of explosives in name of shot-firer (Form RE-5)
detail: Daily record of explosives issued to, consumed by, and returned by each named shot-firer in FORM RE-5.
remarks: Reconciles with CMR Reg 206(b) shot-firer end-of-shift record. The shot-firer's name and permit number must be recorded per issue (Form RE-5 header).

title: Transit pass — Blasting Officer to Magazine In-charge for blasting accessories
detail: Daily transit pass issued by Blasting Officer to Magazine In-charge for blasting accessories issued to shot-firer; returned after blasting.
remarks: Distinct from the magazine issue register — this is the accessories transit slip between Blasting Officer and Magazine In-charge.

title: Magazine licence (LE-3) and SME/ANFO licence (LE-1) — validity tracking
detail: Magazine possession licence in Form LE-3; SME/ANFO manufacturing licence in Form LE-1 — both must be renewed before expiry. Track expiry dates on a live register. CONFIRMED: current LE-3 valid till 31.03.2030. Rule 112 amended 2025: licence period now up to 10 financial years.
frequency: As per validity; renewal window — apply before expiry date; 3-month cut-off after expiry
monitoringAuthority: Licensing Authority (Chief Controller/Controller for LE-1; Controller for LE-3 possession)
remarks: Track expiry dates on a live register. Post-2025 amendment, licence period up to 10 years — but renewal application must still reach the authority before expiry. 3-month outer limit is absolute.

title: Explosive van licence (LE-7) — validity tracking
detail: Licence to transport explosives by road van in Form LE-7; renewed before expiry.
frequency: As per validity; renew before expiry
remarks: Track expiry alongside LE-3 and LE-1. LE-7 is issued by Controller of Explosives.

title: MAXIMUM CONSIGNMENT LIMIT for explosives transported by road van
detail: Quantity transported by road van shall not exceed 10 tonnes or the maximum carrying capacity permitted by road transport authority — whichever is less. For Class 2 explosives: 15 tonnes or van capacity, whichever is less.
frequency: Applies to every consignment moved by road van
remarks: Hard transport quantity cap. Verify current indent/consignment sizes against this limit.

title: PROHIBITION on converting explosives between classes or cutting Class 2/3 cartridges
detail: An explosive of one description/class shall not be converted into an explosive of another description. Class 2 or Class 3 explosives must be used in their original cartridge packing — cartridges must not be cut to make cartridges of different sizes.
frequency: Continuous — applies to every charge preparation
remarks: Direct field-practice prohibition. Cutting cartridges to fit smaller diameter holes is an explicit contravention — even if done informally. Verify tamping and loading practice at face.

title: RECORD OF POST-SHOT-FIRING INSPECTION in bound paged book (CMR Reg 203)
detail: After each shot-firing, the shot-firer must examine the area for safety before allowing re-entry; examination particulars recorded in a bound paged book, signed and dated.
monitoringAuthority: Maintained at mine; produced to DGMS Inspector / Controller on demand
remarks: Distinct from the Explosive Loading Sheet (quantity/hole-depth) — this is the POST-blast safety inspection record. Cross-statutory obligation under CMR.

title: SME MANUFACTURE — daily operating restrictions and end-of-day system cleaning
detail: SME: manufactured strictly per safe working procedures; only between SUNRISE AND SUNSET; at end of loading operations — entire mixing/delivery system including hose pipes emptied (compressed air flush + water) and cleaned; vehicle parked at support plant. Spillages: collected and destroyed at safe place, effluents treated before discharge. ANFO: containers and mixers thoroughly cleaned with detergent and water after each use.
frequency: Daily operating conditions; SUNRISE TO SUNSET ONLY; end-of-day system cleaning
monitoringAuthority: Compliance at site (verified on inspection by Controller/DGMS)
remarks: Daily operational compliance. Manufacture only between sunrise and sunset is an absolute rule — no exceptions for 'urgent orders'. End-of-day cleaning is a safety imperative (AN residue in lines is a significant explosion risk).

title: Explosives licence copy at mine office
detail: A copy of the licence for possession, use, sale, transport or manufacture of explosives shall be kept at the mine office.

title: Magazine register — explosives issued to each competent person + returned
detail:
Reg 185(3): No explosive shall be issued from the magazine or explosive store except on written requisition signed by the shot-firer. The written requisition shall be preserved.
Reg 185(4): A register in a bound paged book shall be maintained showing the quantity of explosives issued to each competent person and the quantity returned.
remarks: Written requisition signed by shot-firer to be preserved.

title: Shot-firing apparatus test record
detail: Every shot-firing apparatus shall be tested at intervals not exceeding three months and after every failure, and the results recorded in a bound paged book.

title: Inspection record after shot-firing
detail: After every shot-firing, the shot-firer shall inspect the place and shall not declare it safe until satisfied that no danger exists. The inspection shall be recorded in a bound paged book.

title: Misfire report register
detail:
Reg 204(10)(b): Every misfire, whether suspected or confirmed, shall be reported by the shot-firer to the competent person and the overman.
Reg 204(10)(c): The shot-firer shall record every misfire and the action taken in a bound paged book.

title: Shot-firer's end-of-shift record
detail: At the end of every shift, every shot-firer shall record in a bound paged book: the quantity of explosive taken from the magazine, the quantity used, the quantity returned to the magazine, the places where shots were fired, the number of shots fired and any misfires.

title: Vibration Report — ground vibration record for each blast
detail: Daily ground vibration record (seismograph) for every blast, per condition of the site-specific DGMS blasting permission.
signerRole: Blasting Officer / Shot-firer; countersigned by Manager
remarks: Not a CMR requirement — CMR is silent on vibration. This is a condition of your specific DGMS blasting permission, so track it exactly as that permission requires and re-verify if the permission is renewed or revised.

title: SHOT-FIRING — protection of apparatus and prohibition on using lighting/power circuits
detail:
Reg 113(1): WHEN SHOT-FIRING IS IN PROGRESS, ADEQUATE PRECAUTIONS SHALL BE TAKEN TO PROTECT APPARATUS AND CONDUCTORS, OTHER THAN THOSE USED FOR SHOT-FIRING, FROM INJURY.
Reg 113(2): CURRENT FROM LIGHTING OR POWER CIRCUITS SHALL NOT BE USED FOR FIRING SHOTS.
Reg 113(3): THE CONSTRUCTION OF SHOT FIRING CABLES SHALL CONFORM TO RELEVANT STANDARDS and ADEQUATE PRECAUTIONS SHALL BE TAKEN TO PREVENT SUCH CABLE TOUCHING OTHER CABLES AND APPARATUS.
remarks: Reg 113(2) is an ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION — lighting or power circuit current must never be used to fire shots. Read with CMR Reg 195 (electric shot-firing) and the quarterly shot-firing apparatus test under CMR Reg 195(5).

title: TRANSPORTING AND STORING OF MATERIAL NEAR ELECTRIC LINES
detail:
Reg 66(1): NO RODS, PIPES OR SIMILAR MATERIALS SHALL BE TAKEN BELOW, OR IN THE VICINITY OF, ANY BARE OVERHEAD CONDUCTORS OR LINES. PROVISO: if these materials contravene Reg 62 and 63, such materials shall be TRANSPORTED UNDER THE DIRECT SUPERVISION OF A DESIGNATED PERSON.
Reg 66(2): NO RODS, PIPES OR OTHER SIMILAR MATERIALS SHALL BE BROUGHT WITHIN THE FLASH OVER DISTANCE OF BARE LIVE CONDUCTORS OR OVERHEAD LINES.
Reg 66(3): NO MATERIAL OR EARTH WORK OR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE SHALL BE DUMPED OR STORED, NO TREES GROWN, BELOW OR IN THE VICINITY OF BARE OVERHEAD CONDUCTORS OR LINES in contravention of Reg 62 and 63.
Reg 66(4): NO FLAMMABLE MATERIAL SHALL BE STORED UNDER THE ELECTRIC LINE.
Reg 66(5): NO FIRE SHALL BE ALLOWED BELOW OVERHEAD LINES AND ABOVE THE DEMARCATED UNDERGROUND CABLES.
remarks: CRITICAL FOR OC OPERATIONS. Reg 66(3) prohibits DUMPING OR STORING MATERIAL OR EARTH WORK below or near bare overhead lines — directly restricts where OB dumps, topsoil stacks and material stockpiles may be sited. Reg 66(4) prohibits FLAMMABLE MATERIAL STORAGE under a line (diesel, oil, explosives-related stores). Reg 66(5) prohibits fires below lines and above demarcated underground cables.

title: PROTECTION AGAINST LIGHTNING for overhead lines, substations and generating stations
detail:
Reg 77(1): THE OWNER OF EVERY OVERHEAD LINE, SUBSTATION OR GENERATING STATION WHICH IS EXPOSED TO LIGHTNING SHALL ADOPT MEANS as per relevant standards FOR DIVERTING ELECTRICAL SURGES TO THE EARTH DUE TO LIGHTNING which may result into injuries.
Reg 77(2): THE EARTHING LEAD FOR ANY LIGHTNING ARRESTER SHALL BE AS SHORT AS POSSIBLE AND SHALL NOT PASS THROUGH ANY IRON OR STEEL PIPE, BUT SHALL BE TAKEN AS DIRECTLY AS POSSIBLE FROM THE LIGHTNING ARRESTER WITHOUT TOUCHING ANY METAL PART TO A SEPARATE VERTICAL EARTH ELECTRODE OR JUNCTION OF THE EARTH MAT already provided for the substation of voltage exceeding 650 V, subject to the avoidance of bends wherever practicable. PROVISO: A VERTICAL EARTH ELECTRODE SHALL BE CONNECTED TO THE JUNCTION OF THE EARTH MAT.
remarks: Very specific installation requirements for the lightning arrester earthing lead — as short as possible, NOT through iron or steel pipe, no contact with metal parts, minimum bends. Read alongside the PESO lightning conductor annual test requirement for the magazine and SME plant under Explosives Rules 2008.

title: Yellow shading = CORRECTED or CLARIFIED item
detail: Yellow shading = CORRECTED or CLARIFIED item

title: No shading = confirmed/carried forward from previous version
detail: No shading = confirmed/carried forward from previous version

title: Prior notice before bringing into use any NEW electrical installation in a mine
detail:
Reg 98(2): The persons specified in regulation 97 (owner, agent, manager, engineer, installation manager) shall give to the Electrical Inspector of mines NOT LESS THAN SEVEN DAYS notice in writing of the intention to bring into use any new installation in a mine, giving details of apparatus installed and its location.

FIRST PROVISO: In case of any ADDITIONS OR ALTERATIONS to an existing installation of voltage NOT EXCEEDING 650 V, IMMEDIATE notice in writing shall be sent to the Electrical Inspector of mines BEFORE such additions or alterations are brought into use.

SECOND PROVISO: This regulation shall not apply to telecommunication or signalling apparatus.

THIRD PROVISO: In case of EMERGENCY which may lead to loss of life or machinery and is detrimental to safety of mine, intimation shall be given WITHIN TWENTY FOUR HOURS to the Electrical Inspector of mines giving the healthiness of the apparatus along with SELF-CERTIFICATION REPORT of such additions or alterations undertaken.
frequency: ≥7 days (new installation); IMMEDIATE before use (additions/alterations ≤650 V); within 24 hrs (emergency, with self-certification report)
remarks: THREE DISTINCT TRIGGERS in one regulation — new installation, additions/alterations ≤650V, and emergency. Each has a different timeline and the emergency route additionally requires a self-certification report. Telecom/signalling apparatus exempt.

title: Written permission before BLASTING within 300 m of substation or lines exceeding 650 V
detail: No blasting for any purpose shall be done within THREE HUNDRED METRE from the boundary of a substation or from the electric supply lines of voltage exceeding 650 V or tower structure thereof, without the WRITTEN PERMISSION of the owner of such substation or electric supply lines or tower structures; and IN CASE OF MINING LEASE HOLD AREA, WITHOUT THE WRITTEN PERMISSION OF THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES.
frequency: Before every blasting activity within 300 m
monitoringAuthority: Owner of substation/line/tower + ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES (mandatory for mining lease hold area)
remarks: CRITICAL for OC blasting operations. Note the dual permission requirement — owner of the asset AND Electrical Inspector of Mines, the latter being specific to mining lease hold areas.

title: Written permission before CUTTING OF SOIL within 10 m of tower structure of 110 kV and above
detail: No cutting of soil within TEN METRE from the tower structure of 110 kV AND ABOVE voltage level shall be permitted without the WRITTEN PERMISSION OF THE OWNER OF TOWER STRUCTURE.
frequency: Before any soil cutting within 10 m of a 110 kV+ tower
remarks: CRITICAL AND FREQUENTLY MISSED. In OC mining, soil cutting is a daily activity — bench cutting, OB removal, haul road widening, drain construction, dozing. If a 110 kV or above tower stands within or near the pit, every excavation within 10 m of its foundation needs prior written permission. Undermining a tower leg risks collapse, fatalities and prosecution. Establish a surveyed 10 m no-cut buffer around every such tower and mark it on the working plan.

title: Prohibition on constructing brick kiln or other POLLUTING UNITS within 500 m of installations or ...
detail: No person shall construct brick kiln or OTHER POLLUTING UNITS near the installations or transmission lines of 220 kV AND ABOVE within a distance of FIVE HUNDRED METRE.
frequency: Before construction / siting of any polluting unit
monitoringAuthority: Compliance obligation (no permission route provided) — verified by Electrical Inspector
remarks: ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION — no permission mechanism exists, unlike Reg 67(2) and 67(3). An SME/ANFO bulk explosives plant, crusher, or similar unit is arguably a polluting unit; verify the 500 m distance from any 220 kV+ line before siting or expanding such facilities.

title: Notice of erection or alteration of buildings, structures, flood banks and elevation of roads nea...
detail:
Reg 65(1): If at any time subsequent to the erection of an overhead line or underground cable, any person proposes to erect a new building or structure or flood bank, or to raise any road level, or to carry out ANY OTHER TYPE OF WORK whether permanent or temporary, or to make in or upon any building, structure, flood bank or road any permanent or temporary addition or alteration, such person AND THE CONTRACTOR whom he employs shall give INTIMATION IN WRITING of his intention to do so, to the supplier or owner AND TO THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR, and shall furnish therewith A SCALE DRAWING showing the proposed building, structure, flood bank, road or addition or alteration AND SCAFFOLDING thereof required during construction.
Reg 65(2): On receipt, the supplier/owner shall examine technical feasibility, right of way, and cost liability and issue notice within 30 days with cost estimate; the person shall deposit within 30 days of receipt.
Reg 65(6): NO WORK shall commence or continue until the Electrical Inspector CERTIFIES that regulations 60, 62, 63, 66 and 79 have not been contravened either during or after construction.
frequency: Before commencement of any such erection/alteration work; cost deposit within 30 days of notice
monitoringAuthority: Supplier or owner of the line + ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR
remarks: Note: "any other type of work" is deliberately broad and covers raising haul road levels and building embankments/flood banks — common OC activities. Both the mine AND the contractor carry the obligation. Work cannot start until the Electrical Inspector certifies clearance compliance.

title: Approval in writing of Electrical Inspector of Mines before connecting installations of 650 V and...
detail:
In case of installations of MINES and oil-fields, the electrical installations of voltage 650 V AND ABOVE shall NOT be connected to supply, unless and until such installation work INCLUDING ALTERATIONS OR ADDITIONS OR RECOMMENCEMENT AFTER SHUTDOWN FOR SIX MONTHS are APPROVED IN WRITING by the ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES.

PROVISO: The electrical installations of voltage BELOW 650 V in mines and oil-fields are to be SELF-CERTIFIED by the owner or agent or manager of the mine before commencement of supply or recommencement after shutdown for six months or more, in the manner specified in sub-regulation (1) [i.e. report submitted to Electrical Inspector in Schedule II forms].
formNo: Schedule II — Form I / II / III / IV (for the below-650 V self-certification route)
frequency: Before connection; before recommencement after 6-month shutdown; on every alteration or addition
mode: Written approval (≥650 V) / Self-certification report (<650 V)
remarks: Two-track system: ≥650 V requires WRITTEN APPROVAL from EIM; <650 V permits SELF-CERTIFICATION but the report must still reach the Electrical Inspector. Deemed received if not acknowledged within 3 working days.

title: Reporting failure of 10 MVA or above transformers in mines
detail:
Reg 48(8): Failures of any 220 kV and above voltage level transformer, reactor and transmission line towers shall be reported by the owner of electrical installation, WITHIN FORTY EIGHT HOURS of the occurrence of the failure, to the Authority, and the reasons for failure and measures to be taken to avoid recurrence shall be sent to the Authority WITHIN ONE MONTH of the occurrence in the forms provided in Schedule VII.

PROVISO: In case of MINES and oil-fields, the failure of 10 MVA OR ABOVE transformers shall be reported to the ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES.
frequency: Within 48 hours of failure; detailed reasons and preventive measures within 1 month
remarks: The mines proviso LOWERS the threshold from 220 kV to 10 MVA and REDIRECTS the report from the Authority to the Electrical Inspector of Mines. Both the 48-hour intimation and the 1-month detailed report are required.

title: Report of disconnection / reconnection of supply due to inflammable gas
detail: Any such disconnection or reconnection of the supply [under Reg 112(6) and 112(7), i.e. where inflammable gas exceeds 1.25% or open sparking occurs] shall be NOTED IN THE LOG SHEET in hard copy AND electronic form which shall be maintained in the form set out in SCHEDULE XI, and SHALL BE REPORTED TO THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES.
remarks: Reg 112 is largely gassy-seam/UG focused, but sub-reg (10) permits the Inspector to extend it to any mine where inflammable gas occurs or is likely.

title: Permission for haulage by electric locomotives or storage battery locomotives
detail: Haulage by electric locomotives on the overhead trolley-wire system at voltage NOT EXCEEDING 650 V, and haulage by storage battery locomotives, may be used WITH THE PRIOR PERMISSION IN WRITING of the ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES, and subject to such conditions as he may impose in the interests of safety.
remarks: Applicable only if locomotive haulage is used; not typical for truck-shovel OC operations but included for completeness.

title: Notice of accident (loss of life / serious bodily injury) or dangerous occurrence
detail:
OSH Rule 7(1): Where an accident occurs resulting in death — inform ICF forthwith in FORM-XI and inform electronically and by telephone to CICF, ICF, DM/SDO and the police station and family members or kin of the victim.
OSH Rule 7(2): Where accident results in bodily injury preventing work ≥48 hours — inform in FORM-XI within 12 hours after completion of 48 hours.
OSH Rule 7(3): Dangerous occurrence whether causing injury or not — within 12 hours send intimation to ICF and DM/SDO.
Proviso: if death occurs after notice already sent — forthwith send further notice by telephone and electronically, confirmed in writing within 12 hours.

CMR Reg 8(1): Forthwith inform RI by telephone/fax/email/special messenger; within 24 hours give formal notice to DM, CI, RI and Competent Authority for compensation. List of dangerous occurrences in Reg 8(1)(b)(i)-(xix) includes: explosion, spontaneous heating, fire, fall of HEMM from height, bursting of pressurised equipment, influx of gases, irruption of water, premature collapse, accident due to explosives, breakage of rope/chain/headgear, failure of dump or side in OC working, failure of structure/installation, electrical flash-over causing burn.

CMR Reg 8(2): Exhibit copy on special notice board at mine office ≥14 days.
formNo: FORM XI (OSH); Form as specified by CI (CMR)
frequency: Forthwith (death — OSH/CMR); within 12 hrs (injury >48hr / DO — OSH); within 24 hrs (CMR formal)
monitoringAuthority: ICF + DM/SDO + Police + Family (OSH); DM + CI + RI + Comp Authority (CMR)
remarks: CMR Reg 8(1)(b)(xvii): failure of dump or side in OC working is a dangerous occurrence — critical for OC mines.

title: Notice of electrical accident
detail: When an accident causing loss of life, serious bodily injury or burn injury occurs in or about a mine in connection with the generation, storage, transformation, transmission, supply or use of electrical energy, the owner, agent or manager shall also forthwith inform the Inspector of Mines (Electrical) by telephone, fax, e-mail or by special messenger. Proviso: if sent by email, shall be immediately followed by fax or letter.
remarks: Additional to S.No. 10 — applies when accident is connected with electrical energy.

title: ANNUAL RETURN OF ELECTRICAL APPARATUS FOR MINES
detail:
Reg 98(1): ON OR BEFORE THE FIRST DAY OF FEBRUARY IN EVERY YEAR, in respect of every mine, RETURNS giving the SIZE AND TYPE OF APPARATUS, together with such particulars in regard to circumstances of its use as may be required, shall be sent to the ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES by the persons specified in regulation 97 in the Form provided in SCHEDULE IX.

SCHEDULE IX requires:
PART A — Year ending; Name of Mine; State; Situation of Mine; District; Postal address; Name and address of owner; Name of agent; Name of manager; Name of engineer; NAME OF ELECTRICAL SUPERVISOR.
PART B — (1) System of supply (DC or AC), voltage of supply, periodicity if AC, source of supply; (2) Voltage at which electricity is used for Lighting and for Power; (3) Particulars of motors etc. — (a) ON SURFACE: type of motor (HP/KW)/apparatus and voltage, type of control gear, location, purpose for which used; (b) IN MINE: same plus ventilation and percentage of inflammable gas or vapour; (c) LIGHTING: type of light fitting, wattage, location, percentage of inflammable gas or vapour.

Schedule IX header states: "This form must be correctly filled up by the owner, agent, manager or engineer and sent to the Electrical Inspector of mines not later than the first day of February every year."
formNo: SCHEDULE IX (Form of Annual Return for Mines)
frequency: ON OR BEFORE 1st FEBRUARY every year
remarks: SAME DUE DATE as the CMR 2017 Reg 4(1) annual return (1st February) — file both together. Requires a complete inventory of every motor and apparatus on surface with rating, control gear, location and purpose, so maintain a live apparatus register through the year rather than compiling in January.

title: Energy data return — electrical energy, diesel and specific energy consumption for the month
detail: Every owner, agent or manager of a colliery and every person engaged in the business of production, supply and distribution of, or trade and commerce in coal, on being directed to do so by the Coal Controller shall submit such returns and other information including information regarding production of dispatch of coal, washery products from his mines, washery and process products, working methods and conditions in his mine or mines, within such time, as may be specified in the direction.
act: Colliery Control Rules, 2004 [as amended by G.S.R. 546(E) dated 09.08.2021]
frequency: Monthly — by the 10th of the succeeding month
monitoringAuthority: Coal Controller's Organisation (CCO), Ministry of Coal

title: Record (register) of DESIGNATED PERSONS authorised to work on electrical lines and apparatus
detail:
Reg 3(1): The owner or agent or manager of a mine shall DESIGNATE PERSONS for the purpose to operate and carry out the work on electrical lines and apparatus.
Reg 3(2): Shall MAINTAIN A RECORD, in paper or electronic form, wherein the NAMES of the designated persons AND THE PURPOSE for which they are designated shall be entered.
Reg 3(3): No person shall be designated unless (i) he possesses a CERTIFICATE OF COMPETENCY or ELECTRICAL WORK PERMIT issued by the Appropriate Government; and (ii) his name is entered in the register.
Reg 4(1): The record shall be PRODUCED BEFORE THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR as and when required.
Reg 4(2): If on inspection the Electrical Inspector finds a designated person does not comply with Reg 3(3), he shall RECOMMEND THE REMOVAL of the name from the record.
frequency: Maintained continuously; updated on every designation/removal; produced on demand
remarks: Only designated persons whose names appear in this register and who hold a valid certificate of competency or work permit may work on electrical lines and apparatus. Verify certificate validity before entry.

title: Designation and records of ELECTRICAL SAFETY OFFICER (mines with >2000 kW connected load)
detail:
Reg 5(3): For MINES with MORE THAN 2000 kW CONNECTED LOAD, the owner of the installation or the management of the mines shall DESIGNATE AN ELECTRICAL SAFETY OFFICER for ensuring compliance of the safety provisions.
Reg 5(2) + proviso: The ESO shall possess a DEGREE in Electrical Engineering with at least FIVE years experience, or a DIPLOMA in Electrical Engineering with at least TEN years experience, in operation and maintenance of electrical installations; and the ESO DESIGNATED FOR MINES shall possess that qualification with AT LEAST FIVE YEARS OF EXPERIENCE RELEVANT TO MINES.
Reg 5(3) PROVISO: The Electrical Safety Officer SHALL CARRY OUT RECOMMENDED PERIODIC TESTS as per relevant standards, and INSPECT SUCH INSTALLATIONS AT INTERVALS NOT EXCEEDING ONE YEAR, and KEEP A RECORD thereof in FORM I or II or III or IV of SCHEDULE II; TEST REPORTS; and A REGISTER OF RECOMMENDATIONS in regard with safety DULY ACKNOWLEDGED BY THE OWNER; and COMPLIANCES MADE THEREAFTER; and such records shall be MADE AVAILABLE TO THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR as and when required.
formNo: Schedule II — Form I / II / III / IV
frequency: ESO designation: on applicability; INSPECTION AT INTERVALS NOT EXCEEDING ONE YEAR; records continuous
remarks: FOUR SEPARATE RECORDS required by the proviso: (a) inspection record in Schedule II forms, (b) test reports, (c) a register of safety recommendations DULY ACKNOWLEDGED BY THE OWNER, and (d) record of compliances made thereafter. The owner acknowledgement on the recommendations register is an easily-missed requirement.

title: Appointment of ELECTRICAL SUPERVISOR(S) and ELECTRICIANS in writing
detail:
Reg 117(1): One or more ELECTRICAL SUPERVISORS shall be APPOINTED IN WRITING by the owner, agent or manager of a mine to supervise the installation, and such number of supervisors shall be on duty as per guidelines issued by DGMS from time to time under intimation in writing to the Authority or as directed by the Electrical Inspector of mines.
Reg 117(2): The electrical supervisor shall hold a VALID ELECTRICAL SUPERVISORS CERTIFICATE OF COMPETENCY COVERING MINING INSTALLATIONS issued by the Appropriate Government.
Reg 117(3): Adequate number of ELECTRICIANS as per DGMS guidelines shall be APPOINTED IN WRITING by owner, agent or manager.
Reg 117(4): The Electrician shall hold a licence under Reg 31(1).
Reg 117(5): For SMALL OPEN CAST MINES receiving supply at voltage not more than 650 V and not having portable or transportable apparatus, electrical supervisor and electrician may be appointed for MORE THAN ONE MINE with the APPROVAL OF THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES.
Reg 117(6): Every person appointed to operate, supervise, examine or adjust any apparatus shall be COMPETENT as directed by the Engineer.
Reg 117(8): In the ABSENCE of any electrical supervisor, the owner, agent or manager SHALL APPOINT IN WRITING A SUBSTITUTE ELECTRICAL SUPERVISOR.
frequency: On appointment; substitute appointed on every absence; ongoing
monitoringAuthority: Electrical Inspector of Mines (guidelines/approval); records at mine
remarks: Certificate must specifically COVER MINING INSTALLATIONS — a general Electrical Supervisor certificate is insufficient. Substitute appointment during absence must also be in writing.

title: ELECTRICAL SUPERVISORS DAILY LOG SHEET / LOG BOOK
detail:
Reg 117(9): The electrical supervisor or the substitute electrical supervisor appointed under sub-regulation (8) shall be PERSONALLY RESPONSIBLE for the MAINTENANCE AT THE MINE of a LOG-BOOK MADE UP OF THE DAILY LOG SHEETS prepared in the form set out in SCHEDULE XI, and the RESULTS OF ALL TESTS carried out in accordance with sub-regulation (7) shall be RECORDED in the log-sheets prepared in the form set out in Schedule XI.

SCHEDULE XI (Log Sheet for Mines) requires daily reporting on:
(1) Name of Electrical Supervisor.
(2) Report as to — (a) CONDITION OF THE INSULATION of the system; (b) SPECIFIED DEFECTS OF INSULATION (particulars of each failure of apparatus to be given); (c) ACCIDENTS OR DANGEROUS OCCURRENCE (including any cases of ELECTRIC SHOCK and any cases of OPEN SPARKING in apparatus where Reg 112 applies); (d) DISCONNECTION AND RECONNECTION of supply as required by Reg 112(9); (e) EXAMINATION OF EARTH FAULT DETECTORS OR RECORDERS as provided by Reg 102(3); (f) EXAMINATIONS OF APPARATUS as provided by Reg 117.
(3) (i) ROUTINE EXAMINATIONS as required by Reg 117(9); (ii) SPECIAL EXAMINATIONS as required by Reg 117(9) — stating which apparatus has been examined or tested and its result.
SIGNED BY: Electrical Supervisor; Examined by ENGINEER; and MANAGER.
NOTE on the form: "This log sheet should be filled in as completely as possible. If, for instance, there are no defects of insulation to report, the word none should be written in the vacant space."
formNo: SCHEDULE XI (Log Sheet for Mines and Oil-fields)
signerRole: Electrical Supervisor (signed); countersigned by ENGINEER and MANAGER
mode: Physical (log book of daily log sheets) + Electronic
remarks: THREE SIGNATURES required on the log sheet — Electrical Supervisor, Engineer, and Manager. The form note explicitly requires "none" to be written where there is nothing to report, so blank fields are a non-compliance.

title: Thorough examination and testing of all apparatus by Electrical Supervisor / Electrician
detail:
Reg 117(7): The ELECTRICAL SUPERVISOR shall be RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PROPER PERFORMANCE of the following duties, BY HIMSELF OR BY AN ELECTRICIAN appointed under sub-regulation (1) —
(i) THOROUGH EXAMINATION OF ALL APPARATUS, INCLUDING THE TESTING OF EARTH CONDUCTORS AND METALLIC COVERINGS FOR CONTINUITY, AS OFTEN AS MAY BE NECESSARY TO PREVENT DANGER; and
(ii) EXAMINATION AND TESTING OF ALL NEW APPARATUS, AND OF ALL APPARATUS RE-ERECTED IN THE MINE, BEFORE IT IS PUT INTO SERVICE IN A NEW POSITION.

Results of all such tests SHALL BE RECORDED in the Schedule XI log sheets (Reg 117(9)).
formNo: Recorded in Schedule XI log sheets
frequency: As often as necessary to prevent danger; and before every new or re-erected apparatus is put into service
remarks: Note the RE-ERECTION trigger: in OC mines, shifting a substation, switchgear, or feeder to a new bench position counts as re-erection and requires fresh examination and testing BEFORE it is energised in the new position. Frequency of routine examination is not fixed — it is "as often as necessary to prevent danger", so the mine must define and justify its own interval.

title: DAILY RECORD OF OPERATION OF SWITCHGEAR AND PROTECTIVE RELAYS
detail: Reg 103(2): The OPERATION OF THE SWITCHGEAR AND THE RELAYS SHALL BE RECORDED DAILY at the generating station, substation or switch station in A REGISTER KEPT FOR THE PURPOSE AND IN ELECTRONIC FORM ALSO.
remarks: The regulation requires the record in BOTH a physical register AND electronic form — "and in electronic form also" is mandatory, not optional.

title: ANNUAL CALIBRATION AND TESTING OF SWITCHGEAR AND PROTECTIVE SYSTEM
detail:
Reg 103(3): The EFFECTIVENESS OF SWITCHGEAR AND PROTECTIVE SYSTEM SHALL ALWAYS BE KEPT IN WORKING ORDER and SHALL BE CHECKED BY CALIBRATING AND TESTING AT LEAST ONCE IN A YEAR, and the RESULT THEREOF SHALL BE RECORDED IN A SEPARATE REGISTER kept for the purpose AND IN ELECTRONIC FORM.

PROVISO: Wherever NUMERICAL RELAYS are being used, they shall be checked by testing procedure as per GUIDELINES OF THE ORIGINAL EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURER or the relevant standards, and PERIODICITY OF SUCH CHECKING SHALL BE AT LEAST ONCE IN A YEAR.
frequency: AT LEAST ONCE IN A YEAR
remarks: Must be kept in a SEPARATE register from the Reg 103(2) daily operation register. Numerical relays follow OEM testing procedure but the same annual minimum periodicity.

title: EARTH FAULT CURRENT LIMITS and restricted neutral system with neutral-ground monitoring
detail:
Reg 103(1): In the interest of safety, the EARTH FAULT CURRENT shall NOT be more than 750 MILLIAMPERE in installations of voltage exceeding 250 V and up to 1100 V FOR BELOW GROUND MINES and oil-fields, and 50 AMPERE in installations of voltage exceeding 1100 V and up to 11 kV IN OPEN CAST MINES; and the magnitude of the earth fault current shall be LIMITED TO THESE SPECIFIED VALUES by employing a SUITABLY DESIGNED RESTRICTED NEUTRAL SYSTEM of power supply INCLUDING NEUTRAL-GROUND MONITORING PROTECTION SYSTEM.

FIRST PROVISO: All electrical installations, IN OR AFTER NOTIFICATION OF THESE REGULATIONS, of voltage exceeding 1100 V and up to 11 kV for below ground mines, OPEN CAST MINES and oil mines, the magnitude of the earth fault current SHALL BE LIMITED UP TO 10 A by employing suitably designed restricted neutral system including neutral-ground monitoring protection system.

SECOND PROVISO: The SETTINGS OF PROTECTIVE RELAYS thereof shall be SET BETWEEN 200 TO 400 MILLIAMPERE for individual apparatus of voltage up to 1100 V with SUITABLE TIME DELAY PROTECTION.
frequency: Design/commissioning requirement; verified at annual testing under Reg 103(3)
remarks: CRITICAL DESIGN LIMIT WITH A CHANGED THRESHOLD. Older OC installations were designed to 50 A; every installation commissioned on or after the notification of CER 2023 must be limited to 10 A. Relay settings for apparatus up to 1100 V must sit between 200-400 mA with time delay. Verify which limit applies to each of your substations by commissioning date.

title: ANNUAL EARTH RESISTANCE TESTING of earthing systems (exceeding 650 V)
detail: Reg 50(8): EVERY EARTHING SYSTEM belonging to either the supplier OR THE CONSUMER shall be TESTED FOR ITS RESISTANCE TO EARTH ON A DRY DAY DURING DRY SEASON NOT LESS THAN ONCE IN A YEAR, and RECORDS OF SUCH TESTS SHALL BE MAINTAINED AND PRODUCED, if so required, BEFORE THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR.
frequency: NOT LESS THAN ONCE IN A YEAR — on a DRY DAY DURING DRY SEASON
remarks: The regulation specifies the TEST CONDITIONS, not just the frequency — testing must be done on a dry day in the dry season, which gives the worst-case (highest) resistance reading. A test done in monsoon does not satisfy this regulation. Plan the annual test for the pre-monsoon dry period.

title: ANNUAL EARTH RESISTANCE TESTING of earthing systems (not exceeding 650 V) + earth fault loop impe...
detail:
