Reg 43(x): ALL EARTHING SYSTEMS BELONGING TO THE SUPPLIER shall in addition be TESTED FOR RESISTANCE ON A DRY DAY DURING THE DRY SEASON AT LEAST ONCE IN A YEAR.
Reg 43(xi): EARTH FAULT LOOP IMPEDANCE SHALL BE TESTED to ensure the automatic operation of the protective device, and A RECORD OF EVERY EARTH TEST MADE AND THE RESULT THEREOF SHALL BE KEPT BY THE SUPPLIER FOR A PERIOD OF NOT LESS THAN TWO YEARS AFTER THE DAY OF TESTING and SHALL BE AVAILABLE TO THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR WHEN REQUIRED.
Reg 43(ix)(c): All earthing systems shall be TESTED TO ENSURE EFFECTIVE EARTH BONDING as per the relevant standards, BEFORE the electric supply lines or apparatus are ENERGISED.
frequency: At least once a year (dry day, dry season); before energising any new installation; RECORDS RETAINED ≥2 YEARS
remarks: Note the SPECIFIC 2-YEAR RETENTION PERIOD for earth test records under Reg 43(xi) — distinct from other record retention periods. Also note the pre-energisation bonding test under Reg 43(ix)(c).

title: PLAN AND SINGLE LINE DIAGRAM of electrical installations at the mine
detail:
Reg 99(1): A CORRECT PLAN, ON THE SAME SCALE AS THE PLAN KEPT AT THE MINE in fulfillment of the requirements of the Mines Act 1952, AND SINGLE LINE DIAGRAM of the electrical installations FROM POINT OF COMMENCEMENT OF SUPPLY, shall be AVAILABLE IN THE OFFICE AT THE MINE showing the POSITION OF ALL FIXED APPARATUS AND CONDUCTORS therein, other than lights, telecommunication or signalling apparatus or cables for the same.

Reg 99(4): The plans specified under this regulation shall be EXAMINED AND CORRECTED AS OFTEN AS NECESSARY TO KEEP THEM UP-TO-DATE, and THE DATES OF SUCH EXAMINATIONS SHALL BE ENTERED THEREON BY THE MANAGER OR OWNER of the mine, and such plans SHALL BE AVAILABLE TO THE INSPECTOR OR INSPECTOR OF MINES AT ANY TIME; and IN CASE EXTENT OF HAZARDOUS AREA IS REVISED, EQUIPMENT COVERED UNDER SUCH AREA SHALL BE REVIEWED as per the relevant standards and/or ATmosphere EXplosible (ATEX).
frequency: Maintained up-to-date; examined and corrected as often as necessary; DATES OF EXAMINATION ENTERED ON THE PLAN
monitoringAuthority: Electrical Inspector / Inspector of Mines (available at any time)
remarks: Two easily-missed points: (a) the plan must be on the SAME SCALE as the statutory mine plan kept under the Mines Act, and (b) the MANAGER OR OWNER must personally ENTER THE DATES OF EXAMINATION on the plan itself — an undated plan is non-compliant even if accurate.

title: TRAINING of personnel for operation and maintenance of electrical installations + REFRESHER TRAIN...
detail:
Reg 118(1): The persons engaged for OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF ELECTRICAL INSTALLATIONS IN MINES are required to UNDERGO THE TYPE OF TRAINING MEANT FOR THE PARTICULAR MINING INSTALLATION OF COAL or Oil or Metal, training syllabus AS ISSUED BY DGMS from time to time under intimation in writing to the Authority.
Reg 118(2): The owner or manager or agent of the mine SHALL ARRANGE FOR TRAINING of their personnel in his OWN INSTITUTE or any other institute RECOGNISED BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT OR STATE GOVERNMENT.
Reg 118(3): THE REFRESHER TRAINING SHALL BE IMPARTED AT A PERIODICITY OF INTERVALS NOT MORE THAN TWO YEARS. A REGISTER or in electronic form shall be MAINTAINED wherein the NAMES OF THE PERSONS TRAINED, DUE DATE OF REFRESHER TRAINING AND THE LIKE shall be entered, and THE REGISTER MAINTAINED SHALL BE PRODUCED BEFORE THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES WHENEVER REQUIRED BY HIM.
frequency: REFRESHER TRAINING AT INTERVALS NOT MORE THAN 2 YEARS; register maintained continuously
remarks: NOTE THE DIFFERENT INTERVAL: electrical refresher training is every 2 YEARS under CER, whereas general mine refresher training under OSH Rule 159 is every 4 YEARS. Track them separately. The register must record the DUE DATE of the next refresher, not merely the date trained.

title: Display of INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESUSCITATION of persons suffering from electric shock
detail:
Reg 30(1): INSTRUCTIONS, in ENGLISH OR HINDI AND THE LOCAL LANGUAGE OF THE DISTRICT (and where Hindi is the local language, in English and Hindi), FOR THE RESUSCITATION OF PERSONS SUFFERING FROM ELECTRIC SHOCK, SHALL BE AFFIXED BY THE OWNER IN A CONSPICUOUS PLACE in every generating station, enclosed substation, enclosed switching station, MINES and in every factory in which electricity is used.
Reg 30(2): The owner shall ENSURE THAT ALL DESIGNATED PERSONS or persons engaged or appointed to operate and maintain electrical plants ARE ACQUAINTED WITH AND ARE COMPETENT TO APPLY THE INSTRUCTIONS referred to in sub-regulation (1).
frequency: Continuous display; competence of designated persons ensured on an ongoing basis
remarks: Not merely a display obligation — Reg 30(2) requires the owner to ENSURE COMPETENCE of every designated person to actually APPLY the resuscitation instructions. Keep a training/briefing record demonstrating this.

title: Display of ADDRESS AND CONTACT of nearest Doctor, Hospital, Ambulance and Fire Service near shock...
detail: Reg 29(6): ADDRESS AND CONTACT NUMBER OF THE NEAREST DOCTOR, HOSPITAL WITH A FACILITY FOR FIRST-AID TREATMENT FOR ELECTRIC SHOCK AND BURNS, AMBULANCE SERVICE AND FIRE SERVICE SHALL BE PROMINENTLY DISPLAYED NEAR THE ELECTRIC SHOCK TREATMENT CHART IN THE CONTROL ROOM AND OPERATOR CABIN.
remarks: Must be displayed adjacent to the Reg 30 resuscitation chart, in BOTH the control room AND the operator cabin. Contact numbers must be kept current.

title: PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT — fire buckets, fire extinguishers (tested), first-aid boxes, gas masks, art...
detail:
Reg 29(1): FIRE BUCKETS FILLED WITH CLEAN DRY SAND and ready for immediate use, IN ADDITION TO FIRE EXTINGUISHERS suitable for dealing with fires, shall be CONSPICUOUSLY MARKED AND KEPT in all generating stations, enclosed substations and enclosed switching-stations in convenient location.
Reg 29(2): Appropriate type of fire extinguisher conforming to relevant standards shall be INSTALLED, MAINTAINED, PERIODICALLY INSPECTED AND TESTED as per the relevant standards, and RECORD OF SUCH TESTS SHALL BE MAINTAINED.
Reg 29(3): SUFFICIENT NUMBER OF FIRST-AID BOXES OR CUPBOARDS conspicuously marked and equipped shall be provided and maintained at appropriate locations in every generating station, enclosed substation, enclosed switching station AND IN VEHICLES USED FOR MAINTENANCE OF LINES, readily available and accessible at all times; and except in unattended substations, kept UNDER THE CHARGE OF RESPONSIBLE PERSONS TRAINED IN FIRST-AID, one of whom shall be AVAILABLE DURING WORKING HOURS.
Reg 29(4): TWO OR MORE GAS MASKS shall be provided and maintained at accessible places in every generating station of 5 MW and above and ENCLOSED SUBSTATION WITH TRANSFORMATION CAPACITY OF 5 MVA AND ABOVE.
Reg 29(5): In every generating station, substation or switching station, an ARTIFICIAL RESPIRATOR, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, FIRST-AID BOXES AND GAS MASKS shall be provided and KEPT IN GOOD WORKING CONDITION, and LOCATIONS OF THE SAME SHALL BE DISPLAYED IN THE CONTROL ROOM AND OPERATOR CABIN.
frequency: Continuous provision; fire extinguishers periodically inspected and TESTED with RECORD MAINTAINED
remarks: Note the 5 MVA threshold triggers the GAS MASK requirement for enclosed substations — commonly overlooked in OC mine substations. First-aid boxes are also required IN LINE MAINTENANCE VEHICLES, not just at fixed installations.

title: DANGER NOTICES on installations exceeding 250 V
detail:
Reg 20: The owner of EVERY INSTALLATION OF VOLTAGE EXCEEDING 250 V shall AFFIX PERMANENTLY IN A CONSPICUOUS POSITION A DANGER NOTICE IN HINDI OR ENGLISH AND THE LOCAL LANGUAGE OF THE DISTRICT, WITH A SIGN OF SKULL AND BONES of a design as per relevant standards, on —
(a) every MOTOR, GENERATOR, TRANSFORMER and other electrical plant and equipment together with apparatus used for controlling or regulating the same;
(b) ALL SUPPORTS OF OVERHEAD LINES OF VOLTAGE EXCEEDING 650 V which can be easily climbed upon without the aid of ladder or special appliances; and
(c) luminous tube sign, X-ray and similar high frequency installations exceeding 650 V but not exceeding 33 kV.
PROVISO: Where it is not possible to affix such notices on any generator, motor, transformer or other apparatus, they shall be affixed AS NEAR AS POSSIBLE THERETO, or the word "DANGER" AND THE VOLTAGE of the apparatus shall be PERMANENTLY PAINTED ON IT.
SECOND PROVISO: Where the apparatus is WITHIN AN ENCLOSURE, ONE NOTICE AFFIXED TO THE SAID ENCLOSURE SHALL BE SUFFICIENT.
mode: Physical (permanently affixed, with skull and bones sign)
remarks: Must be in Hindi or English AND the local language. Where affixing is impossible, the word DANGER plus THE VOLTAGE must be permanently painted on the apparatus.

title: Prohibition notices for undesignated persons and disconnection instruction notices in mines
mode: Physical (Hindi + local language, protected to remain legible)
remarks: Mines-specific notice requirement, distinct from the general Reg 20 danger notices. The disconnection-instruction notice must give FULL INSTRUCTIONS, not just a contact number.

title: SUNDRY PRECAUTIONS — apparatus maintenance, housing, fault isolation, operation only by designate...
detail:
Reg 111(1): All apparatus shall be MAINTAINED REASONABLY FREE FROM DUST, DIRT AND MOISTURE, and shall be KEPT CLEAR OF OBSTRUCTION.
Reg 111(2): All apparatus other than portable and transportable shall be HOUSED IN A ROOM, COMPARTMENT OR BOX so constructed as to PROTECT THE CONTENTS FROM DAMAGE OCCASIONED BY FALLING MATERIAL OR PASSING TRAFFIC.
Reg 111(3): INFLAMMABLE OR EXPLOSIVE MATERIAL SHALL NOT BE STORED in any room, compartment or box containing apparatus, OR IN THE VICINITY OF ANY APPARATUS.
Reg 111(4): IN CASE OF A FAULT IN ANY CIRCUIT, THE PART AFFECTED SHALL BE MADE DEAD WITHOUT DELAY AND SHALL REMAIN SO UNTIL THE FAULT HAS BEEN REMEDIED.
Reg 111(5): While lamps are being changed the SUPPLY SHALL BE DISCONNECTED.
Reg 111(8): ALL APPARATUS, INCLUDING PORTABLE AND TRANSPORTABLE APPARATUS, SHALL BE OPERATED ONLY BY THOSE PERSONS WHO ARE DESIGNATED FOR THE PURPOSE.
Reg 111(9): Where a PLUG-AND-SOCKET COUPLING other than of bolted type is used with flexible cables, AN ELECTRICAL INTERLOCK OR OTHER APPROVED DEVICE SHALL BE PROVIDED TO PREVENT THE OPENING OF THE COUPLING WHILE THE CONDUCTORS ARE LIVE.
remarks: Reg 111(3) — the prohibition on storing inflammable or explosive material "IN THE VICINITY OF ANY APPARATUS" is directly relevant to siting of explosive stores, diesel storage and the SME/ANFO plant relative to electrical apparatus.

title: FLEXIBLE CABLE examination by designated operator + length limits for OC HEMM
detail:
Reg 109(5): EVERY FLEXIBLE CABLE ATTACHED TO A PORTABLE OR TRANSPORTABLE MACHINE SHALL BE EXAMINED PERIODICALLY BY THE PERSON DESIGNATED TO OPERATE THE MACHINE, and if such cable is used underground it shall be examined AT LEAST ONCE IN EACH SHIFT by such person; and IF SUCH CABLE IS FOUND TO BE DAMAGED OR DEFECTIVE, IT SHALL FORTHWITH BE REPLACED BY A CABLE IN GOOD CONDITION.
Reg 109(8): FLEXIBLE CABLE EXCEEDING ONE HUNDRED METRE IN LENGTH SHALL NOT BE USED with any portable or transportable apparatus.
SECOND PROVISO: The aforesaid cable IN CASE OF AN OPEN CAST MINE WHEN USED WITH ELECTRICALLY OPERATED HEAVY EARTH MOVING MACHINERY SHALL NOT EXCEED SIX HUNDRED METRE IN LENGTH, and FOR BUCKET WHEEL EXCAVATOR AT 11 kV SHALL NOT EXCEED ONE THOUSAND METRE IN LENGTH.
THIRD PROVISO: In case of DRAGLINE OR 42 CUBIC METRE CAPACITY SHOVEL, flexible cable length may be raised UP TO 600 METRE.
Reg 109(11): Where flexible cables are used they shall be DETACHED OR OTHERWISE ISOLATED FROM THE SOURCE OF SUPPLY WHEN NOT IN USE, and ARRANGEMENTS SHALL BE MADE TO PREVENT THE ENERGISING OF SUCH CABLES BY UNDESIGNATED PERSONS.
frequency: Examined PERIODICALLY by the designated operator (at least once per shift if used underground); replaced forthwith if damaged
remarks: DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO OC HEMM. Trailing cable length limits: 600 m for electrically operated HEMM including draglines and 42 cu.m shovels; 1000 m for bucket wheel excavator at 11 kV. Exceeding these is a contravention. Note also Reg 109(6) proviso exempts reeling/unreeling OC equipment from the flexible metallic screening requirement.

title: MINIMUM CLEARANCE of overhead lines where DUMPERS or TRACKLESS VEHICLES operate
detail:
Reg 100(4): IN CASE OF MINES, MINIMUM CLEARANCE ABOVE GROUND OF THE LOWEST CONDUCTOR OF OVERHEAD LINES OR OVERHEAD CABLES WHERE DUMPERS OR TRACKLESS VEHICLES ARE BEING OPERATED SHALL NOT BE LESS THAN TWELVE METRE IN HEIGHT FROM THE GROUND ACROSS THE ROAD WHERE DUMPERS OR TRACKLESS VEHICLES CROSS.

PROVISO: WHERE DUMPER BUCKET IS IN RAISED POSITION, THE CLEARANCE BETWEEN THE TOP OF DUMPER BODY AND THE LOWEST CONDUCTOR OF OVERHEAD LINES OR OVERHEAD CABLES SHALL NOT BE LESS THAN ONE METRE.
frequency: Continuous — design and maintenance requirement; verify on every haul road realignment
remarks: CRITICAL FOR OC HAUL ROADS. 12 m minimum ground clearance at every dumper crossing, PLUS a separate 1 m minimum between a RAISED DUMPER BODY and the conductor. Haul roads shift constantly in OC mining — re-verify clearance after every road realignment or bench-level change, and mark and sign every line crossing point.

title: METHOD OF EARTHING in mines — connection to surface substation earthing system
detail:
Reg 102(1): WHERE EARTHING IS NECESSARY IN A MINE, IT SHALL BE CARRIED OUT BY CONNECTION TO AN EARTHING SYSTEM AT THE SURFACE SUBSTATION OF THE MINE.
Reg 102(2): ALL METALLIC SHEATHS, COVERINGS, HANDLES, JOINT BOXES, SWITCHGEAR FRAMES, INSTRUMENT COVERS, SWITCH AND FUSE COVERS OF BOXES, ALL LAMP HOLDERS (unless efficiently protected by an insulated covering of fire resisting material), AND THE FRAMES AND BEDPLATES OF GENERATORS, TRANSFORMERS AND MOTORS INCLUDING PORTABLE MOTORS, SHALL BE EARTHED by connection to an earthing system in the manner specified in sub-regulation (1).
Reg 102(4): All conductors of an earthing system shall have CONDUCTIVITY at all parts and joints AT LEAST EQUAL TO FIFTY PER CENT of that of the largest conductor used solely to supply the apparatus; and NO CONDUCTOR of an earthing system shall have a CROSS-SECTIONAL AREA LESS THAN 0.15 SQ. CM (except the earth conductor of a flexible cable used with portable apparatus where voltage does not exceed 125 V).
Reg 102(5): All joints in earth conductors and in the metallic covering of cables shall be PROPERLY SOLDERED OR OTHERWISE EFFECTIVELY MADE.
Reg 102(6): NO SWITCH, FUSE OR CIRCUIT BREAKER SHALL BE INSERTED IN ANY EARTH CONDUCTOR.
Reg 102(7): This regulation shall not apply, EXCEPT IN THE CASE OF PORTABLE APPARATUS, to any system in a mine in which the VOLTAGE DOES NOT EXCEED 30 V.
frequency: Design and installation requirement; verified at examination and annual earth testing
remarks: Reg 102(6) is absolute — no switch, fuse or circuit breaker may ever be inserted in an earth conductor. Also note the examination of earth fault detectors/recorders under Reg 102(3) is a required Schedule XI log sheet entry [see Record S.No. 4, item (e)].

title: DISCONNECTION OF SUPPLY — switchgear at EIM-recommended point and designated person availability
detail:
Reg 107(1): PROPERLY CONSTRUCTED SWITCHGEAR FOR DISCONNECTING THE SUPPLY OF ELECTRICITY TO A MINE SHALL BE PROVIDED AT A POINT RECOMMENDED BY THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES.
Reg 107(2): AT ANY TIME WHEN ANY CABLE OR OVERHEAD LINE SUPPLYING ELECTRICITY TO THE MINE FROM THE AFORESAID SWITCHGEAR IS LIVE, A PERSON DESIGNATED TO OPERATE THE SAID SWITCHGEAR SHALL BE AVAILABLE WITHIN EASY REACH THEREOF.
Reg 107(3): When necessary in the interest of safety, any apparatus suitably placed shall be provided for DISCONNECTING THE SUPPLY FROM EVERY PART OF A SYSTEM.
Reg 107(5): EVERY MOTOR shall be controlled by switchgear so arranged as to DISCONNECT THE SUPPLY FROM THE MOTOR AND FROM ALL APPARATUS CONNECTED THERETO, and such switchgear shall be SO PLACED AS TO BE EASILY OPERATED BY THE PERSON DESIGNATED TO OPERATE THE MOTOR.
Reg 107(6): A suitably rated switchgear INCORPORATED WITH PROTECTIVE MECHANISM to disconnect automatically the supply in the event of OVER-CURRENT, EARTH FAULT OR LEAKAGE, UNDER VOLTAGE AND SINGLE PHASING.
Reg 107(8): EVERY FEEDER OF THE MINE shall be controlled by a suitably rated switchgear with protective mechanism to disconnect the supply automatically in the event of OVER-CURRENT, SHORT CIRCUIT, SINGLE PHASING, UNDER VOLTAGE AND EARTH FAULT OR LEAKAGE as relevant.
frequency: Continuous — designated person available within easy reach whenever supply line is live
monitoringAuthority: Electrical Inspector of Mines (recommends the point; inspects)
remarks: The disconnection point is not chosen by the mine — it is RECOMMENDED BY THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES. A designated person must be within easy reach of it at all times while the supply line is live, which is a manning obligation, not just an equipment one.

title: ISOLATION AND FIXING OF TRANSFORMER AND SWITCHGEAR
detail:
Reg 101(1): TRANSFORMERS AND SWITCHGEAR SHALL BE PLACED IN A SEPARATE ROOM, COMPARTMENT OR BOX where necessary, or in a manner to PREVENT DANGER OF MECHANICAL DAMAGE AND SPREAD OF FIRE.
Reg 101(2): Unless the apparatus is so constructed, protected and worked as to obviate the risk of fire, NO INFLAMMABLE MATERIAL SHALL BE USED IN THE CONSTRUCTION of any room, compartment or box containing apparatus or in the construction of any fittings therein; and EACH SUCH ROOM, COMPARTMENT OR BOX SHALL BE SUBSTANTIALLY CONSTRUCTED AND SHALL BE KEPT DRY AND ILLUMINATED, and EFFICIENT VENTILATION SHALL BE PROVIDED for all apparatus installed therein.
Reg 101(3): ALL APPARATUS THAT HAS TO BE WORKED OR ATTENDED TO AND ALL HANDLES INTENDED TO BE OPERATED SHALL BE PLACED AT A SPACIOUS WORKING PLACE WHICH IS ACCESSIBLE, CLEAR OF OBSTRUCTION AND FREE FROM DANGER, so far as circumstances permit.
remarks: Substation rooms must be kept DRY, ILLUMINATED and EFFICIENTLY VENTILATED — three separate conditions frequently found deficient at inspection.

title: FIRE EXTINGUISHING APPLIANCES in every place in a mine containing apparatus
detail: Reg 100(3): FIRE EXTINGUISHING APPLIANCES OF ADEQUATE CAPACITY AND OF AN APPROVED TYPE as per relevant standards as amended from time to time SHALL BE INSTALLED AND PROPERLY MAINTAINED IN EVERY PLACE IN A MINE CONTAINING APPARATUS, other than cables, telecommunication and signalling apparatus.
remarks: Applies to EVERY PLACE containing apparatus, not just substations. Read together with CMR Reg 139(6) which requires monthly examination of all fire-fighting equipment, and Reg 29(2) of CER which requires periodic testing with records.

title: ADEQUATE ILLUMINATION and EMERGENCY LIGHTING in opencast mines
detail:
Reg 100(1): ADEQUATE ILLUMINATION BY ELECTRICITY as per relevant standards SHALL BE PROVIDED IN THE MINES.

THIRD PROVISO: In a belowground metalliferous mine OR ANY OPEN CAST MINE or oil-fields, such LIGHTING FIXTURES SHALL BE SUITABLE FOR THE TYPE OF APPLICATION CONFORMING TO THE RELEVANT STANDARDS OR HARMONISED STANDARDS, and ADEQUATE EMERGENCY LIGHTING SYSTEM SHALL BE MAINTAINED IN ALL PLACES WHERE FAILURE OF THE ELECTRIC LIGHT AT ANY TIME SHALL BE PREJUDICIAL TO SAFETY.
remarks: Identify and document every location where lighting failure would be prejudicial to safety (crusher, workshop, fuel bay, control room, magazine approach, haul road junctions) and provide emergency lighting there.

title: MEANS OF COMMUNICATION between disconnection switchgear point and distributing centres
detail: Reg 100(2): EFFICIENT MEANS OF COMMUNICATION SHALL BE PROVIDED IN EVERY MINE BETWEEN THE POINT WHERE THE SWITCHGEAR UNDER SUB-REGULATION (1) OF REGULATION 107 IS ERECTED, THE SHAFT BOTTOM AND OTHER DISTRIBUTING CENTRES IN THE MINES.
remarks: For OC, the obligation is communication between the main disconnection switchgear point and all distributing centres/substations.

title: VOLTAGE LIMITS for lighting, hand-held portable apparatus and remote control circuits
detail:
Reg 104 PROVISO (i): WHERE HAND-HELD PORTABLE APPARATUS IS USED, THE VOLTAGE SHALL NOT EXCEED 125 V.
PROVISO (ii)(b): ON THE SURFACE OF A MINE OR IN AN OPEN CAST MINE, the voltage FOR ELECTRIC LIGHTING MAY BE RAISED TO 250 V, IF THE NEUTRAL OR THE MID-POINT OF THE SYSTEM IS CONNECTED WITH EARTH AND THE VOLTAGE BETWEEN THE PHASES DOES NOT EXCEED 250 V.
PROVISO (iv) final part: IN FIXED PLANTS ON SURFACE OF THE MINES OR OPENCAST MINES, THE SAID VOLTAGE FOR THE REMOTE CONTROL OR ELECTRIC INTER-LOCKING MAY BE PERMITTED UP TO 250 V.
remarks: The 250 V lighting allowance for OC is CONDITIONAL on the neutral or mid-point being earthed and phase-to-phase voltage not exceeding 250 V. Hand-held portable apparatus is capped at 125 V with no OC relaxation.

title: PORTABLE AND TRANSPORTABLE MACHINES — remote control and operator tripping device in OC mines
detail:
Reg 110 main: The person designated to operate an electrically driven portable or transportable machine SHALL NOT LEAVE THE MACHINE WHILE IT IS IN OPERATION and shall, before leaving the area, ENSURE THAT THE SUPPLY IS DISCONNECTED FROM THE FLEXIBLE CABLE; and steps shall be taken to ensure THE FLEXIBLE CABLE IS NOT DRAGGED ALONG BY THE MACHINE.

SECOND PROVISO: THE PORTABLE AND TRANSPORTABLE MACHINES USED IN OPEN CAST MINES SHALL HAVE THE PROVISION SUCH THAT THE POWER SUPPLY TO THE MACHINE FROM CONCERNED SWITCHGEAR IS REMOTELY CONTROLLED FROM THE MACHINE.

THIRD PROVISO: THE PORTABLE OR TRANSPORTABLE MACHINES USED IN OPEN CAST MINE, PROVISION OF TRIPPING DEVICE OR SWITCH DEVICE FROM THE OPERATORS CABIN SHALL BE PROVIDED TO DISCONNECT POWER SUPPLY TO SUCH MACHINE FROM THE FIELD SWITCHGEAR.
frequency: Continuous — equipment provision and operating discipline
signerRole: Owner / Agent / Manager; Designated operator (operating duty)
remarks: TWO SEPARATE OC-SPECIFIC EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS: (a) remote control of power supply from the machine, and (b) a tripping/switch device IN THE OPERATORS CABIN to disconnect from field switchgear. Also note the cable-dragging prohibition, a common cause of trailing cable damage on OC benches.

title: SWITCHGEAR, TERMINALS, CABLE ENDS AND JOINTS — construction and maintenance standards
remarks: Clause (v) — protection against open sparking where COAL DUST may be ignited — applies at OC coal handling plants, crushers, conveyor transfer points and stockyards, not only in gassy underground seams.

title: CABLES — insulation, mechanical protection, metallic covering continuity and earthing
remarks: The 50% conductivity requirement for metallic covering (clause (iv)(d)) mirrors the earthing conductor requirement in Reg 102(4) and is a frequent inspection finding on older or repaired cable runs.

title: SHOT-FIRING — protection of apparatus and prohibition on using lighting/power circuits
detail:
Reg 113(1): WHEN SHOT-FIRING IS IN PROGRESS, ADEQUATE PRECAUTIONS SHALL BE TAKEN TO PROTECT APPARATUS AND CONDUCTORS, OTHER THAN THOSE USED FOR SHOT-FIRING, FROM INJURY.
Reg 113(2): CURRENT FROM LIGHTING OR POWER CIRCUITS SHALL NOT BE USED FOR FIRING SHOTS.
Reg 113(3): THE CONSTRUCTION OF SHOT FIRING CABLES SHALL CONFORM TO RELEVANT STANDARDS and ADEQUATE PRECAUTIONS SHALL BE TAKEN TO PREVENT SUCH CABLE TOUCHING OTHER CABLES AND APPARATUS.
remarks: Reg 113(2) is an ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION — lighting or power circuit current must never be used to fire shots. Read with CMR Reg 195 (electric shot-firing) and the quarterly shot-firing apparatus test under CMR Reg 195(5).

title: EARTHING OF NEUTRAL POINTS in mines exceeding 30 V
detail:
Reg 116: WHERE THE VOLTAGE OF AN ALTERNATING CURRENT SYSTEM EXCEEDS 30 V, THE NEUTRAL OR MID-POINT SHALL BE EARTHED BY CONNECTION TO AN EARTHING SYSTEM IN THE MANNER SPECIFIED IN REGULATION 102.

FIRST PROVISO: When the system concerned is REQUIRED FOR BLASTING AND SIGNALLING PURPOSES, the provisions of this regulation SHALL NOT APPLY.

SECOND PROVISO: In case of UNEARTHED NEUTRAL SYSTEM, IT SHALL BE EQUIPPED WITH A SUITABLE GROUND PROTECTION SYSTEM APPROVED BY THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF MINES to ensure isolation of power supply to the faulty section in appropriate manner.
monitoringAuthority: Electrical Inspector of Mines (approves ground protection system for unearthed neutral)
mode: Compliance at site + EIM approval where applicable
remarks: If any unearthed neutral system is used, the ground protection system requires EXPRESS APPROVAL of the Electrical Inspector of Mines — obtain and retain that approval in writing.

title: HANDLING OF ELECTRIC SUPPLY LINES AND APPARATUS — PPE, permit-to-work and Schedule I precautions
detail:
Reg 21(1): BEFORE ANY CONDUCTOR OR APPARATUS IS HANDLED, ADEQUATE PRECAUTIONS SHALL BE TAKEN, BY EARTHING OR OTHER SUITABLE MEANS, TO DISCHARGE ELECTRICALLY SUCH CONDUCTOR OR APPARATUS, AND ANY ADJACENT CONDUCTOR OR APPARATUS if there is danger therefrom, AND TO PREVENT ANY CONDUCTOR OR APPARATUS FROM BEING ACCIDENTALLY OR INADVERTENTLY ELECTRICALLY CHARGED WHEN PERSONS ARE WORKING THEREON.
Reg 21(2): EVERY PERSON WORKING ON AN ELECTRIC SUPPLY LINE OR APPARATUS SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH — (a) PPE, TOOLS AND DEVICES such as RUBBER GLOVES AND SAFETY FOOTWEAR SUITABLE FOR WORKING VOLTAGE, SAFETY BELTS FOR WORKING AT HEIGHT, NONCONDUCTIVE LADDER, EARTHING DEVICES OF APPROPRIATE CLASS, HELMET, LINE TESTER, HAND LINES, VOLTAGE DETECTOR AND HAND TOOLS; and (b) ANY OTHER DEVICE FOR PROTECTING HIM FROM MECHANICAL AND ELECTRICAL INJURY DUE TO ARC FLASH; and such PPE SHALL ALWAYS BE MAINTAINED IN SOUND WORKING CONDITION.
Reg 21(3): NO PERSON SHALL OPERATE AND UNDERTAKE MAINTENANCE WORK on any part of an electrical plant or supply line, AND NO PERSON SHALL ASSIST SUCH PERSON, UNLESS HE IS DESIGNATED IN THAT BEHALF AND OBSERVES THE SAFETY PRECAUTIONS GIVEN IN PART-I, PART-II, PART-III AND PART-IV OF SCHEDULE I.
Reg 21(5): ALL NON-CURRENT CARRYING METAL PARTS OF SWITCHGEAR AND CONTROL PANELS SHALL BE PROPERLY EARTHED AND INSULATING FLOORS OR MATS conforming to relevant standards, OF APPROPRIATE VOLTAGE LEVEL, SHALL BE PROVIDED IN FRONT AND REAR OF THE PANELS.
Schedule I Part-II requires the Engineer or Supervisor in-charge to IDENTIFY HAZARDS, BRIEF THE WORKING GROUP, and OBTAIN PROPER PERMIT-TO-WORK from the Operation In-charge, ensuring the section is ISOLATED FROM ALL SOURCES OF ENERGY, DE-ENERGISED AND EARTHED.
frequency: Before and during every job on electrical lines/apparatus; PPE maintained continuously
remarks: PERMIT-TO-WORK SYSTEM IS MANDATORY via Schedule I Part-II. Insulating mats are required in FRONT AND REAR of panels, not just in front. Maintain permit-to-work records as evidence of compliance.

title: TRANSPORTING AND STORING OF MATERIAL NEAR ELECTRIC LINES
detail:
Reg 66(1): NO RODS, PIPES OR SIMILAR MATERIALS SHALL BE TAKEN BELOW, OR IN THE VICINITY OF, ANY BARE OVERHEAD CONDUCTORS OR LINES. PROVISO: if these materials contravene Reg 62 and 63, such materials shall be TRANSPORTED UNDER THE DIRECT SUPERVISION OF A DESIGNATED PERSON.
Reg 66(2): NO RODS, PIPES OR OTHER SIMILAR MATERIALS SHALL BE BROUGHT WITHIN THE FLASH OVER DISTANCE OF BARE LIVE CONDUCTORS OR OVERHEAD LINES.
Reg 66(3): NO MATERIAL OR EARTH WORK OR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE SHALL BE DUMPED OR STORED, NO TREES GROWN, BELOW OR IN THE VICINITY OF BARE OVERHEAD CONDUCTORS OR LINES in contravention of Reg 62 and 63.
Reg 66(4): NO FLAMMABLE MATERIAL SHALL BE STORED UNDER THE ELECTRIC LINE.
Reg 66(5): NO FIRE SHALL BE ALLOWED BELOW OVERHEAD LINES AND ABOVE THE DEMARCATED UNDERGROUND CABLES.
remarks: CRITICAL FOR OC OPERATIONS. Reg 66(3) prohibits DUMPING OR STORING MATERIAL OR EARTH WORK below or near bare overhead lines — directly restricts where OB dumps, topsoil stacks and material stockpiles may be sited. Reg 66(4) prohibits FLAMMABLE MATERIAL STORAGE under a line (diesel, oil, explosives-related stores). Reg 66(5) prohibits fires below lines and above demarcated underground cables.

title: ANTI-CLIMBING DEVICES on supports of overhead lines exceeding 650 V
detail:
Reg 75: THE OWNER OF EVERY OVERHEAD LINE OF VOLTAGE EXCEEDING 650 V SHALL MAKE ADEQUATE ARRANGEMENTS as per relevant standards TO PREVENT UNAUTHORISED PERSONS FROM CLIMBING ANY OF THE SUPPORTS of such overhead lines which can be easily climbed upon without the help of a ladder or special appliances.

PROVISO: BARBED WIRES conforming to relevant standards FOR A VERTICAL DISTANCE OF 30 TO 40 CM, AT A HEIGHT OF 3.5 METRE TO 4 METRE FROM GROUND LEVEL, OR CLAMPS WITH PROTRUDING SPIKES AT A HEIGHT OF 3 TO 4 METRE, SHALL BE PROVIDED ON EACH POLE OR TOWER OF 11 kV LINE AND ABOVE.
remarks: The proviso gives EXACT DIMENSIONS — barbed wire over a 30-40 cm vertical band at 3.5-4 m height, or spiked clamps at 3-4 m, on EACH pole or tower of 11 kV and above. Verify against actual site installations.

title: SAFETY AND PROTECTIVE DEVICES — earth guarding of overhead lines in mines and bird guards
detail:
Reg 76(1): EVERY OVERHEAD LINE which is NOT being suspended from a dead bearer wire, NOT covered with insulating material, and NOT a trolley-wire, WHICH IS LAID OVER ANY PART OF A STREET OR OTHER PUBLIC PLACE OR IN ANY FACTORY OR MINE OR ON ANY CONSUMERS PREMISES, SHALL BE PROTECTED WITH EARTH GUARDING FOR RENDERING THE LINE ELECTRICALLY HARMLESS IN CASE ITS CONDUCTOR BREAKS.
Reg 76(2): An Electrical Inspector may, BY NOTICE IN WRITING, REQUIRE THE OWNER of any such overhead line, WHEREVER IT MAY BE LAID, TO PROTECT IT in the manner specified in sub-regulation (1).
Reg 76(3): TO PREVENT BIRD DROPPING ON THE SUSPENSION INSULATOR STRINGS, SUITABLE BIRD GUARDS as per relevant standards SHALL BE PROVIDED ON CROSS ARMS of suspension tower or suspension pole structures, over the suspension insulator strings.
monitoringAuthority: Electrical Inspector (on inspection; may issue written notice)
remarks: Earth guarding is expressly required for bare overhead lines laid in a MINE. Bird guards on suspension insulator strings are a separate and often-overlooked requirement.

title: PROTECTION AGAINST LIGHTNING for overhead lines, substations and generating stations
detail:
Reg 77(1): THE OWNER OF EVERY OVERHEAD LINE, SUBSTATION OR GENERATING STATION WHICH IS EXPOSED TO LIGHTNING SHALL ADOPT MEANS as per relevant standards FOR DIVERTING ELECTRICAL SURGES TO THE EARTH DUE TO LIGHTNING which may result into injuries.
Reg 77(2): THE EARTHING LEAD FOR ANY LIGHTNING ARRESTER SHALL BE AS SHORT AS POSSIBLE AND SHALL NOT PASS THROUGH ANY IRON OR STEEL PIPE, BUT SHALL BE TAKEN AS DIRECTLY AS POSSIBLE FROM THE LIGHTNING ARRESTER WITHOUT TOUCHING ANY METAL PART TO A SEPARATE VERTICAL EARTH ELECTRODE OR JUNCTION OF THE EARTH MAT already provided for the substation of voltage exceeding 650 V, subject to the avoidance of bends wherever practicable. PROVISO: A VERTICAL EARTH ELECTRODE SHALL BE CONNECTED TO THE JUNCTION OF THE EARTH MAT.
remarks: Very specific installation requirements for the lightning arrester earthing lead — as short as possible, NOT through iron or steel pipe, no contact with metal parts, minimum bends. Read alongside the PESO lightning conductor annual test requirement for the magazine and SME plant under Explosives Rules 2008.

title: UNUSED OVERHEAD LINES — maintain in safe condition or remove
detail:
Reg 78: WHERE AN OVERHEAD LINE CEASES TO BE USED AS AN ELECTRIC SUPPLY LINE —
(i) THE OWNER SHALL MAINTAIN IT IN A SAFE MECHANICAL CONDITION IN ACCORDANCE WITH REGULATION 59 OR REMOVE IT; and
(ii) THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR SHALL, BY A NOTICE IN WRITING SERVED ON THE OWNER, REQUIRE HIM TO MAINTAIN IT IN A SAFE MECHANICAL CONDITION OR TO REMOVE IT WITHIN THIRTY DAYS OF THE RECEIPT OF THE NOTICE.
frequency: On the line ceasing to be used; 30 days from receipt of Inspector notice
remarks: RELEVANT TO OC MINE PROGRESSION. As pits advance and substations/lines are relocated, disused overhead lines must either be kept in certified safe mechanical condition or removed. Abandoned lines left in place without maintenance are a contravention.

title: DISTINCTION OF DIFFERENT CIRCUITS and installations having more than one feed
detail:
Reg 26: THE OWNER OF EVERY GENERATING STATION, SUBSTATION, JUNCTION BOX OR PILLAR BOX IN WHICH THERE ARE ANY CIRCUITS OR APPARATUS, WHETHER INTENDED FOR OPERATION AT DIFFERENT VOLTAGES OR AT THE SAME VOLTAGE, SHALL ENSURE BY MEANS OF INDICATION OF A PERMANENT NATURE THAT THE RESPECTIVE CIRCUITS ARE READILY DISTINGUISHABLE FROM EACH OTHER.

Reg 27: THE OWNER OF EVERY INSTALLATION INCLUDING SUBSTATION, DOUBLE POLE STRUCTURE, FOUR POLE STRUCTURE OR ANY OTHER STRUCTURE HAVING MORE THAN ONE FEED, SHALL ENSURE BY MEANS OF INDICATION OF A PERMANENT NATURE, THAT THE INSTALLATION IS READILY DISTINGUISHABLE FROM OTHER INSTALLATIONS.

Reg 21(6): ALL PANELS SHALL BE PAINTED WITH THE DESCRIPTION OF THEIR IDENTIFICATION AT FRONT AND AT THE REAR.
remarks: Multi-feed installations are a serious isolation hazard — permanent identification is mandatory. Panel identification must be painted at BOTH front AND rear per Reg 21(6).

title: SUPPLY TO VEHICLES AND CRANES
detail: Reg 22: EVERY PERSON OWNING A VEHICLE, TRAVELLING CRANE, OR THE LIKE TO WHICH ELECTRICITY IS SUPPLIED FROM AN EXTERNAL SOURCE SHALL ENSURE THAT IT IS EFFICIENTLY CONTROLLED BY A SUITABLE SWITCH ENABLING ALL VOLTAGE TO BE CUT OFF IN ONE OPERATION; AND WHERE SUCH VEHICLE, TRAVELLING CRANE OR THE LIKE RUNS ON METAL RAILS, THE OWNER SHALL ENSURE THAT THE RAILS ARE ELECTRICALLY CONTINUOUS AND EARTHED AT MULTIPLE POINTS TO ENSURE EQUIPOTENTIAL.
remarks: Single-operation isolation switch required. Rail-mounted equipment additionally requires electrically continuous, multi-point earthed rails.

title: CABLES FOR PORTABLE OR TRANSPORTABLE APPARATUS — general requirements
detail:
Reg 23(1): FLEXIBLE CABLES SHALL NOT BE USED FOR PORTABLE OR TRANSPORTABLE MOTORS, GENERATORS, TRANSFORMERS, RECTIFIERS, ELECTRIC DRILLS, ELECTRIC SPRAYERS, WELDING SETS OR ANY OTHER PORTABLE OR TRANSPORTABLE APPARATUS UNLESS THEY ARE INSULATED FOR REQUIRED VOLTAGE as per relevant standards AND ADEQUATELY PROTECTED FROM MECHANICAL DAMAGE.
Reg 23(2): WHERE THE PROTECTION IS BY MEANS OF METALLIC COVERING, THE COVERING SHALL BE IN METALLIC CONNECTION WITH THE FRAME OF ANY SUCH APPARATUS AND EARTHED.
Reg 23(3): THE CABLES SHALL BE THREE CORE TYPE AND FOUR CORE TYPE FOR PORTABLE AND TRANSPORTABLE APPARATUS WORKING ON SINGLE PHASE AND THREE PHASE SUPPLY RESPECTIVELY, AND THE CORE MEANT TO BE USED FOR EARTH CONNECTION SHALL BE EASILY IDENTIFIABLE.
remarks: Applies to workshop welding sets and portable tools as well as mining equipment. Read together with the mines-specific flexible cable requirements in Reg 109.

title: PERIODIC INSPECTION AND TESTING OF INSTALLATIONS — mines inspected by Electrical Inspector
detail:
Reg 32(2): The PERIODICITY of electrical inspection by the Electrical Inspector or the self-certification shall be AS DIRECTED BY THE APPROPRIATE GOVERNMENT. PROVISO: THE PERIODICITY OF ELECTRICAL INSPECTION AND SELF-CERTIFICATION SHALL NOT EXCEED FIVE YEARS. FURTHER PROVISO: In respect of the electrical installation belonging to MINES, oil-fields and railways, SUCH DIRECTION SHALL BE ISSUED BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT.
Reg 32(4): Notwithstanding sub-regulation (3), EVERY ELECTRICAL INSTALLATION COVERED UNDER SECTION 54 OF THE ACT INCLUDING EVERY ELECTRICAL INSTALLATION OF MINES, OIL-FIELDS AND RAILWAYS SHALL BE PERIODICALLY INSPECTED AND TESTED BY THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR OF THE APPROPRIATE GOVERNMENT.
Reg 32(8): IT SHALL BE THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE OWNER OF ALL INSTALLATIONS TO MAINTAIN AND OPERATE THE INSTALLATIONS IN A CONDITION FREE FROM DANGER AND AS RECOMMENDED BY THE MANUFACTURER OR BY THE RELEVANT STANDARDS.
Reg 32(7): In the event of FAILURE OF THE OWNER TO RECTIFY THE DEFECTS pointed out by the Electrical Inspector within the time indicated, SUCH INSTALLATION SHALL BE LIABLE TO BE DISCONNECTED under the directions of the Electrical Inspector after serving NOT LESS THAN FORTY EIGHT HOURS NOTICE.
formNo: Schedule II — Form I / II / III / IV (self-certification route)
frequency: PERIODICITY NOT EXCEEDING FIVE YEARS; for mines, as directed by the Central Government
monitoringAuthority: Electrical Inspector / Electrical Inspector of Mines
remarks: MINES ARE EXPRESSLY CARVED OUT under Reg 32(4) — mine installations must be inspected and tested BY THE ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR, with the self-certification route limited to below-650 V installations under Reg 45(7) proviso. Failure to rectify notified defects can lead to DISCONNECTION on 48 hours notice.

title: ACCESSIBILITY TO BARE CONDUCTORS and accidental charging prevention
detail:
Reg 19: WHERE BARE CONDUCTORS ARE USED IN A BUILDING, THE OWNER OF SUCH CONDUCTORS SHALL — (a) ENSURE THAT THEY ARE INACCESSIBLE TO GENERAL PUBLIC; (b) PROVIDE IN READILY ACCESSIBLE POSITION SWITCHES FOR RENDERING THEM DEAD WHENEVER NECESSARY; and (c) TAKE SUCH OTHER SAFETY MEASURES as specified in the relevant standards.

Reg 28(1): THE OWNERS OF ALL CIRCUITS AND APPARATUS SHALL SO ARRANGE THEM THAT THERE SHALL BE NO DANGER OF ANY PART THEREOF BECOMING ACCIDENTALLY CHARGED TO ANY VOLTAGE BEYOND THE LIMITS OF VOLTAGE FOR WHICH THEY ARE INTENDED.
Reg 28(2): WHERE ALTERNATING CURRENT AND DIRECT CURRENT CIRCUITS ARE INSTALLED ON THE SAME BOX OR SUPPORT, THEY SHALL BE SO ARRANGED AND PROTECTED THAT THEY SHALL NOT COME INTO CONTACT WITH EACH OTHER.

title: Weekly Thorough Inspection of All Machinery and Plant (incl. HEMM)
detail:
Reg 213(3): Every person in-charge of any machinery, apparatus or appliance shall, before commencing work, see that it is in proper working order and if he observes any defect therein, he shall immediately report the fact to the manager, engineer or other competent person.
Reg 213(5): A competent person or persons appointed for the purpose shall, once at least in every seven days, make a thorough inspection of all machinery and plant in use, and shall record the result thereof in a bound paged book kept for the purpose.
Reg 213(6): In respect of electrical machinery and plant, the competent person shall be an engineer or electrician holding qualifications as specified in CEA Regulations 2010.
frequency: Once at least in every 7 days (weekly thorough inspection); defect reporting is continuous/before commencing work
remarks: CORRECTED: This is a single weekly thorough inspection requirement for ALL machinery, distinct from the operator's own daily shift inspection under Reg 62(c)/63(c) (S.No. 28-29). Reg 213 does NOT prescribe separate daily/monthly/annual tiers — that was an earlier drafting error, now fixed. This weekly inspection is over and above the operator's daily pre-shift check.

title: Cranes / lifting gear — test certificates, SWL markings, examination records
detail: No crane or lifting gear shall be used unless it has been tested and certified before first use and periodically thereafter. Safe Working Load (SWL) shall be clearly marked. Examination records maintained in bound paged book.
frequency: Before first use; periodically as prescribed

title: Fire Detection and Suppression System on HEMM (Opencast) + Monthly Fire Equipment Examination
detail:
Reg 139(1)(d): Every heavy earth moving machinery used in opencast workings shall be provided with automatically operated fire detection and suppression device or system. Proviso: for trucks and dumpers of less than 35 tonne capacity used in OC mines, a semi-automatic type fire suppression system may suffice.
Reg 139(6): A competent person shall, once at least in every month, examine all the equipment, material and arrangements provided for fire-fighting and shall discharge and re-fill fire-extinguishers as necessary; any deficiency found shall be immediately remedied.
Reg 139(7): A report of every such examination shall be made in a bound paged book, duly signed and dated by the person making the examination.
frequency: Fire suppression system: fitted before HEMM deployment; Examination: once at least every month
remarks: Direct HEMM-specific fire safety requirement — every OC HEMM unit must carry auto fire detection/suppression; smaller trucks/dumpers (<35T) may use semi-automatic type.

title: ANNUAL TESTING of LIGHTNING CONDUCTOR + display of test certificate
detail: Every magazine and process building must have efficient lightning conductors per BIS specifications. Earth resistance tested at least ONCE EVERY YEAR by a qualified electrical engineer or State Govt-certified competent person. Resistance not more than 10 ohms. Test certificate showing results and date of last test CONSPICUOUSLY DISPLAYED at the premises.
formNo: Test certificate (no prescribed form) — prominently displayed; fee Rs. 500 if tested by Departmental officer
frequency: AT LEAST ONCE IN EVERY YEAR; certificate CONSPICUOUSLY DISPLAYED
monitoringAuthority: Displayed at premises; produced to Controller / testing officer on demand
signerRole: Qualified Electrical Engineer or State-Govt certified competent person; Licensee (display obligation)
remarks: THREE DISTINCT REQUIREMENTS: annual test by a QUALIFIED PERSON; resistance ≤10 OHMS; certificate CONSPICUOUSLY DISPLAYED with date of last test. A test done but not displayed is still a contravention. Note: LE-4 condition (tractor compressor) requires annual check of compressor fittings — safety valve, limiting pressure switch and pressure gauge — in addition to lightning conductor.

title: BMD VEHICLE — static electricity control, hose testing, electrical continuity and bonding
detail: Grounding device and semiconductive hose used during mixing/loading to prevent static electricity. Flexible hoses tested PERIODICALLY by water at prescribed pressure AND for electrical continuity. BMD vehicle body and equipment electrically continuous with chassis and bonded. Generator/battery cut-off switch accessible.
regulationRef: SET-V Cond. 7, 8; Schedule VI Part 2, items 14, 15, 17
frequency: PERIODIC hose tests — hydraulic pressure test AND electrical continuity test; static evaluation before each day's operations
mode: Physical + dated test records per hose per vehicle
remarks: TWO SEPARATE PERIODIC HOSE TESTS required: water pressure test AND electrical continuity test. Maintain dated test record per hose per vehicle. Periodicity not fixed by rule — define and justify in SOP (e.g. quarterly).

title: PRECAUTIONS AT BLASTING SITE — power discontinuation, 15 m exclusion, charged holes unattended
detail: Electric power discontinued before charging. No work other than charging within 15 m of holes. Charged holes never left unattended until blasting is complete. Surplus explosives removed from vicinity of hole after charging. No damage to fuse/wires during stemming.
remarks: Rule 92(4): CHARGED HOLES MUST NEVER BE LEFT UNATTENDED — significant manpower implication for overnight or multi-shift charging. Read with CMR Reg 203/206.

title: PRECAUTIONS AGAINST STRAY CURRENTS and regular testing of exploders
detail: Tests made for stray currents wherever electrically operated equipment is used in conductive ground or continuous metal objects are present. Exploders regularly tested and maintained in fit condition; must not be used above rated capacity. Electric circuit tested for continuity before firing; all non-essential persons withdrawn before continuity testing.
frequency: Stray current tests per blasting round (where applicable); exploders REGULARLY TESTED; continuity tested BEFORE EVERY FIRING
remarks: DIRECTLY RELEVANT IN AN OC MINE with HT lines, trailing cables and conveyor structures — conductive ground and continuous metal objects are the norm. Read with CER Reg 113 and CMR Reg 195(5) quarterly exploder testing.

title: USE OF ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT in explosives premises requires prior written CHIEF CONTROLLER PERMIS...
detail: No electrical equipment may be used in places where explosives are being manufactured, handled or stored without prior written permission of the Chief Controller. Equipment type must be acceptable to the Chief Controller.
frequency: Prior written permission before installing or using any electrical equipment
mode: Written permission (retained on file with licence)
remarks: CRITICAL AND OFTEN OVERLOOKED. Even lighting, fans, CCTV cameras or a mobile charging point inside or at a magazine requires PRIOR WRITTEN PERMISSION OF THE CHIEF CONTROLLER, and the equipment type itself must be acceptable to him. Retain that permission permanently with the licence file.

title: Consent to Operate (CTO) and renewal
detail: The mine shall operate only under a valid consent to operate, and application for renewal shall be made before its expiry as stipulated by the Board.
act: Water Act 1974 s.25 / Air Act 1981 s.21

title: Prohibition on constructing brick kiln or other POLLUTING UNITS within 500 m of installations or ...
detail: No person shall construct brick kiln or OTHER POLLUTING UNITS near the installations or transmission lines of 220 kV AND ABOVE within a distance of FIVE HUNDRED METRE.
frequency: Before construction / siting of any polluting unit
monitoringAuthority: Compliance obligation (no permission route provided) — verified by Electrical Inspector
remarks: ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION — no permission mechanism exists, unlike Reg 67(2) and 67(3). An SME/ANFO bulk explosives plant, crusher, or similar unit is arguably a polluting unit; verify the 500 m distance from any 220 kV+ line before siting or expanding such facilities.

title: Records of hazardous waste generated, stored and disposed
detail: The occupier shall maintain records of hazardous and other wastes handled in the prescribed form and make them available for inspection.

detail: Hazardous waste shall be transported only with the prescribed movement document (manifest), copies whereof shall be retained and circulated as prescribed; used/waste oil sold only to registered recyclers.

detail: Periodic environmental quality monitoring (PM10/PM2.5, water quality of mine discharge, noise) shall be carried out at the stipulated locations and frequency and the results recorded and reported as per consent and EC conditions.

title: Top soil management, OB dump stabilisation and green belt/plantation records
detail: Top soil shall be stacked separately and used for reclamation; OB dumps benched, stabilised and vegetated; annual plantation targets achieved and survival records maintained.

title: Precaution Against Dust — Sampling of Airborne Respirable Dust (Surface & Belowground)
detail:
Reg 143(1): The owner, agent or manager of every mine shall take steps necessary for minimising emission of dust and for suppression of dust entering the air at any workplace belowground OR ON SURFACE, ensuring worker exposure to respirable dust is limited to permissible levels.
Reg 143(3): Within 3 months of CMR coming into force and once at least in every month thereafter (or whenever RI requires), air at every workplace where airborne dust is generated shall be sampled and concentration of respirable dust determined.
Reg 143(8): All results of measurement of airborne respirable dust shall be systematically recorded within 14 days of sample collection, in a bound paged book, and every entry countersigned and dated by the manager within 24 hours.
frequency: Monthly sampling; results recorded within 14 days; manager countersign within 24 hours
remarks: Applies to OC surface operations directly — not UG-only as commonly assumed.

title: Dust Suppression Device — Weekly Inspection + Monthly Test
detail: Every device used for the prevention and suppression of dust produced by any machinery, equipment or process, as also for the filtering of exhausted air and every dust respirator, shall be inspected once at least in every seven days and shall be thoroughly examined and tested at least once in every month, and the results of every such inspection, examination and test shall be recorded in the register maintained under Reg 143(8).
mode: Physical (bound paged book — same register as Reg 143(8))
remarks: Directly relevant to OC: water spray systems on drills, crushers, haul roads.

title: Vibration Report — ground vibration record for each blast
detail: Daily ground vibration record (seismograph) for every blast, per condition of the site-specific DGMS blasting permission.
signerRole: Blasting Officer / Shot-firer; countersigned by Manager
remarks: Not a CMR requirement — CMR is silent on vibration. This is a condition of your specific DGMS blasting permission, so track it exactly as that permission requires and re-verify if the permission is renewed or revised.

title: REMOVAL AND DESTRUCTION OF EMPTY PACKAGES + disposal of waste and split explosives
detail: Empty packages removed at the earliest and destroyed. Spillages/split explosives immediately collected and destroyed at safe place. Rule 42(1): Process buildings and machineries swept and cleaned at end of each shift; waste explosives collected, stored safely and safely disposed. Rule 42(2): Adequate facilities for safe destruction at a LICENSING-AUTHORITY-APPROVED place must be provided. Effluents discharged after proper treatment.
regulationRef: Rule 17; Rule 42(1)-(2); SET-VII Cond. 24; SET-V Cond. 11
frequency: Empty packages removed AT THE EARLIEST and destroyed; spillages collected and destroyed IMMEDIATELY; process building cleaning at END OF EACH SHIFT
monitoringAuthority: Controller (on inspection); destruction accounted in RE returns
remarks: NEW: Rule 42(1) end-of-shift cleaning and Rule 42(2) approved destruction place were missing from previous register. The destruction-approved place must be separately approved by the licensing authority — confirm this is in place. Destruction of explosives must be accounted for in quarterly return (Rule 24(3) covers explosives DESTROYED).

title: Milestone 1 – GR (Geological Report)
detail: Geological Report (GR): The foundational exploration document for the coal block, compiled from drilling/borehole data and geophysical surveys and approved by CMPDI/Ministry of Coal. It establishes the coal reserves (proved/indicated/inferred), number and thickness of seams, coal quality and grade, gradient, depth, overburden ratio and the geological structure (faults, dykes) of the block. The approved GR is the basis on which the Mining Plan and all subsequent development is prepared, so its approval is Milestone 1 of the commencement chain.

title: Milestone 2 – Mining Plan Approval
detail: Mining Plan Approval: Preparation and approval of the Mining Plan together with the Progressive & Final Mine Closure Plan under the MMDR Act, 1957 and applicable Mineral Concession/Coal Block rules, submitted to the Ministry of Coal / Coal Controller's Organisation for approval. It sets out the method of working (opencast), year-wise production and development schedule, ultimate pit design, OB dump and backfilling plan, environmental management and progressive/final closure with financial assurance. No mining operation can begin until the Mining Plan is approved.

title: Milestone 3 – FC / EC / Public Hearing
detail: Forest Clearance, Environmental Clearance & Public Hearing: The three linked environmental gates. (1) Forest Clearance (FC) under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 for diversion of forest land — Stage-I in-principle approval followed by Stage-II final approval after compliance with conditions (compensatory afforestation, NPV). (2) Environmental Clearance (EC) from MoEF&CC under the EIA Notification, 2006, based on an EIA/EMP study. (3) Public Hearing conducted by the State Pollution Control Board (CGPCB) as the mandatory public-consultation stage of the EC process, recording the views of project-affected people before EC is granted.

title: Milestone 4 – R&R
detail: Rehabilitation & Resettlement (R&R): Land acquisition and resettlement of project-affected families under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (and, for coal, the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition & Development) Act, 1957 where applicable) read with the State/Company R&R policy. Covers Social Impact Assessment, award of compensation, employment/monetary R&R benefits, and implementation of the R&R plan for displaced families — a precondition to taking physical possession of the land.

title: Milestone 5 – DGMS CTO
detail: DGMS Permission / Consent to Operate (CTO): The safety-regulator clearances from the Directorate General of Mines Safety before opening the mine — statutory Notice of Opening/Commencement (FORM VII), appointment of a qualified Manager, and DGMS approvals/permissions for the required plans and systems (e.g. Safety Management Plan, mine plans, HEMM/electrical installations) under the Mines Act, 1952 and the OSH Rules, 2026. This is the final statutory permission-to-operate gate; regular working may start only once DGMS consent is in place.

title: Commencement plan
detail: Commencement plan: The consolidated pre-commencement roadmap that sequences and tracks all preceding milestones (GR → Mining Plan → FC/EC/Public Hearing → R&R → DGMS CTO) against target dates, showing the critical path and current status of each statutory clearance up to the actual start of mining operations.

title: Pre-commencement report
detail: Pre-commencement report: A monthly progress report submitted during the pre-commencement phase summarising the status of each milestone/clearance, actions completed and pending, bottlenecks and revised target dates — used to monitor readiness of the greenfield project until operations commence.
